children.text: abhūn nṛpo vibudha-sakhaḥ paraṃ-tapaḥ śrutā'nvito daśa-ratha ityudāhṛtaḥ,
children.translated_text: There was a king, friend of the gods, of supreme austerity, endowed with learning, known as <s>Daśaratha</s>,

children.text: guṇair varaṃ bhuvana-hitac-chalena yaṃ sanā-tanaḥ pitaramupāgamat svayam.
children.translated_text: him whom the Eternal One (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), pre-eminent in virtues, himself approached as a father, under the pretext of benefiting the world.

children.text: so'dhyaiṣṭa vedāṃs, tri-daśānayaṣṭa, pit npārīt, samamaṃsta bandhūn,
children.translated_text: He studied the <s>Veda</s>s, worshipped the gods, protected his subjects, esteemed his kinsmen equally,

children.text: vyajeṣṭa ṣaḍ-vargamaraṃsta nītau, sa-mūla-ghātaṃ nyavadhīdarīṃś ca.
children.translated_text: conquered the six (inner) enemies, delighted in <s>nīti</s> (statecraft), and destroyed his foes root and all.

children.text: vasūni toyaṃ ghana-vad vyakārīt, sahā''sanaṃ gotra-bhidā'dhyavātsīt,
children.translated_text: He distributed wealth like a rain-cloud, sat on a throne with the Splitter of Mountains (<s>Indra</s>),
worshipped none other than <s>Tryambaka</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), and eclipsed the fame of all warriors.
Meritorious, attended by hosts of great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, gratifying, most excellent among the dwellers of heaven,

children.text: jajvāla loka-sthitaye sa rājā yathā'dhvare vahnirabhipraṇītaḥ.
children.translated_text: that king blazed forth for the sustenance of the world, like fire solemnly brought forth at a sacrifice.
He, of auspicious fame, equal to <s>Śatamanyu</s> (<s>Indra</s>), his prosperity rivaling the world of <s>Mahendra</s>,
ruled from <s>Ayodhyā</s>, pleasant in all seasons, inhabited by <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s of advanced wisdom.
That (city), the very limit of the creative skill of the Lotus-seated (<s>Brahmā</s>) in his endeavors,
stood as if mocking the city of <s>Maghon</s> (<s>Indra</s>) with its upward-flashing gem-rays.
With precious gems, pearls, fruits, diamonds, variegated mineral ores, and gardens,

children.text: strībhir yutānyapsarasāmivaughair meroḥ śirāṃsīva gṛhāṇi yasyām.
children.translated_text: its houses, accompanied by women like hosts of <s>Apsaras</s>es, were like the peaks of <s>Meru</s>.
Radiances of brilliant gems set within, streaming out through the latticed windows,
shone from the houses in that (city) like cascades of <s>Gaṅgā</s>-water from a ledge of the snowy mountain.
In his three excellent wives — righteous, bringing desire, wealth, and fame,

children.text: vidyāsu vidvāniva so'bhireme patnīṣu rājā tisṛṣūttamāsu.
children.translated_text: well-regarded in the world, acquired at the proper time — that king delighted, like a learned man in the branches of knowledge.

children.text: putrīyatā tena varā'ṅganābhi- rānāyi vidvān kratuṣu kriyāvān
children.translated_text: Desiring sons, by those noble women, he brought the learned, ritual-performing,

children.text: vipaktrima-jñāna-gatir manasvī mānyo muniḥ svāṃ puramṛṣya śṛṅgaḥ
children.translated_text: wise sage <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>, of knowledge gained not through artifice, the venerable one, to his own city.

children.text: aihiṣṭa taṃ kārayituṃ kṛtā''tmā kratuṃ nṛpaḥ putra-phalaṃ munīndram,
children.translated_text: The self-disciplined king wished to have that lord of sages perform

children.text: jñānā''śayas tasya tato vyatānīt sa karmaṭhaḥ karma sutā'nubandham.
children.translated_text: the sacrifice yielding the fruit of sons; thereafter that diligent one arranged the ritual whose sequel was offspring.

children.text: rakṣāṃsi vedīṃ parito nirāstha- daṅgānyayākṣīdbhitaḥ pradhānam,
children.translated_text: He warded off the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s from around the sacrificial altar, sprinkled the principal limbs (of the sacrifice),

children.text: śeṣāṇyahauṣīt suta-saṃpade ca, varaṃ vareṇyo nṛpateramārgīt.
children.translated_text: offered the remaining oblations for the attainment of sons, and the most excellent one requested a boon from the king.

children.text: niṣṭāṃ gate daktrima-sabhaya-toṣe vihitrime karmaṇi rāja-patnyaḥ
children.translated_text: When the sacrifice, performed with due and joyous solemnity, reached its conclusion, the queens of the king

children.text: prāśur hutocchiṣṭamudāra-vaṃśyās tisraḥ prasotuṃ caturaḥ su-putrān.
children.translated_text: partook of the sacrificial remnants — those three of noble lineage — to give birth to four excellent sons.

children.text: kausalyayā'sāvi sukhena rāmaḥ prāk, kekayī-to bharatas tato'bhūt,
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> was born happily first to <s>Kausalyā</s>; from <s>Kekayī</s>, <s>Bharata</s> was then born;

children.text: prāsoṣṭa śatru-ghnamudāra-ceṣṭa- mekā sumitrā saha lakṣmaṇena.
children.translated_text: <s>Sumitrā</s> alone gave birth to <s>Śatrughna</s> of noble deeds, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: ārcīd dvi-jātīn paramā'rtha-vindā- nudejayān bhūta-gaṇān nyaṣedhīt,
children.translated_text: He honored the twice-born, gave generous gifts, drove away the hosts of evil spirits,

children.text: vidvānupāneṣṭa ca tān sva-kāle yatir vaśiṣṭo yamināṃ variṣṭhaḥ.
children.translated_text: and the learned, self-controlled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, foremost of the restrained, initiated them at the proper time.
They mastered the entire <s>Veda</s> with its limbs, and learned weapons that conquer,

children.text: te bhinna-vṛttīnyapi mānasāni samaṃ janānāṃ guṇino'dhyavātsuḥ,
children.translated_text: and though differing in temperament, those virtuous ones equally won the hearts of people.
Then the son of <s>Gādhi</s> (<s>Viśvāmitra</s>), whose ritual activities were obstructed by <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, came to the lord of the earth

children.text: rāmaṃ varītuṃ parirakṣaṇā-rthaṃ, rājā''jihat taṃ madhuparka-pāṇiḥ.
children.translated_text: to request <s>Rāma</s> for protection; the king received him with the <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-offering) in hand.

children.text: aiṣīḥ punar-janma-jayāya yat tvaṃ, rūpā''di-bodhān nyavṛtac ca yat te,
children.translated_text: 'That you have striven for the conquest of rebirth, and that you have turned away from perceptions of form and the like,

children.text: tattvānyabuddhāḥ pratinūni yena, dhyānaṃ nṛpas tacchivamityavādīt.
children.translated_text: and that you have understood the subtle principles through which — that <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is auspicious,' the king said.

children.text: ākhyan munis tasya śivaṃ samādher, vighnanti rakṣāṃsi vane kratūṃśca,
children.translated_text: The sage told him that <s>Rākṣasa</s>s were obstructing the auspicious meditation and the forest sacrifices:

children.text: tāni dviṣad-vīrya-nirākariṣṇus tṛṇeḍhu rāmaḥ saha lakṣmaṇena.
children.translated_text: 'Let <s>Rāma</s>, with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, who can negate the power of enemies, treat them as mere grass.'
He heard those words; the king, unable to bear separation from his son, was bewildered;

children.text: ahaṃyunā'tha kṣiti-paḥ śubhaṃyu- rūce vacas tāpasa-kuñjareṇa.
children.translated_text: then the lord of the earth, seeking auspiciousness, was addressed by the elephant among ascetics.

children.text: mayā tvamāpthāḥ śaraṇaṃ bhayeṣu, vayaṃ tvayā'pyāpsmahi dharma-vṛddhyai,
children.translated_text: 'You have been obtained by me as refuge in times of fear; we too shall be obtained by you for the increase of <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: kṣatraṃ dvija-tvaṃ ca parasparā'rthaṃ, śaṅkāṃ kṛthā mā, prahiṇu-sva-sūnum.
children.translated_text: the <s>Kṣatriya</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> classes exist for each other's benefit — have no doubt, send your son.'

children.text: ghāniṣyate tena mahān vipakṣaḥ, sthāyiṣyate yena raṇe purastāt,
children.translated_text: 'The great adversary will be slain by him, who will stand foremost in battle;

children.text: mā māṃ mahā''tman paribhūr-yogye na mad-vidho nyasyati bhāramagryam.
children.translated_text: do not disregard me, O great soul — one like me does not place a supreme burden on an unworthy one.'

children.text: krudhyan kulaṃ dhakṣyati vipra-vahnir, yāsyan sutas tapsyati māṃ sa-manyum,
children.translated_text: 'Angered, the fire of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> will burn (your) lineage; if the son departs (unfulfilled), he will reproach me with anger.'

children.text: itthaṃ nṛpaḥ pūrvamavāluloce, tato'nujajñe gamanaṃ sutasya.
children.translated_text: Thus the king first deliberated, then gave permission for his son's departure.

children.text: āśīrbhirabhyarcya muniḥ kṣitīndraṃ prītaḥ pratasthe punarāśramāya,
children.translated_text: Honoring the lord of the earth with blessings, the sage departed gladly for his hermitage again;

children.text: taṃ pṛṣṭha-taḥ praṣṭhamiyāya namro hiṃsreṣu-dīptā''pta-dhanuḥ kumāraḥ.
children.translated_text: behind him followed the prince, humble, with bow ready for the fierce ones, blazing with splendor.

children.text: prayāsyataḥ puṇya-vanāya jiṣṇo- rāmasya rociṣṇu-mukhasya ghṛṣṇuḥ
children.translated_text: Of the victorious <s>Rāma</s>, departing for the sacred forest, with radiant face, the bold one,

children.text: trai-māturaḥ kṛtsna-jitā'stra-śastraḥ sadhryaṅ rataḥ śreyasi lakṣmaṇo'bhūt.
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> became the companion — born of three mothers, having fully mastered all weapons and arms, devoted equally to the good.

children.text: iṣu-mati raghu-siṃhe dandaśūkāñ jighāṃsau dhanuraribhira-sahyaṃ muṣṭi-pīḍaṃ dadhāne
children.translated_text: As the lion of the <s>Raghu</s> dynasty, skilled with arrows, wishing to slay the serpents (demons), took up the bow unbearable to foes, grasped tightly in his fist,

children.text: vrajati, pura-taruṇyo baddha-citrā'ṅgulitre kathamapi guru-śokān mā rudan māṅgalikyaḥ
children.translated_text: and departed — the young women of the city, with fingers fixed on their painted (eyes), could barely hold back their tears of great sorrow, O auspicious ones!

children.text: atha jagaduranīcai-rāśiṣas tasya viprās, tumula-kala-ninādaṃ tūryamājaghnuranye,
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s uttered blessings upon him aloud throughout the world; others struck the drum with tumultuous melodious sound;

children.text: abhimata-phala-śaṃsī cāru pusphora bāhus, taruṣu cukuvuruccaiḥ pakṣiṇaś cā'nukūlāḥ.
children.translated_text: his arm, foretelling the desired fruit, beautifully throbbed; and favorable birds sang aloud in the trees.

children.text: vanaspatīnāṃ sarasāṃ nadīnāṃ tejasvināṃ kāntibhṛtāṃ diśāṃ ca
children.translated_text: Departing from that city of trees, lakes, rivers, luminaries, beauties, and regions,

children.text: niryāya tasyāḥ sa puraḥ samantā cchriyaṃ dadhānāṃ śaradaṃ dadarśa.
children.translated_text: he saw all around the autumn, resplendent, bearing beauty.

children.text: taraṅga-saṅgāc capalaiḥ palāśair jvālā-śriyaṃ sā'tiśayāṃ dadhanti
children.translated_text: Bearing an extraordinary splendor of flames through their restless leaves intermingled with waves,
the red lotuses, swarming with bees, shone with a radiance like that of smoky blazing fire.

children.text: bimbā''gatais tīra-vanaiḥ samṛddhiṃ nijāṃ vilokyā'pahṛtāṃ payobhiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing their own beauty carried away by the waters through the reflections of the trees on the banks,
the riverbanks, as if in indignation, displayed the beauty of lotuses through the smiles of land-lotuses.
With clear drops dripping from the tips of leaves like night-dew resembling tears,
a tree on the bank, with humming bees, seemed to weep over the lotus-pond at the start of day.

children.text: vanāni toyāni ca netra-kalpaiḥ puṣpaiḥ sarojaiś ca nilīna-bhṛṅgaiḥ
children.translated_text: The forests and waters, with flowers and lotuses in which bees had settled, like eyes,
seemed to gaze at each other's beauty with wonder and with regard.
The lotus-pond, its form trembling from the blows of the morning breeze, with body yellowish from the pollen of night-lotuses,

children.text: nirāsa bhṛṅgaṃ kupiteva padminī, na māninī saṃsahate 'nya-saṅgamam.
children.translated_text: cast out the bee, as if a proud lotus-lady would not tolerate contact with another.
Attentive to the song of the honey-bees, wishing to kill the deer standing motionless,

children.text: ākarṇayannutsuka-haṃsa-nādān lakṣye samādhiṃ na dadhe mṛgāvit.
children.translated_text: hearing the eager cries of the swans, the hunter could not fix his concentration on the target.

children.text: girer nitambe marutā vibhinnaṃ toyā'vaśeṣeṇa himā''bhamabhram
children.translated_text: On the slope of the mountain, a cloud, broken by the wind, white as snow, with only a little water remaining,
accumulating at the mouths of streams, imitated the beauty of the lord of mountains.

children.text: garjan hariḥ sā'mbhasi śaila-kuñje pratidhvanīnātma-kṛtān niśamya
children.translated_text: A lion, roaring at a pool in a mountain grove, hearing echoes of his own making,
checked his step, angrily intending to advance, thinking them the roars of another king of beasts.
He (Rāma) gazed at the fresh blue lotuses in the waters, and heard the sounds of the bees,

children.text: āghrāyi vān gandha-vahaḥ su-gandhas tenā'ravinda-vyatiṣaṅga-vāṃś ca.
children.translated_text: and the fragrance-bearing wind, beautifully scented, was also smelled by him, bringing the touch of lotuses.
He gathered flowers as creepers swayed, and touched the holy waters at the river-crossing,

children.text: kutūhalāc, cāru-śilopaveśaṃ kākutstha īṣat smayamāna āsta.
children.translated_text: out of curiosity, and the descendant of <s>Kakutstha</s>, slightly smiling, sat upon a beautiful rock-seat.
In the morning, he saw the far-off waters, churned by the sharp rays of the sun,

children.text: gabhasti-dhārābhiriva drutāni tejāṃsi bhānor bhuvi saṃbhṛtāni.
children.translated_text: as if streams of radiance, flowing rapidly, were the splendors of the sun gathered on the earth.
Pervading the directions, delightful to the eyes, as if flowing with affection, in orderly rows,
he was pleased seeing the rows of excellent crops, straight and extended, with clear intervals between the grasses.
By men who knew not the experience of the sorrow of separation, who paid the king's share at the proper time,

children.text: āhārya-śobhā-rahitairamāyai- raikṣiṣṭa pumbhiḥ pracitān sa goṣṭhān
children.translated_text: who were without artificial adornment, guileless — he beheld the well-tended cattle-stations.
The ornament of women — their unaffected gestures, their glances beautiful though shy,

children.text: ṛjūṃśca viśvāsa-kṛtaḥ svabhāvān gopā'ṅganānāṃ mumude vilokya.
children.translated_text: and the straightforward, trusting natures of the cowherd-women — he delighted in beholding.
With turning sides, with lovely movements of the body, with uplifted beautiful buttocks, charming,
the dance of the cowherd-women, with rhythm given by the soft sound of churning, delighted him.

children.text: vicitramuccaiḥ plavamānamārāt kutūhalaṃ trasnu tatāna tasya
children.translated_text: Leaping high in variegated patterns from nearby, curiosity and alarm spread in him
at the herds of deer raised by the wind, born from the rain-season's forest splendor, in <s>Kadamba</s>-groves.

children.text: sitā'ravinda-pracayeṣu ca līnāḥ saṃsakta-peṇeṣu ca saikateṣu
children.translated_text: Settled among clusters of white lotuses and on sandy banks covered with foam,
rows of white geese, white as <s>Kunda</s> flowers, were perceived through their sounds pleasing to the ear.

children.text: na taj jalaṃ, yan na su-cāru-paṅkajaṃ, na paṅkajaṃ tad, yada-līna-ṣaṭ-padam,
children.translated_text: There was no water without beautiful lotuses, no lotus without a bee settled upon it,

children.text: na ṣaṭ-pado'sau, na juguñja yaḥ kalaṃ; na guñjitaṃ tan, na jahāra yan manaḥ.
children.translated_text: no bee that did not hum sweetly, no humming that did not captivate the mind.

children.text: taṃ yāyajūkāḥ saha bhikṣu-mukhyais tapaḥ-kṛśāḥ śāntyudakumbha-hastāḥ,
children.translated_text: Sacrificers, together with chief monks, emaciated by austerities, with peace-water pots in hand,
wandering ascetics, and others with flowers and fruits, worshipped him — the world-venerable one, worthy of worship.

children.text: vidyāmathainaṃ vijayāṃ jayāṃ ca rakṣo-gaṇaṃ kṣipnuma-vikṣatā''tmā
children.translated_text: 'Let us teach him the <s>vidyā</s>s (sciences) — <s>Vijayā</s> and <s>Jayā</s> — and swiftly destroy the host of <s>Rākṣasa</s>s,' —

children.text: adhyāpipad gādhi-suto yathāvan nighātayiṣyan yudhi yātudhānān.
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Gādhi</s> properly instructed him, intending to slay the night-rangers in battle.
Standing firm in battle, born of weapons, unfailing, for the approaching great combat,

children.text: dadau vadhāya kṣaṇadācarāṇāṃ tasmai muniḥ śreyasi jāgarūkaḥ
children.translated_text: the sage, vigilant for the good, gave (the weapons) to him for the destruction of the night-wanderers.

children.text: taṃ vipra-darśaṃ kṛta-ghāta-yatnā yāntaṃ vane rātricarī ḍuḍhauke,
children.translated_text: That female night-wanderer (<s>Tāḍakā</s>), having made efforts to kill, pursued him as he went into the forest for the sage's purpose;

children.text: jighāṃsu-vedaṃ dhṛta-bhāsurā'stram tāṃ tāḍakā''khyāṃ nijaghāna rāmaḥ.
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, wishing to slay her, holding a shining weapon, killed that one called <s>Tāḍakā</s>.
Then he beheld the hermitage-grove with branches smooth and dark as collyrium, like the crests of sacrificial fire-smoke,
resounding with the sweet jingling of birds, overwhelmed by sacred recitation.

children.text: kṣudrān na jakṣur hariṇān mṛgendrā, viśaśvase pakṣi-gaṇaiḥ samantāt,
children.translated_text: Lions did not devour the small deer; birds from all around were trustful;

children.text: nannamyamānāḥ phala-ditsayeva cakāśire tatra latā vilolāḥ.
children.translated_text: creepers, bending as if wishing to offer their fruits, gleamed there, swaying.
The chief forest-dwellers, skilled in hospitality, honored (them) with mats, water for the feet, and garlands;
the two princes accepted seats and the rest, together with the <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-offering).

children.text: daityā'bhibhūtasya yuvāmavoḍhaṃ magnasya dorbhir bhuvanasya bhāram,
children.translated_text: 'You two shall bear the burden of the world, which has been overwhelmed by <s>Daitya</s>s (demons) and is sinking —
protect even now the sacrificial offerings!' — thus they were addressed by the ascetics.

children.text: tān pratyavādīdatha rāghvo'pi--, yathepsitaṃ prastuta karma dharmyam,
children.translated_text: Then the scion of <s>Raghu</s> also replied: 'Let the desired, righteous, appointed ritual proceed;
let the fire of our arrows be kindled by the wind of your austerities upon the fuel of our enemies.'

children.text: pratuṣṭuvuḥ karma tataḥ prakwxlqqptais te yajñiyair dravya-gaṇair yathāvat,
children.translated_text: Then they commenced the rite with properly prepared sacrificial materials as prescribed;

children.text: dakṣiṇya-diṣṭaṃ kṛtamārtvijīnais tad yātudhānaiś cicite prasarpat.
children.translated_text: the performance, directed with expertise by the officiating priests, was disrupted by the night-rangers as it progressed.
With hair tawny, rough, and standing upright, with veiny shanks, tall as mountain peaks,

children.text: tataḥ kṣapā'ṭaiḥ pṛthu-piṅgalā'kṣaiḥ khaṃ prāvṛṣeṇyairiva cā''naśe'bdaiḥ.
children.translated_text: then by those night-wanderers with broad tawny eyes, the sky was darkened as if by rainy-season clouds.
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, with bow strung, fist firm on the arm, with eyes raised and right thigh advanced,
with left shank bent, a sure archer drawing slowly, slew them.
<s>Rāma</s> too, skilled with weapons, with smiling face, destroying the one fiercely fighting with illusions, directed by the son of <s>Gādhi</s>,

children.text: sthāsnuṃ raṇe smera-mukho jagāda mārīcamuccair vacanaṃ mahā'rtham.
children.translated_text: uttered a mighty word to <s>Mārīca</s>, standing firm in battle.

children.text: ātmaṃbharis tvaṃpiśitair narāṇāṃ phalegrahīn haṃsi vanaspatīnām,
children.translated_text: 'Self-dependent, you feast on the flesh of men, you destroy the fruit-bearing forest trees;

children.text: śauvastikatvaṃ vibhavā na yeṣāṃ vrajanti, teṣāṃ dayase na kasmāt.
children.translated_text: those whose possessions do not lead to the well-being (of others) — why do you not have compassion for them?

children.text: admo dvijān, devayajīn nihanmaḥ, kurmaḥ puraṃ preta-narā'dhivāsam,
children.translated_text: 'We devour the twice-born, we slay those who sacrifice to the gods, we make the city a dwelling of ghosts and men,

children.text: dharmo hyayaṃ dāśarathe ! nijo no, naivā'dhyakāriṣmahi veda-vṛtte.
children.translated_text: for this, O son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, is our own <s>dharma</s>! We have never transgressed the Vedic ordinance.'

children.text: dharmo'sti satyaṃ tava rākṣasā'ya- manyo vyatiste tu mamā'pi dharmaḥ,
children.translated_text: "<s>Dharma</s> and truth are yours, O <s>Rākṣasa</s> — but another <s>dharma</s> also belongs to me,

children.text: brahma-dviṣas te praṇihanmi yena, rājanya-vṛttir dhṛta-kārmukeṣuḥ.
children.translated_text: By which I slay these <s>Brahman</s>-haters, being a <s>kṣatriya</s> in conduct, bow in hand and arrow ready."
With such speeches and fierce combat in battle, <s>Rāma</s> and the night-wanderer strove against each other,

children.text: tṛṇāya matvā raghu-nandano 'tha bāṇena rakṣaḥ pradhanān nirāsthat.
children.translated_text: Then the scion of <s>Raghu</s>, considering the <s>rākṣasa</s> as mere straw, drove him from the foremost of the battle with an arrow.

children.text: jagmuḥ prasādaṃ dvija-mānasāni, dyaur varṣukā puṣpa-cayaṃ babhūva,
children.translated_text: The minds of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s became serene, the sky rained down a shower of flowers,

children.text: nir-vyājamijyā vavṛte. vacaś ca bhūyo babhāṣe muninā kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: The sacrifice proceeded without obstruction. And the prince was again addressed by the sage:
"Being honored exceedingly by you, who conquered the gluttonous and swift demons at the sacrifice,

children.text: divo'pi vajrā''yudha-bhūṣaṇāyā hriṇīyate vīra-vatī na bhūmiḥ.
children.translated_text: This earth, possessed of heroes, is not ashamed even before heaven, which has the thunderbolt-wielder as its ornament."

children.text: balir babandhe, jaladhir mamanthe, jahre'mṛtaṃ, daitya-kulaṃ vijigyo,
children.translated_text: "<s>Bali</s> was bound, the ocean was churned, <s>amṛta</s> (nectar of immortality) was seized, the <s>Daitya</s> clan was conquered,

children.text: kalpā'nta-duḥsthā vasudhā tathohe yenaiṣa bhāro'ti-gurur na tasya.
children.translated_text: And the earth, distressed at the end of a <s>kalpa</s>, was thus upheld — this burden is not too heavy for him."

children.text: iti bruvāṇo madhuraṃ hitaṃ ca tamāñjihan maithila-yajña-bhūmim
children.translated_text: Speaking thus sweetly and beneficially, the sage left that sacrificial ground of <s>Mithilā</s>,

children.text: rāmaṃ muniḥ prīta-manā makhā'nte yaśāṃsi rājñāṃ nijighṛkṣayiṣyan.
children.translated_text: Pleased in mind, at the end of the sacrifice, intending to cause the glories of kings to increase for <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: etau sma mitrā-varuṇau kimetau, kimaśvinau soma-rasaṃ pipāsū,
children.translated_text: "Are these two <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>? Are these the <s>Aśvin</s>s, thirsting for <s>Soma</s>-juice?"

children.text: janaṃ samastaṃ janakā''śrama-sthaṃ rūpeṇa tāvaujihatāṃ nṛ-siṃhau.
children.translated_text: Thus all the people dwelling in the hermitage of <s>Janaka</s> were struck with wonder by the beauty of those two lions among men.

children.text: ajigrahat taṃ janako dhanus tad "yenā'rdidad daitya-puraṃ pinākī",
children.translated_text: <s>Janaka</s> grasped that bow — "with which <s>Pinākī</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) had split the <s>Daitya</s> city" —

children.text: jijñāsamāno balamasya bāhvor. hasannabhāṅkṣvīd raghu-nandanas tat.
children.translated_text: Wishing to test the strength of his arms. The scion of <s>Raghu</s>, laughing, broke it.

children.text: tato nadī-ṣṇān pathikān giri-jñā- nāhvāyakān bhūmi-paterayodhyām
children.translated_text: Then the chief of <s>Mithilā</s>'s mortals, wishing to give his daughter, dispatched

children.text: ditsuḥ sutāṃ yodha-harais turaṅgair vyasarjayan maithila-martya-mukhyaḥ.
children.translated_text: River-crossers, wayfarers, mountain-experts, and heralds to <s>Ayodhyā</s> of the lord of the earth, with swift battle-seizing horses.
Quickly then, the king, though extremely old, traveling swiftly by horse like a youngest youth,
Having heard of his son's exploits from the messengers, came to <s>Mithilā</s> with unwearied march.

children.text: vṛndiṣṭhamārcīd vasudhā-dhipānāṃ taṃ preṣṭhametaṃ guru-vad gariṣṭham
children.translated_text: The most venerable of earth's lords honored him, the most dear, the most weighty like a teacher,
Equal in greatness, an abode of good deeds, of most expansive fame, and foremost in glory.
Having seated him, who had mastered the three aims of life, on a single throne, <s>Indra</s>

children.text: viveka-dṛśva-tvamagāt surāṇāṃ, taṃ maithilo vākyamidaṃ babhāṣe.
children.translated_text: Attained the state of discernment of the gods; and the king of <s>Mithilā</s> spoke these words.

children.text: hiraṇmayī sāla-lateva jaṅgamā cyutā divaḥ sthāsnurivā'cira-prabhā
children.translated_text: Like a golden creeping vine in motion, like a flash of lightning that has descended from heaven and become permanent,

children.text: śaśāṅkaṃ-kānteradhidevatā''kṛtiḥ sutā dade tasya sutāya maithilī.
children.translated_text: Like the presiding deity of moonstone in form, the daughter of <s>Mithilā</s> was given to his son.
Then <s>Rāma</s>, whose conduct was universally admired, accepted that woman who was his very own,
Who enhanced the glory of the <s>Raghu</s> dynasty, shining with the burden of fine jewels and pearls.
That army, whose joy had been aroused in the beautiful morning, praised by worshippers, headed for <s>Ayodhyā</s>,
Rich with horses, nobles, and elephants, accompanied by the king — the traveling host.
Broad-chested, arrow in hand, with two palm-trees as his height, ahead of them

children.text: bhīṣmo dhanuṣmānupajānvaratni- raiti sma rāmaḥ pathi jāmadagnyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Fearsome, bow in hand, arm reaching to the knee, <s>Rāma Jāmadagnya</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) came along the path.

children.text: uccairasau rāghavamāhvatedaṃ dhanuḥ sa-bāṇaṃ kuru, sā'tiyāsīḥ.
children.translated_text: He loudly challenged <s>Rāghava</s>: "String this bow with arrow — you have gone too far!"
The lord of the earth, knowing his valor, wishing to conciliate him, spoke humbly regarding his dear offspring:

children.text: aneka-śo nirjita-rājakas tvaṃ, pit natārpsīr nṛpa-rakta-toyaiḥ,
children.translated_text: "You who have conquered kings many times, you satisfied your ancestors with the blood-waters of kings,
Having withdrawn your fury against an unworthy foe — what grounds have you, O <s>Rāma</s>, against this child <s>Rāma</s>?"

children.text: ajīgaṇad daśarathaṃ na vākyaṃ yadā sa darpeṇa, tadā kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: When he proudly disregarded the words of <s>Daśaratha</s>, then the prince

children.text: dhanur vyakārkṣīd guru-bāṇa-garbhaṃ, lokānalāvīd vijitāṃśca tasya.
children.translated_text: Drew the heavy bow loaded with an arrow, and took away his conquered worlds.
When the enemy of the king was defeated, the armies with their flowers became cheerful,
Resounding gradually without fear, and with the permission of the aged king, they entered the many-mouthed roads.

children.text: atha puru-java-yogān nedayad dūra-saṃsthaṃ davayadati-rayeṇa prāptamurvī-vibhāgam
children.translated_text: Then, making the distant-stationed army resound with the force of great speed, spreading the earth with excessive velocity,
Without fatigue, unconsciously making the earth free of dust, the army, adorned with beauty, quickly arrived at <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
Through the slaughter of the flesh-eating ones in battle, and through the subjugation of the destroyer of <s>kṣatriya</s>s,

children.text: āḍhyaṃbhaviṣṇur yaśasā kumāraḥ priyaṃbhaviṣṇur na sa yasya nā''sīt.
children.translated_text: The prince, destined to become rich in glory, destined to become dear — there was none for whom he was not so.
Then the lord of the earth, having gladdened his citizens and servants, making it known to the entire people softly that "I shall consecrate my son in the kingdom,"

children.text: āghoṣayan bhūmi-patiḥ samastaṃ bhūyo'pi lokaṃ sumanīcakāra.
children.translated_text: Pleased the populace even more.
He pointed out the throne with footstool, blazing like a kindled fire,
Beautiful with heated gold and <s>vajra</s> (diamonds), with precious gems arranged in compartments.

children.text: prāsthāpayat pūga-kṛtān sva-poṣaṃ pṛṣṭān prayatnād dṛḍha-gātra-bandhān
children.translated_text: He dispatched men in groups, well-nourished, asked with care, firm in their bodily bonds,
Bearing water-pots on their shoulders, swift, in all directions for the water from holy places.

children.text: ukṣān pracakrur nagarasya mārgān, dhvajān babandhur, mumucuḥ kha-dhūpān,
children.translated_text: They sprinkled the streets of the city, they bound banners, they released aerial incense,

children.text: diśaśca puṣpaiścakarur vicitrai- rartheṣu rājñā nipuṇā niyuktāḥ
children.translated_text: And decorated the directions with various flowers — skilled men appointed by the king for these tasks.
Having gone to his maternal grandfather's residence, not having asked <s>Bharata</s> at that time out of delusion,

children.text: tat kekayī soḍhuma-śaknuvānā vavāra rāmasya vana-prayāṇam.
children.translated_text: That <s>Kaikeyī</s>, unable to bear it, demanded the forest-exile of <s>Rāma</s>.
Her greed for the kingdom planted by whispers in her ear, led astray by feminine fickleness,

children.text: rāma-pravāse vyamṛśan na doṣaṃ janā'pavādaṃ sa-narendra-mṛtyum
children.translated_text: In <s>Rāma</s>'s exile she did not consider the fault — the public censure together with the king's death.

children.text: vasūni deśāṃśca nivartayiṣyan rāmaṃ nṛpaḥ saṃgiramāṇa eva
children.translated_text: As the king, wishing to bestow on <s>Rāma</s> wealth and territories, was still speaking,
He was defeated by her; the consecration of <s>Bharata</s> [was demanded], and the stake of despair was driven into his mind.
Then the king, wishing to send the prince into exile, ordered his departure to the forest,
Accompanied by <s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>) and <s>Sītā</s>, grieving, with <s>Sumantra</s> as charioteer.

children.text: kecin ninindur nṛpama-praśāntaṃ, vicukruśuḥ kecana sā'sramuccaiḥ,
children.translated_text: Some reproached the restless king, some cried aloud with tears,

children.text: ūcus tathā 'nye bharatasya māyāṃ, dhik kekayīmityaparo jagāda.
children.translated_text: Others likewise spoke of <s>Bharata</s>'s deceit, and another said: "Shame on <s>Kaikeyī</s>!"

children.text: "gato vanaṃ śvo bhaviteti rāmaḥ," śokena dehe janatā 'timātram,
children.translated_text: "<s>Rāma</s> has gone to the forest and will be there tomorrow" — the people, with excessive grief in their bodies,

children.text: dhīrās tu tatra cyuta-manyavo 'nye dadhuḥ kumārā'nugame manāṃsi.
children.translated_text: But the steadfast ones, whose anger had subsided, set their minds on following the prince.
Those two, about to depart, having approached the lamenting ones, said this to them:
"Why do you grieve here for us in our good fortune, alas — us who have been made fulfilled by obtaining our father's command?

children.text: asṛṣṭa yo, yaśca bhayeṣvarakṣīd, yaḥ sarvadā 'smānapuṣat sva-poṣam,
children.translated_text: He who created us, who protected us in dangers, who always nourished us with his own nourishment —

children.text: mahopakārasya kimasti tasya tucchena yānena vanasya mokṣaḥ,
children.translated_text: For such a great benefactor, is this not a trifling repayment — liberation through a journey to the forest?

children.text: vidyut-praṇāśaṃ sa varaṃ pranaṣṭo, yadvordhva-śoṣaṃ tṛṇa-vad viśuṣkaḥ,
children.translated_text: Better that one perishes like the vanishing of lightning, than that one withers upward like grass;

children.text: arthe durāpe kimuta pravāse na śāsane 'vāsthita yo gurūṇām.
children.translated_text: What to say of exile, when the goal is hard to reach — one who does not stand by the command of elders.
Citizens! Turn back!" he enjoined. "Be the removers of father's grief,

children.text: mā darśatā'nyaṃ bharataṃ ca matto," nivartayetyāha rathaṃ sma sūtam
children.translated_text: And see no one else but <s>Bharata</s> as different from me." And he told the charioteer to turn back the chariot.

children.text: jñātveṅgitair gatvaratāṃ janānā- mekāṃ śayitvā rajanīṃ sa-pauraḥ
children.translated_text: Having perceived by gestures the people's desire not to go, having slept one night with the citizens,

children.text: rakṣan vane-vāsa-kṛtād bhayāt tān prātaś chalenā 'pajagāma rāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Protecting them from fear born of forest-dwelling, <s>Rāma</s> departed at dawn by a stratagem.

children.text: asrākṣurasraṃ karuṇaṃ ruvanto, muhurmuhur nyaśvasiṣuḥ kapoṣṇam,
children.translated_text: They shed tears, cried pitifully, sighed warm sighs again and again,

children.text: hā rāma ! hā kaṣṭamiti brunvataḥ parāṅ-mukhais te nyavṛtan manobhiḥ
children.translated_text: Saying "Alas, <s>Rāma</s>! Alas, how terrible!" — they turned back with averted minds.
The charioteer too, having purified himself with the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, together with his horses and himself, with no small anger,
Devoted to <s>Rāghava</s> and <s>Sītā</s>, sighing hot sighs, entered the city.

children.text: pratīya sā pūr dadṛśe janena dyaur bhānu-śītāṃśu-vinākṛteva
children.translated_text: Having come back, that city was seen by the people as if the sky had been deprived of the sun and moon,
Though endowed with the stars of the <s>kṣatriya</s>s, all its activities destroyed by the darkness of grief.

children.text: vilokya rāmeṇa vinā sumantra- macyoṣṭa satvān nṛ-patiś cyutā''śaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Sumantra</s> without <s>Rāma</s>, the king lost his spirit and fell, his hopes shattered;

children.text: madhūni naiṣīd vyalipan na gandhair, mano-rame na vyavasiṣṭa vastre.
children.translated_text: He did not take honey, did not anoint himself with perfumes, did not dress in pleasing garments.

children.text: āsiṣṭa naikatra śucā, vyaraṃsīt kṛtā'kṛtebhyaḥ kṣiti-pāla-bhāg-bhyaḥ,
children.translated_text: He did not sit in any one place with grief; he became estranged from all his royal duties, done and undone;
Anointed with sandalwood, <s>uśīra</s>, and lotus stalks, he went to heavenly abode, consumed by the fire of grief.

children.text: vicukruśur bhūmi-pater mahiṣyaḥ, keśāṃl luluñcuḥ, sva-vapūṃṣi jaghnuḥ,
children.translated_text: The chief queens of the king cried out, tore their hair, struck their own bodies,

children.text: vibhūṣaṇānyunmumucuḥ, kṣamāyā petur, babhañjur valayāni caiva.
children.translated_text: Removed their ornaments, fell to the ground of patience, and broke their bangles as well.

children.text: tāḥ sāntvayantī bharata-pratīkṣā taṃ bandhu-tā nyakṣipadāśu taile,
children.translated_text: She who was consoling them, waiting for <s>Bharata</s>, quickly placed that one in oil through family bond;
And they dispatched messengers by the counsel of ministers, desiring to bring the young prince.

children.text: "supto nabhastaḥ patitaṃ nirīkṣāṃ- cakre vivasvantamadhaḥ sphurantam,"
children.translated_text: "I slept, and looking, saw from the sky the shining sun falling and flickering below,"

children.text: ākhyad vasan mātṛ-kule sakhibhyaḥ paśyan pramādaṃ bharato 'pi rājñaḥ.
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s>, dwelling in his maternal family's home, was telling this to his friends, even as he saw the king's calamity.
When the messengers arrived and made him hear that urgent matter, desiring to depart,

children.text: āṃhiṣṭa jātā'ñjihiṣas tadā 'sā- vutkaṇṭhamāno bharato gurūṇām.
children.translated_text: He became distressed, desiring to go quickly, full of longing for his elders, that <s>Bharata</s>.
He feared for his kinsmen, being agitated, having approached them bound by affection in the face of calamity;
And the flocks of jackals and deer did not move properly, and they were terrified of fearsome omens.

children.text: sa proṣivānetya puraṃ pravekṣyan śuśrāva ghoṣaṃ na janaugha-janyam,
children.translated_text: Returning from abroad to enter the city, he heard no sound born of crowds of people,

children.text: ākarṇayāmāsa na veda-nādān, na copalebhe vaṇijāṃ paṇā'yān.
children.translated_text: He did not perceive the chanting of <s>Veda</s>s, nor did he find the trading of merchants.
The mothers, having come near, cried aloud upon meeting the king, approaching with tears;
And the chief priest, ministers, and warriors, with fully increased and overflowing anger.

children.text: didṛkṣamāṇaḥ paritaḥ sa-sītaṃ rāmaṃ yadā naikṣata lakṣmaṇaṃ ca,
children.translated_text: When, looking around, he did not see <s>Rāma</s> together with <s>Sītā</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
Weeping, he then asked; and they told him what had happened in full.
With terribly furrowed brows, with red, fierce eyes that seemed to blaze,

children.text: uccairupālabdha sa kekayīṃ ca, śoke muhuś cāvirataṃ nyamāṅkṣīt.
children.translated_text: He loudly reproached <s>Kaikeyī</s>, and repeatedly and ceaselessly plunged into grief.

children.text: nṛpā''tmajau cikliśatuḥ sa-sītau, mamāra rājā, vi-dhavā bhavatyaḥ,
children.translated_text: "The two princes together with <s>Sītā</s> have suffered, the king has died, you have become widows,

children.text: śocyā vayaṃ, bhūra-nṛpā, laghutvaṃ kekayyupajñaṃ bata bahvanartham.
children.translated_text: We are to be pitied, O multitude of kings — the fickleness devised by <s>Kaikeyī</s>, alas, has brought much calamity!"

children.text: naitan mataṃ matkamiti bruvāṇaḥ sahasra-śo 'sau śapathānaśapyat
children.translated_text: Saying "This is not my intention," he took a thousand oaths,

children.text: udvāśyamānaḥ pitaraṃ sa-rāmaṃ luṭhyan sa-śoko bhuvi rorudā-vān.
children.translated_text: Weeping, bewailing with grief, rolling on the ground, making his father and <s>Rāma</s> his constant address.

children.text: taṃ susthayantaḥ sacivā narendraṃ didhakṣayantaḥ samudūhurārāt
children.translated_text: The ministers, consoling that lord, wishing to cremate the king, brought him near
Together with <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, wishing to make the final oblation, desiring to prepare the sacrificial vessels.
They raised banners of silk and fine cloth, sounded flutes, drums, and cymbals,

children.text: kambūṃś ca tārānadhaman samantāt, tathā''nayan kuṅkuma-candanāni.
children.translated_text: And blew conch-shells and high-pitched sounds all around, and likewise brought saffron and sandalwood.
Having adorned the ears, eyes, nose, and face with gold, having placed him on a skin with head to the east,

children.text: sañcitya pātrāṇi yathā-vidhāna- mṛtvig juhāva jvalitaṃ citā'gnim
children.translated_text: Having gathered the vessels according to the prescribed rites, the <s>ṛtvik</s> (priest) offered oblations into the blazing funeral pyre.
When the offering of rice-balls and water had been made, setting aside the consecration begun by the people,

children.text: pratyāninīṣur vinayena rāmaṃ prāyādaraṇyaṃ bharataḥ sa-pauraḥ.
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s>, with the citizens, went to the forest to bring back <s>Rāma</s> with humility.
By people hastening, covering the horizons, walking on pathless ground, crawling,
Though unadorned due to grief, the earth shone, mixed with great elephants, chariots, and horses.

children.text: uccikyire puṣpa-phalaṃ vanāni, sasnuḥ pit n pipriyurāpagāsu,
children.translated_text: They gathered flowers and fruits of the forests, the ancestors bathed and were pleased in the rivers,
They climbed the riverbanks without fear, and, taking shade, rested as well.
Having reached the bank of the river <s>Tamasā</s>, worthy of purification through contact with the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: vigāhituṃ yāmunamabmu puṇyaṃ yayur niruddha-śramavṛttayas te.
children.translated_text: They went to bathe in the holy waters of the <s>Yamunā</s>, their wearied activities having ceased.

children.text: īyur bharadvāja-muner niketaṃ, yasmin viśaśrāma sametya rāmaḥ
children.translated_text: They went to the dwelling of the sage <s>Bharadvāja</s>, where <s>Rāma</s> had rested upon arrival,
Free from hunger, with the splendor of fruit-bearing abundance, dispelling thirst with cool waters.
Those who controlled their speech, who slept on the bare ground, who always desired <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), who strove for union,

children.text: adhyāpayantaṃ vinayāt praṇemuḥ padgā bharadvāja-muniḥ sa-śiṣyaṃ.
children.translated_text: They bowed with their feet to the sage <s>Bharadvāja</s> together with his disciples, who was teaching with discipline.
For him who wished to offer hospitality to these, wish-fulfilling trees burst forth by the power of <s>yoga</s>,
They bore garments endowed with softness befitting the expanse of his splendor, and possessing great length;

children.text: ājñāṃ pratīṣur, vinayādupāsthur, jaguḥ sarāgaṃ, nanṛtuḥ sa-hāvam,
children.translated_text: They awaited his command, attended upon him with modesty, sang with passion, danced with grace,
Bowed with charm, spoke nobly — <s>Tilottamā</s> and the other celestial women in that place.

children.text: vastrā'nna-pānaṃ śayanaṃ ca nānā kṛtvā'vakāśe ruci-saṃprakwxlqqptam
children.translated_text: Having arranged clothing, food, drink, and various beds in a suitable space, prepared to please,

children.text: tān prīti-mānāha munis tataḥ sma "nivadhvamādhvaṃ, pibatā'tta śedhvam.
children.translated_text: The sage, pleased, then said to them: "Settle down, eat, drink, partake, and rest.

children.text: te bhuktavantaḥ su-sukhaṃ vasitvā vāsāṃsyuṣitvā rajanīṃ prabhāte
children.translated_text: Having eaten well, dwelt most comfortably, worn the garments, and stayed the night, at dawn

children.text: drutaṃ samadhvā ratha-vāji-nāgair mandākinīṃ ramya-vanāṃ samīyuḥ.
children.translated_text: They swiftly set out with chariots, horses, and elephants and reached the <s>Mandākinī</s> with its lovely forests.
Having heard tidings of <s>Rāma</s> from the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> ascetics, then, toward a flock of birds resounding,
They approached the mountain <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, whose peak touched the clouds and obstructed the path of the sun.

children.text: dṛṣṭvorṇuvānān kakubho balaughān vitatya śārṅgaṃ kavacaṃ pinahya
children.translated_text: Seeing the multitudes of armies covering the horizons, stretching his bow <s>Śārṅga</s>, fastening his armor,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, stood ready to fight, with sharpened arrows, raising his brow and eye;
But seeing them wearing white upper garments, unarmed, approaching slowly on foot, their anger subsided,

children.text: auhiṣṭa tān vīta-viruddha-buddhīn vivandiṣūn dāśarathiḥ sva-vargyān
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Daśaratha</s> received those whose hostile intentions had departed, who wished to pay homage — his own kinsmen.
Weeping with their eyes down to the roots, their fury intensified,
They reported loudly that the king had died of grief from separation from <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: ciraṃ ruditvā karuṇaṃ sa-śabdaṃ gotrā'bhidhāyaṃ saritaṃ sametya
children.translated_text: Having wept long, pitifully, with loud cries, invoking the family name, coming together at the river,
In the midst of the water, from <s>Rāghava</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the water offering of two handfuls was given near the waters.

children.text: "araṇya-yāne su-kare pitā mā prāyuṅkta, rājye bata duṣ-kare tvām,
children.translated_text: "In the easy task of forest-dwelling, father employed me; alas, in the difficult task of kingship, he employed you;

children.text: mā gāḥ śucaṃ vīra !, bharaṃ vahā 'mum," ābhāṣi rāmeṇa vacaḥ kanīyān.
children.translated_text: Do not grieve, O hero! Bear this burden" — thus the younger brother was addressed by <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: "kṛtī śrutī vṛddha-mateṣu dhīmāṃs tvaṃ paitṛkaṃ ced vacanaṃ na kuryāḥ,
children.translated_text: "You are accomplished, learned in the counsels of elders, wise — if you would not carry out your father's word,

children.text: vicchidyamāne 'pi kule parasya puṃsaḥ kathaṃ syādiha putra-kāmyā.
children.translated_text: Even when another man's lineage is being cut off, how could there be desire for a son in this world?

children.text: asmākamuktaṃ bahu manyase ced, yadīśiṣe tvaṃ na mayi sthite ca,
children.translated_text: If you respect what has been said by us, if you are capable even when I am not present,

children.text: jihreṣya-tiṣṭhan yadi tāta-vākye, jahīhi śaṅkāṃ, vraja, śādhi pṛthvīm."
children.translated_text: If you would feel shame standing against your father's word — abandon doubt, go, rule the earth."
"How could I, the younger, presume to bear the yoke of kingship meant for the eldest?

children.text: mā māṃ prayukthāḥ kula-kīrti-lope," prāha sma rāmaṃ bharato'pi dharymam.
children.translated_text: Do not employ me in the destruction of the family's glory" — <s>Bharata</s> too spoke to <s>Rāma</s> what was righteous.
"This powerful force of elephants and horses, and these royal jewels,

children.text: rājanyakaṃ caitadahaṃ kṣitīndras tvayi sthite syāmiti śāntamaitat."
children.translated_text: And this royal dignity — I would be a king only while you stand; all this is at peace with you."

children.text: iti nigaditavantaṃ rāghavas taṃ jagāda "vraja bharata ! gṛhītvā pāduke tvaṃ madīye,
children.translated_text: To him who had thus spoken, <s>Rāghava</s> said: "Go, <s>Bharata</s>! Taking my sandals,
Free from all apprehension, honored by the multitudes of people, govern the kingdom of the entire world by our authority."
When <s>Bharata</s> had departed, the wise <s>Rāma</s>, proceeding to the forest of austerities,
Arrived there and, being honored, went to the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.
Wandering through the wilderness with <s>Sītā</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
He was forcibly seized and lifted up by the terrible <s>Rākṣasa</s> who desired to devour him.
That one named <s>Virādha</s>, invincible even by Death, head-downward and feet-upward —

children.text: bhaṅktvā bhujau virādhā''khyaṃ taṃ tau bhuvi nicakhnatuḥ.
children.translated_text: Breaking both his arms, those two buried him in the earth.
The two tigers of the <s>Raghu</s> line then proceeded to the hermitage of <s>Śarabhaṅga</s>,
Which was endowed with the splendor of <s>Brahman</s> and was a refuge for those seeking shelter.
Before <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Śarabhaṅga</s> offered his body as an oblation in the fire,
Having pointed out the nearby dwelling of the sage <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s>,
Saying: "You shall come together here; we have not been in the forest in vain;

children.text: dṛṣṭāḥ stha, svasti vo, yāmaḥ sva-puṇya-vijitāṃ gatim"
children.translated_text: You have been seen; blessings upon you; we depart to the abode won by our own merit."
When he had become one with the fire, in the presence of the sage <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s>,
<s>Rāma</s> dwelt in a leaf-hut, wandering constantly among the hermitages.
Living in the forests suitable for dwelling, sleeping on beds of leaves,
Rising from his bed, hunting deer, and showing hospitality, he moved about.
Honoring those who studied the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> <s>Vedas</s>,
He ate after making offerings to the gods — roasted meat of the finest kind, being possessed of splendor.
Wearing garments of bark that covered his entire body, like woven cloth,
The archer, bearing sword and bow <s>Śārṅga</s>, wearing armor, protected the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>;
Having abandoned those forests whose fruits had been eaten, where existence through eating had been sustained,
In those forests, that enemy of serpents roamed fearlessly, free from clouds.
With weapons blazing against outcast beasts, honoring those who pressed <s>Soma</s>,
He wandered among the hermitages of the neighboring assemblies of great <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.
Thinking about the morrow, today, yesterday, and the day after,
About the growth and decline of the great sages, he attained a state of benevolent affection.
Standing firm, muttering prayers at twilight, restraining the moving cattle at the approach of evening,
Awakened at dawn before the stars by the birds, he bowed to the sun.
Then he saw in the leaf-hut a <s>Rākṣasī</s> (demoness) of fearsome appearance;
Disdaining his marriage, she stood before <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> eagerly.
Having a waist with folds like wrinkles, with eyes at the hollows of her ears,
With excessively loose bark-garments, like a crescent moon at the end of a fortnight,
With beautiful feet, thighs like an elephant's trunk, with soft palms and fingers,
With massive, dense hips that bore great breadth,
Bearing a face with an upturned nose, with pure, dangling earrings,
Making a show before his gaze, garlanded, with a beautifully smiling face,
Having arrived and flirting, approaching the best of the <s>Raghu</s>s swiftly,
The sweet-spoken one, following him, began to entreat him to make her his beloved.
"O son of <s>Sumitrā</s>! Take me — desirable, willing, obedient!
Free from fear, live a human lifetime with me as your companion and lover."
He said to her: "In the forest, frightful to both women and men, without social gatherings,
You, whose beauty is not to be seen by the sun — why do you, fearless one, cry out?
You who desire humans, yet are radiant, of divine nature —
You who behave like an <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymph) here — how do you move about independently?
With fierce gaze, agitated in the forest, devoid of modesty,
Skilled in the solicitations of lovers — are you or are you not a married woman?
Go to <s>Rāghava</s> in the leaf-hut, desiring a husband in private,
Who is my lord, possessed of beloved women, with eyes reaching to his ears,
Whose body has the fragrance of sandalwood, whose face is adorned with ear-ornaments,
Whose hands, reaching to his knees, are capable of all deeds in battle.
He by whom a sword is girded for the protection of the weak,
And who bears a bow hard as stone, with arrows, unbearable by others.
The conqueror of those who obstruct sacrifices in battle, the perpetuator of <s>Dharma</s> in the forest,
He who always grants freedom from fear to the wives and cattle of the sages."
Then, being turned away, she entered <s>Rāma</s>'s hut,
Saying respectfully: "Take me, <s>Rāma</s>!"
"He is not without a wife, while I am with a wife; he will nourish you more,
As your husband" — thus <s>Rāma</s> spoke: "Go to him alone; do not abandon him."
She, lusting, went to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> again, like a cow approaching a great bull,
Her mind tormented by the onslaught of <s>Manmatha</s>'s (the god of love's) weapons.
As the lustful one kept approaching, the best of the <s>Raghu</s>s,
Drawing the sword from its sheath, made her face noseless.
"I am named <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>; surely you did not know me —
This punishment which has been inflicted on me, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> warrior's deed!" — so she said.
She cursed them while standing in the sky, displaying her terrifying form,

children.text: apisphavac ca bandhūnāṃ ninaṅkṣur vikramaṃ muhuḥ
children.translated_text: And repeatedly proclaimed the valor of her kinsmen, desiring to destroy them;
Before her brothers <s>Khara</s> and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>, she lamented,
Wishing to incite them to seize <s>Rāma</s>, the dwellers of the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest:
"Those two who were banished by their father for the sake of the son of the favored wife, <s>Bharata</s>,

children.text: pitrā daurbhāgineyau yau, paśyataṃ ceṣṭitaṃ tayoḥ.
children.translated_text: The sons of the unfavored wife — see what they have done!
I, the sister of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> my lord, have suffered this degradation from the ascetics by your two —

children.text: ayaṃ tāpasakād dhvaṃsaḥ, kṣamadhvaṃ, yadi vaḥ kṣamam.
children.translated_text: Bear it, if you are able to bear it.
Wearing garments not properly fashioned, eating fruits not cultivated,
Surrounded by retainers not hired — yet they treated me with contempt."
"Tomorrow you shall have obtained your satisfaction" — she was told by the brothers,

children.text: prāṇivas tava mānā'rthaṃ, vrajā''śvasihi, mā rudaḥ.
children.translated_text: "We shall fight for your honor; go, take heart, do not weep.
We devour men day and night, even the innocent;

children.text: kutas-tyaṃ bhīru ! yat tebhyo druhyadbhyo 'pi kṣamāmahe."
children.translated_text: How could it be, O timid one, that we would tolerate those who actually offend us?"
Those two then set forth with a force of fourteen thousand,
Accompanied by those bearing battle-axes, bows, spears, and lances.
Then, as the terrible ones rushed forward, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> with their arrows
Slew in battle those with many heads, those with two heads, and those with three heads.
With those cut, broken, crushed, shattered, split, and destroyed,
Submerged, agitated, shrunken, and wretched — the earth was covered.
Some were seized by trembling, others by intense shivering,

children.text: sa-raktaṃ vamathuṃ kecid, bhrājathuṃ na ca ke-cana.
children.translated_text: Some by vomiting blood, but some no longer shone at all.

children.text: mṛgayumiva mṛgo 'tha dakṣiṇermā, diśamiva dāha-vatīṃ marāvudanyan,
children.translated_text: Like a deer toward a hunter, like one toward a direction burning with fire in a desert,
The three-headed one approached the son of <s>Raghu</s>, as a serpent approaches the fierce-faced king of birds;
With all his heads severed by sharp arrows, like a mountain whose peaks are shattered by an earthquake,
He instilled fear in the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, resembling the portent of the total destruction of the entire clan.
<s>Khara</s> and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>, repelling, advancing, growing in battle,
Leaping, enduring — the two moved about in combat.
Those two, bearing swords, maces, spears, discuses, arrows, and clubs in their hands,
Created a shadow of weapons in the battle shrouded by dust and darkness.
Then, with sharp iron arrows striking the vital points, the best of the <s>Raghu</s>s
Struck and bewildered those two, dispatching the enemies to the abode of <s>Yama</s> (Death).
Her kinsmen slain, <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s> then went from the forest
To her lord <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, dwelling across the ocean in <s>Laṅkā</s>.
Reaching the assembly of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, she wailed, overcome with rage;
She wept out a litany of names — her brothers — before <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
"O hero! Those two who ruled the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, those champions of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>,
Were reduced by two humans in battle — they along with their followers, the lords of the land.
Your war with <s>Indra</s>, whose minister is <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,

children.text: sārdhaṃ kumāra-senānyā, śūnyaś cā'sīti ko nayaḥ
children.translated_text: Together with <s>Kumāra</s> the general — and it was in vain — what kind of policy is this?
If I, O lord, had not come, noseless, with kinsmen slain,
You would not have known all this, being negligent and weak in intelligence.

children.text: kariṣyamāṇaṃ vijñeyaṃ kāryaṃ, kiṃ nu kṛtaṃ paraiḥ,
children.translated_text: What is to be done should be known before it is done; what use is what has already been done by enemies?

children.text: apakāre kṛte 'pyajño vijigīṣur na vā bhavān.
children.translated_text: Even when an offense has been committed, are you, ignorant one, desirous of conquest or not?
You, surrounded by courtesans, lying in bed, heedless,
Addicted to drink, a leader of fortune heading to ruin, with mind lost in trifles —
In sacrifices where fires are piled, where <s>Soma</s> is pressed, in the hermitages,
To consume the principal oblation meant for <s>Indra</s> — there goes one who is difficult to dislodge now.
The curdled milk, the yogurt and milk, the sacrificial cakes, the herbs,
The oblation, and the clarified butter — the <s>Rākṣasas</s> can no longer obtain them.
A young warrior with bow in hand, standing on the earth, while the sky-travelers,
<s>Rāma</s> slays those who obstruct the sacrifices with arrows like the shafts of Death.
The deities eat the meats, the lip-licking offerings, the ritual substances,
While the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, terrified of <s>Rāma</s>, flee weeping in all directions.
Adopt a policy sharp as the tip of <s>Kuśa</s> grass; abandon complacency;
Lead your fortune, which belongs to your descendants, to a state worthy of sons and grandsons.

children.text: sahāya-vanta udyuktā bahavo nipuṇāś ca yām
children.translated_text: The fortune that many capable, diligent, and skillful men with allies

children.text: śriyamāśāsate, lolāṃ tāṃ haste-kṛtya mā śvasīḥ
children.translated_text: Aspire to — that fickle one you hold in hand — do not be complacent!
<s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune), they say, desires the company of men; like a wanton woman, out of curiosity,
Even while standing near her lord, she glances at another through deception.
His beloved is a woman among women, walking like a swan,
Dark as a blade of <s>Dūrvā</s> grass, round as a banyan tree.

children.text: nā''syaṃ paśyati yas tasyā, niṃste danta-cchadaṃ na vā,
children.translated_text: He who does not see her face, or does not revile her lips —
He does not heed what is said; that one is falsely self-restrained.
He is the essence of the objects of the senses for her, and she is the delight of him to whom she belongs;

children.text: talpe kāntā'ntaraiḥ sārdhaṃ manye 'haṃ dhiṅ nimajjathum.
children.translated_text: I think she would plunge into bed with other lovers — shame!

children.text: na taṃ paśyāmi, yasyā 'sau bhaven nodejayā mateḥ
children.translated_text: I do not see anyone whose resolve she could not agitate;

children.text: trailokyenā'pi vindas tvaṃ tāṃ krītvā sukṛtī bhava.
children.translated_text: even with all three worlds you could not obtain her — buy her and become fortunate.

children.text: naivendrāṇī, na rudrāṇī, na mānavī na rohiṇī,
children.translated_text: Neither <s>Indrāṇī</s>, nor <s>Rudrāṇī</s>, nor <s>Mānavī</s>, nor <s>Rohiṇī</s>,

children.text: varuṇānī na, nā 'gnāyī tasyāḥ sīmantinī samā."
children.translated_text: neither <s>Varuṇānī</s> nor <s>Agnāyī</s> is equal to that parted-haired beauty."
The lord of <s>Rākṣasa</s>s replied to her: "Be reassured! Why do you tremble?

children.text: tyaja naktañcari ! kṣobhaṃ, vācāṭe ! rāvaṇo hyaham.
children.translated_text: Abandon your agitation, O night-wanderer! O prattler! For I am <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
<s>Hari</s> (Indra), struck by the <s>yāṣṭīka</s> weapon, worshipped me, eager to see me,
facing me from afar to receive my command, glanced at sideways with disregard.
The thunderbolt, with its sharp edge broken, [struck] upon my chest —
the mighty one thinks himself unbroken and powerful a hundredfold.
Having made <s>Airāvata</s>, the elephant, tethered to the tree of <s>Laṅkā</s>,
I released him like a blade of grass, since he was useless for binding.
Behold my heroic boasting! With the radiance of excellent jewels,
even in the darkness-dispelled city, the presence of the full moon is perpetual.
Robbed of his jewels, his enterprise ruined, paying tribute to the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s in heaven —
does not <s>Gotrabhit</s> (Indra) approach <s>Pūtakratāyī</s> (Śacī) with shame?
A battle with <s>Rāma</s>, who has incomparable might,
would be shameful — yet still I shall strive to subdue him."
Springing up into the sky, the ten-necked one, traveling at the speed of thought, bearing sharp weapons,
proceeded toward <s>Mārīca</s>, who dwelt near the ocean.
Arriving at his abode, he made him hear that entire story;
then, by the frightened one who had heard the purpose, <s>Daśānana</s> (Rāvaṇa) was told:
"Hide yourself from that tiger of the <s>Raghu</s> line, O lord of <s>Rākṣasa</s>s!

children.text: yo raṇne durupasthāno hasta-rodhaṃ dadhad dhanuḥ,
children.translated_text: He who is unapproachable in battle, holding his bow with a firm grip,
he who humiliated <s>Kārtavīrya</s> in a broken treaty —

children.text: jigāya tasya hantāraṃ sa rāmaḥ sārvalaukikam.
children.translated_text: that <s>Rāma</s> conquered the slayer of that one, [a feat] famous in all the worlds.
<s>Tāḍakā</s>, the night-gazing she-demon, knows his valor.
And I, who fancied myself a hero, was repelled from battle by him who roars like a lion.
You have not experienced him, nor has he been experienced by you,
but he has been experienced by me, and I shall be experienced by him again.

children.text: adhyaṅ śastra-bhṛtāṃ rāmo, nyañcas taṃ prāpya mad-vidhāḥ,
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> is supreme among weapon-bearers; those like me become humbled upon encountering him.
He who broke the bow as the bride-price at <s>Mithilā</s> in the sacrifice —
<s>Khara</s> and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>, his co-combatants, knew his power,

children.text: yajvānaś ca sa-sutvāno, yānagopīn makheṣu saḥ.
children.translated_text: as did the sacrificers and <s>Soma</s>-pressers, whose sacrificial cows he protected in the rites.
Born to pleasure, drinking wine, eating human flesh, wearing garlands —
gamble with women in <s>Laṅkā</s>; do not undertake a war with the mighty one."
Abusing him who spoke in fear, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> retorted:

children.text: "yāta-yāmaṃ vijitavān sa rāmaṃ yadi, kiṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: "If he conquered that <s>Rāma</s> who was already spent, what of it?
<s>Tāḍakā</s> was killed by him — she whose ornaments were shame and fear —

children.text: strī-jane yadi tac chlāghyaṃ, dhig lokaṃ kṣudra-mānasam.
children.translated_text: if that is praiseworthy regarding a woman, then shame on the world of petty minds!
That he frightened you, a coward roaring only at home, with arrows

children.text: ku-brahma-yajña-ke rāmo bhavantaṃ, pauruṣaṃ na tat.
children.translated_text: at the wretched <s>Brahmayajña</s> — that was no valor on <s>Rāma</s>'s part.
A bow that had been kept for ages, old, hollowed by worms —

children.text: kiṃ citraṃ yadi rāmeṇa bhagnaṃ kṣatriya-kā'ntike.
children.translated_text: what wonder if it was broken by <s>Rāma</s> in the presence of the <s>Kṣatriya</s>s?
Two heroes who lost their guard against forest-dwelling ascetics —

children.text: kiṃ citraṃ yadi sā'vajñau mamratuḥ khara-dūṣaṇau.
children.translated_text: what wonder if <s>Khara</s> and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>, held in contempt, perished?

children.text: tvaṃ ca bhīruḥ su-durbuddhe ! nityaṃ śaraṇa-kāmyasi,
children.translated_text: And you are a coward, O most wicked one! You always seek refuge,

children.text: guṇāṃś cā'pahnuṣe'smākaṃ, stauṣi śatrūṃś ca naḥ sadā.
children.translated_text: and you deny our virtues while constantly praising our enemies.
Therefore I shall make you increase the earth [by beheading you],
or I shall make you perform the task, wishing to seize the forest-dweller."
To him who had raised a sharp sword, <s>Mārīca</s>, desiring to live, replied,
pacifying him in fear: "I shall be your ally against the enemy.
I shall lure away <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Saumitri</s> (Lakṣmaṇa), becoming a deer to deceive the deer-hunters;
and you carry out the campaign against the enemy as you wish."
Then, becoming a wondrous deer made of gold and jewels,
he leaped about in front of <s>Sītā</s>, greatly enticing her.
The doe-eyed <s>Maithilī</s> (Sītā) wished to make <s>Rāma</s> pursue
that deer, and wished to have a deerskin spread for the broad-chested one.
Then, entrusting <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> with the care and protection of <s>Sītā</s>,
<s>Rāma</s>, striding like an elephant, went in pursuit of the deer.

children.text: sthāyaṃ sthāyaṃ kvacid yāntaṃ krāntvā krāntvā sthitaṃ kvacit
children.translated_text: Now standing here, now going there; now having crossed over, standing still somewhere —
<s>Rāma</s>, watching the deer's wondrous movements, was amazed.
After long exertion, <s>Rāma</s>, skilled in vital points, struck the deceptively bounding one
who was crying out — the night-wanderer who inspired fear.
Hearing a roar resembling thunder, the lamenting one,
thinking <s>Rāma</s> was in distress, urged <s>Saumitri</s> (Lakṣmaṇa) to go.
"This brother of yours roars like a rain-born cloud in the rainy season;

children.text: jñāteyaṃ kuru saumitre ! bhayāt trāyasva rāghavam."
children.translated_text: understand this, O <s>Saumitri</s>! Save <s>Rāghava</s> from danger!"
"This is not <s>Rāma</s>'s cry, but only the sound of the deer that wishes to deceive —
a sound resembling <s>Rāma</s>'s voice" — thus he spoke to her.
"One whose shoulders, neck, and limbs swell with rage, who is able to endure battle,

children.text: prorṇuvantaṃ diśo bāṇaiḥ kākutsthaṃ bhīru ! kaḥ kṣamaḥ
children.translated_text: who covers the directions with arrows — O timid one! Who can face <s>Kākutstha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>)?
The deer, wishing to destroy its body in the fire of weapons, desiring life,
approached <s>Rāma</s> whose thumb was hardened by the bowstring's friction, with the wish to die.

children.text: śatrūn bhīṣayamāṇaṃ taṃ rāmaṃ vismāpayeta kaḥ,
children.translated_text: Who could astonish that <s>Rāma</s> who terrifies his enemies?

children.text: mā sma bhaiṣīs, tvayā 'dyaiva kṛtā'rtho drakṣyate patiḥ"
children.translated_text: Do not fear — today itself you shall see your husband having accomplished his purpose."

children.text: "yāyās tvamiti kāmo me, gantumutsahase na ca,
children.translated_text: "My desire is that you should go, yet you do not venture to go;

children.text: icchuḥ kāmayituṃ tvaṃ mām", ityasau jagade tayā.
children.translated_text: you wish to desire me" — thus she spoke to him.
To her who spoke false and harsh words, the truth-speaking best of the <s>Raghu</s> line
departed, cursing: "You shall fall into the hands of the enemy" — he who was self-controlled.

children.text: gate tasmin, jala-śuciḥ śuddha-dan rāvaṇaḥ śikhī
children.translated_text: When he had gone, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, [disguised as] a fire-priest pure as water, with clean teeth,
muttering prayers, bearing a rosary of beads, carrying a gourd vessel,
with a water-pot and skull-bowl, with a cleanly-shaven head,

children.text: saṃvastrya lākṣike vastre mātrāḥ saṃbhāṇḍya daṇḍa-vān
children.translated_text: wrapping himself in red-dyed garments, carrying a staff, with his accoutrements assembled,
reciting knowledge as one who knows the Self, maintaining the vow of a wandering ascetic,
speaking much with finger-snapping, raising his eyebrows while looking around,
wishing to display a peaceful demeanor while concealing his <s>Rākṣasa</s> nature,
the stroller approached and said to <s>Sītā</s>: "May you be well!"
She whose radiance, with its ever-extending brilliance, put to shame the evening beauty of lotuses and their daytime splendor, she of the pure smile,
the keeper of the lunar calendar —
"Who are you, O timid one, alone in this forest devoid of companions?

children.text: kṣudhyanto 'pyaghasan vyālās tvāma-pālāṃ kathaṃ na vā.
children.translated_text: Even hungry serpents have not devoured you, unprotected — how is that?
You, of heart-captivating form, make even this fearsome forest
auspicious and beautiful — tell me, by what reason have you come here?
O beneficent one, doing what is dear — whom do you serve and adore?

children.text: puṇya-kṛc cāṭu-kāras te kiṅkaraḥ surateṣu kaḥ.
children.translated_text: Who is the meritorious, sweet-speaking servant to you in love-play?
You have assumed a form difficult to obtain even up to the heavenly world.
Having seen your form, excellent life is [found] in us.
Like a lotus-pond on a fine day, from which bees have drunk the nectar,
possessing the beauty of true fragrance — I think you are not without a husband.

children.text: mithyaiva śrīḥ śriyaṃ-manyā, śrīman-manyo mṛṣā hariḥ,
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) who considers herself beautiful is falsely so; <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu) who considers himself handsome is falsely so;
having seen you directly, I consider you one who surpasses the beauty of <s>Śrī</s> herself.
<s>Smara</s> (Kāmadeva) would not feel thirsty at all if he saw you;
sporting perpetually, he would not even keep <s>Rati</s> in his company.

children.text: valgūyantīṃ vilokya tvāṃ strī na mantūyatīha kā,
children.translated_text: What woman, seeing you singing sweetly, would not be envious?

children.text: kāntiṃ nā'bhimanāyeta ko vā sthāṇu-samo 'pi te.
children.translated_text: And what man, even if like a pillar, would not admire your beauty?

children.text: duḥkhāyate janaḥ sarvāh, sa evaikaḥ sukhāyate,
children.translated_text: All people feel pain, but he alone feels happiness
near whom you, being eager, do not act with aversion.
What man, considering himself wise, having taken you who are like a morsel of food,
trembling before hostile ones, would inhabit this empty forest?"
Growing in strength, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, having offered him the guest-portion,
spoke to the ten-headed one with respect, in a faltering voice:
"My husband is of great lineage, in the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> dynasty, a son of <s>Daśaratha</s>,
doing what is dear to his father, a protector of ascetics.
A slayer of those who make enmity, always honoring the virtuous,
the finisher of the might of <s>Paraśurāma</s> in battle,
protector of sacrificers and their oblations in rites, always [performing] meritorious deeds,

children.text: pitur niyogād rāja-tvaṃ hitvā yo'bhyāgamad vanam
children.translated_text: he who, by his father's command, gave up kingship and came to the forest.
In the frightening forest frequented by <s>Piśāca</s>s, foxes, and bears,
the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, severed by his arrows, lie in rows.
Sporting with sharp arrows, hurling great maces,

children.text: nighnānaṃ śātravān rāmaṃ kathaṃ tvaṃ nā'vagacchasi.
children.translated_text: slaying enemies — how do you not know <s>Rāma</s>?

children.text: bhrātari nyasya yāto māṃ mṛgāvin mṛgayāmasau,
children.translated_text: Having entrusted me to his brother, that hunter of deer has gone hunting;

children.text: eṣituṃ preṣito yāto mayā tasyā 'nu-jo vanam
children.translated_text: and his younger brother, sent by me to seek him, has gone into the forest.
Then, with reddened eyes, dripping with profuse drops of sweat,
revealing his inner intention, <s>Daśānana</s> (Rāvaṇa) spoke to her:
"For the sake of his stepmother's son, the elder [<s>Rāma</s>] was banished —
who would think much of <s>Rāghava</s>, who resembles one robbed while naked?
He drove away <s>Rākṣasa</s>s at a petty sacrifice, [fighting] heroes in mock-array —
if that is so, O frog-in-a-well! What pride do you take in just this much?
His kingdom, enjoyments, and possessions have been curtailed by my valor —

children.text: yuktaṃ mamaiva kiṃ vaktuṃ daridrāti yathā hariḥ
children.translated_text: is it fitting to say of me as one says '<s>Hari</s> is impoverished'?
Without <s>Laṅkā</s>, without pride, the lord of wealth, robbed of the <s>Puṣpaka</s> [chariot],

children.text: adhyāste 'ntar-giraṃ yasmāt, kas tan nā 'vaiti kāraṇam.
children.translated_text: dwells within a mountain — who does not know the reason for that?

children.text: bhinna-nauka iva dhyāyan mat-to bibhyad yamaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: Like one on a broken boat, brooding, afraid of me — <s>Yama</s> himself
sits inactive, with a face assuming a darkening complexion.
A golden city on the plateau of a mountain by the ocean —
a treasury of jewels, called <s>Laṅkā</s> by name, is mine, O <s>Maithilī</s>!
In a dwelling sprinkled and swept, you, anointed and perfumed with fragrances,
adorned with garlands of great fragrance — dwell there with me.

children.text: saṃgaccha pauṃsni ! straiṇaṃ māṃ yuvānaṃ taruṇī śubhe !

<s>Rāghava</s> becomes worse by absence — abandon that worthless one.
Eating, drinking, and going about, engaged in the sport of love,
having brought the ten-necked one under your control, rejoice in the finest palace.

children.text: mā sma bhūr grāhiṇī bhīru ! gantumutsāhinī bhava,
children.translated_text: Do not be one who seizes [and holds back], O timid one! Be willing to go;

children.text: udbhāsinī ca bhūtvā me vakṣaḥsaṃmārdinī bhava."
children.translated_text: and becoming radiant, be one who presses against my chest."
Deeming her hostile, the terrible-formed night-wanderer, wishing to seize her,
embracing her with arms pressing tight, soared into the sky.
Carrying her, trembling, toward the abode of the night-wanderers,
the animals and birds fell silent out of fear.
The bird-king <s>Jaṭāyu</s> reached her who was crying aloud pitifully,

children.text: jaṭāyuḥ prāpa pakṣīndraḥ paruṣaṃ rāvaṇaṃ vadan.
children.translated_text: calling for <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, speaking harshly to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
"O enemy! You who roam the forest, taking what belongs to the foremost forest-dwellers,

children.text: agre-saro jaghanyānāṃ mā bhūḥ pūrva-saro mama.
children.translated_text: a leader of the lowest — do not be my predecessor [in death].
One whose conduct brings fame, renowned on earth as compassionate,
who obeys his father's word — shame on you, shameless one, who harm <s>Rāma</s>!
I shall surely be the destroyer of your [darkness],
like the sun [destroying] darkness, O <s>Rākṣasa</s>! <s>Rāma</s>'s servant, comparable to his deeds.
The bird, making the virtuous angry, the one who creates enmity with the man-eater,
that quarrel-maker, making a loud cry, swooped down from the sky.
Shaking the canopy of clouds across all the paths of the sky with his two wings,
he fought with beak-blows that displayed flesh and blood.

children.text: na bibhāya, na jihrāya, na caklāma, na vivyathe
children.translated_text: He did not fear, he did not feel ashamed, he did not grow weary, he did not tremble,

children.text: āghnāno vidhyamāno vā raṇān nivavṛte na ca.
children.translated_text: whether striking or being struck — and he did not retreat from battle.
The chariot with its canopy and armor, driven by one with a demon's face —
In battle, he shattered the terrible one who bore a banner on his chariot, as [one breaks] a bad chariot.

body.translated_text: Henceforth begins the section on the <s>ām</s>-periphrastic [perfect tense].

children.translated_text: He caused terror in the enemy; he delighted the gods who were watching.
He, with his twenty arms, caused the enemy to abandon <s>Sītā</s>.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, undisturbed, made [her] tremble with his weapons, not cold [but fierce].
Again the bird, whose weapons were claws and beak, caused him to split apart.
Those two, overpowered by rage, strove to kill each other.

children.text: na vā palāyāṃcakre vir dayāṃcakre na rākṣasaḥ.
children.translated_text: The hero did not flee, nor did the <s>rākṣasa</s> show mercy.
Gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, and <s>kinnaras</s> attended to watch.
By trickery, the flesh-eater cut off the wings of the bird.

children.text: praluṭhitamavanau vilokya kṛttaṃ daśa-vadanaḥ kha-carottamaṃ prahṛṣyan
children.translated_text: Seeing the best of sky-goers fallen on the ground with wings severed, the ten-faced one rejoiced,
And mounting his excellent chariot yoked with terrible horses, he went to his own city, having seized <s>Rāma</s>'s beloved.
The fire of desire tormented the ten-faced one day and night.
He came to know <s>Vaidehī</s> as one without longing for anyone other than <s>Rāma</s>.
He kept vigil constantly and attentively over the endeavors of the enemy.
He caused terror, being suspicious of <s>Kākutstha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>).
Then, though threatened, he felt no shame in soliciting <s>Sītā</s>.
Nor did he maintain his self-control, being intensely fixated upon <s>Vaidehī</s>.
'Let them find out about <s>Rāma</s>'s conduct,' he told his own [servants],
And the <s>rākṣasas</s>, making great effort, he commanded to guard <s>Sītā</s>.
<s>Rāma</s> too, having slain <s>Mārīca</s>, about to return,
Heard the fierce jackals howling horribly, yelping with ominous portents.
Fearing <s>Vaidehī</s> to be devoured, slain, or dead,
He saw his brother <s>Śatrughna</s>'s co-born [i.e. <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>] coming from afar.
Learning that <s>Sītā</s>, left by <s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>), was alone, trembling, heading south,
<s>Kākutstha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) thought: 'In destruction, safety is very hard to find.'

body.translated_text: Henceforth begins the section on the [aorist with] <s>duh</s>- and related [roots].

children.text: so'pṛcchal lakṣmaṇaṃ sītāṃ yācamānaḥ śivaṃ surān,
children.translated_text: He asked <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> about <s>Sītā</s>, praying to the gods for her welfare.

children.text: rāmaṃ yathāsthitaṃ sarvaṃ brātā brūte sma vihvalaḥ
children.translated_text: His brother, distraught, told <s>Rāma</s> everything as it happened.

children.text: saṃdṛśya śaraṇaṃ śūnyaṃ bhikṣamāṇo vanaṃ priyām
children.translated_text: Seeing the empty shelter, seeking his beloved in the forest like a beggar,
As if milking his own <s>prāṇas</s> (life-breaths), he restrained grief and his mind, and wept.
'She must have gone gathering flowers from the hermitage trees.

children.text: ā yatra tāpasān dharmaṃ sutīkṣṇaḥ śāsti, tatra sā.
children.translated_text: Where <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to the ascetics -- there she must be.'

children.text: āḥ, kaṣṭaṃ, bata, hī-citraṃ, hūṃ, mātar, daivatāni dhik,
children.translated_text: 'Ah! Alas! Woe! How strange! Hmm! O Mother! Curse the gods!

children.text: hā pitaḥ !, kvā 'si he su-bhru !," bahvevaṃ vilalāpa saḥ,
children.translated_text: Alas, Father! Where are you? O fair-browed one!' -- thus he lamented much.
'Here you stayed, here you slept' -- recalling her playful ways, he wandered from here,
The elder brother of <s>Bharata</s> grew faint, remembering <s>Maithilī</s> thus.
'This nocturnal garland of flowers, and that daytime one,
Hung on the branch as if in grief, wither without her.

children.text: aikṣiṣmahi muhuḥ suptāṃ yāṃ mṛtā ''śaṅkayā vayam,
children.translated_text: How often we gazed at her sleeping, fearing from her stillness that she was dead!

children.text: a-kāle durmaramaho, yaj jīvāmas tayā vinā,
children.translated_text: Alas, it is hard to die at the wrong time, since we live without her!

children.text: a-kṣemaḥ parihāso 'yaṃ. parīkṣāṃ mā kṛthā mama,
children.translated_text: This jest is not harmless. Do not test me!

children.text: matto mā 'ntirdhathāḥ sīte ! mā raṃsthā jīvitena naḥ,
children.translated_text: Do not hide from me, <s>Sītā</s>! Do not toy with our lives!'

body.translated_text: Henceforth begins the section on the <s>siñc</s>-aorist.

children.text: ahaṃ nyavadhiṣaṃ bhīmaṃ rākṣasaṃ krūra vikramam,
children.translated_text: 'I slew the terrible <s>rākṣasa</s> of cruel valor.

children.text: mā ghukṣaḥ patyurātmānaṃ, mā na ślikṣaḥ priyaṃ priye.
children.translated_text: Do not destroy yourself because of your husband! Do not cease to love [me], O beloved!

children.text: mā sma drākṣīr mṛṣā doṣaṃ, bhaktaṃ mā māticikliśaḥ,
children.translated_text: Do not see fault where there is none! Do not torment your devoted one!

children.text: śailaṃ nyaśiśriyad vāmā, nadīṃ, nu pratyadudruvat.
children.translated_text: Did the left-eyed one [<s>Sītā</s>] climb upon a mountain, or run back to the river?

children.text: ai vācaṃ dehi. dhairyaṃ nas tava hetorasusruvat.
children.translated_text: Please, speak a word! Our courage has flowed away for your sake.
Lost, you have stolen our reason; you have robbed [us of] our very life-breaths.
Weeping, our eyes swelled; for your sake our faces have swollen.

children.text: mriye 'haṃ, māṃ nirāsthaś cen, mā na vocaś cikīrṣitam.
children.translated_text: I shall die! If you discard me, do not fail to tell me your intention!
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, tell me -- if she said anything as a cause of anger,
