How can a remedy be applied to a fault that is not known?

children.text: iha sā vyalipad gandhaiḥ, snāntīhā'bhyaṣicaj jalaiḥ,
children.translated_text: Here she anointed herself with fragrances; here, bathing, she sprinkled herself with water.

children.text: ihā 'haṃ draṣṭumāhvaṃ tāṃ," smarannevaṃ mumoha saḥ
children.translated_text: Here I used to call her to see me.' -- Remembering thus, he fainted.
The fire of grief consumed her inner being like burning a piece of wood,

children.text: aliptevā 'nilaḥ śīto vane taṃ, na tvajihladat.
children.translated_text: And the cool breeze in the forest did not refresh him, as if it were unguent [on fire].
He, sprinkled by the waters of bathing together with his beloved, weeping without her,
Thus sprinkled water for his ancestors, overcome by grief.

children.text: tathā '' rto 'pi kriyāṃ dharmyāṃ sa kāle nā 'mucat kvacit,
children.translated_text: Even so afflicted, he never abandoned righteous observance at the proper time,

children.text: mahatāṃ hi kriyā nityā chidre naivā 'vasīdati.
children.translated_text: For the ritual action of the great is constant -- it never fails even in times of distress.

children.text: āhvāsta sa muhuḥ śūrān, muhurāhvata rākṣasān,
children.translated_text: He repeatedly called upon the heroes, and again challenged the <s>rākṣasas</s>:
'Come, you enemies of <s>Sītā</s>! Face <s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) in battle!
She who nourished you -- bird-young and deer-fawns that you are -- at her own expense!

children.text: adyutac cendunā sārdhaṃ, tāṃ prabrūta, gatā yataḥ."
children.translated_text: She who shone alongside the moon -- tell me where she has gone!'
<s>Rāma</s> searched the mountain, seeking the one born of <s>Janaka</s>.
A great battle had taken place there; he wished <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> well.
'O <s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>)! The <s>rākṣasas</s> who wished to kill <s>Sītā</s> were surely stopped here.',
'This fresh blood dropped from those two during their fight.
This armor dripped [blood]; this chariot with its horse has been crushed.
Come, let us quickly plunge into searching this mountain!'
'My anger, I think, has become paralyzed; dejection has halted my energy;

children.text: ajārīdiva ca prajñā, balaṃ śokāt tathājarat.
children.translated_text: My wisdom has aged as it were, and strength has decayed from grief.'
'The wings of the vulture here have been made motionless -- look, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>!
Surely this destruction befell him from the night-rover when he tried to devour [<s>Sītā</s>].'
The tiger of <s>Raghu</s>'s race blazed in anger, his eyes reddened in an instant,
He awakened the three worlds from their distress, and like the sun filled [them] with radiance.
Even his supreme courage diminished as if its purpose had been fulfilled.
Great power accumulated in him as he became enraged.
His dejection was milked out as it were, his valor seemed confined,

children.text: samabhāvi ca kopena, nyaśvasīc cā''yataṃ muhuḥ.
children.translated_text: He was united with rage, and sighed deeply again and again.
Then <s>Rāma</s>, grasping his bow, roared with the stride of an elephant:
'I block the path of the sun! I split the great mountains!

children.text: riṇacmi jaladhes toyaṃ, vivinacmi divaḥ surān,
children.translated_text: I drain the waters of the ocean! I scatter the gods from heaven!
I crush the serpents in the netherworld! I cut down the night-roamers!
I yoke <s>Yama</s> (Death) with Time, kindling my skill in weapons!
I grind the earth to dry powder, unwearied by my own splendor!
I crush the prosperity of the <s>yakṣas</s>! I destroy <s>Indra</s>'s valor!
I break all boundaries! I stretch out the vast sky!

children.text: na tṛṇehmīti loko 'yaṃ māṃ vinte niṣ-parākram,"
children.translated_text: This world thinks me without prowess because I do not crush it [to grass]!'
Speaking thus, the son of <s>Daśaratha</s> fitted an arrow to his bow.
The son of <s>Sumitrā</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>) restrained him who wished to destroy the world.
From the hermitage they saw from afar a bird, mountain-like.
<s>Rāma</s>, thinking him the slayer of <s>Sītā</s>, rushed to kill him.
'Do not slay me, <s>Jaṭāyu</s>! I am <s>Rāma</s>! I saw <s>Sītā</s>!'
When he spoke thus, <s>Rāghava</s> attended upon that friend of his father.
He asked the bird about news of <s>Jānakī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>) and about the battle.

body.translated_text: Then the best of birds, having told about <s>Rāvaṇa</s> as the enemy,

children.translated_text: Dying from the pain of his wounds, perished in the mountain cave.
Having performed the rites of fire and water for him, the two set forth again into the forest.
With a terrible [being] who was devouring the strength of creatures ceaselessly,
Hungry, the two were seized by a long-armed <s>rākṣasa</s>.
The two best of <s>Raghu</s>'s line cut off his arms with their swords.
He, with arms severed, fell down bewildered, making the earth tremble.
To one asking what should be asked, he related what should be told:

children.text: ātmānaṃ vana-vāsaṃ ca jeyaṃ cā 'riṃ raghūttamaḥ
children.translated_text: About himself, his forest-dwelling, and the enemy who should be conquered -- the best of <s>Raghu</s>'s line [related all].

children.text: "labhyā kathaṃ nu vaidehī, śakyo draṣṭuṃ kathaṃ ripuḥ,
children.translated_text: 'How can <s>Vaidehī</s> be obtained? How can the enemy be seen?

children.text: sahyaḥ kathaṃ viyogaś ca, gadyametat tvayā mama."
children.translated_text: How can the separation be endured? Tell me this!'

children.text: "ahaṃ rāma ! śriyaḥ putro madya-pīta iva bhraman,
children.translated_text: 'I, O <s>Rāma</s>, am the son of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), wandering as if intoxicated with liquor,

children.text: pāpa-caryo muneḥ śāpāj jāta" ityavadat sa tam.
children.translated_text: Born with an evil form through a sage's curse' -- so he told him.
'Going to your [destined] death, purified by weapons, I tell you:

children.text: rāvaṇena hṛtā sītā laṅkāṃ nītā surāriṇā.
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> was seized by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, taken to <s>Laṅkā</s> by the enemy of the gods.
On <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s> there dwells a blameless monkey, [wrongly] sold by his brother's slaying,
Named <s>Sugrīva</s> -- he is excellent, and of beautiful valor, worthy of you.
Through that ally you shall slay the hateful one among man-eaters,
The <s>rākṣasa</s> of cruel deeds, enemy of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), dwelling far away.

children.text: āste smaran sa kāntāyā hṛtāyā vālinā kapiḥ
children.translated_text: That monkey sits remembering his beloved, seized by <s>Vālin</s>,
Like a bull struck with a stick in the pen because of a cow about to calve.
Having allied with that noble one, O <s>Rāma</s>, act swiftly on what must not grow stale!

children.text: laṅkāṃ prāpya tataḥ pāpaṃ daśa-grīvaṃ haniṣyasi.
children.translated_text: Having reached <s>Laṅkā</s>, you shall then slay the sinful ten-necked one.
There is no untruth to be spoken there -- I speak truthfully.
Having become his friend, you shall accomplish the slaying of the enemy.

children.text: ādṛtyas tena vṛtyena stutyo juṣyeṇa saṃgataḥ
children.translated_text: Respectful in his manner, praiseworthy, gratifying in association,
Thus, as a disciple to a teacher, through his devotion you shall obtain your goal.
Even the ocean is not untraversable for one who possesses such excellent servants.

children.text: manyus tasya tvayā mārgyo, mṛjyaḥ śokaś ca tena te."
children.translated_text: His anger should be sought by you, and your grief should be wiped away by him.'
He, radiant with splendor like the sun, as if he had performed the <s>Rājasūya</s> sacrifice,

children.text: a-mṛṣodyaṃ vadan rucyo jagāhe dyāṃ niśā-caraḥ
children.translated_text: Speaking truth not to be gainsaid, the splendid night-wanderer (<s>Kabandha</s>) ascended to heaven.
Then the two sons of <s>Daśaratha</s>, seeing creepers bearing fruit without cultivation,
Wandered, having lost their memories, [amidst] jewels, food, drink, and wares.
The two, crossing rivers resembling those to be split and overcome, without distress,
Reached in the forest <s>Śabarī</s>, renowned as one who had attained perfection, like a star.
Clad in clean bark garments, with a girdle made of purified [fibers],
Emaciated, dark like a lump of collyrium, staff-bearing, seated on an antelope skin,
Virtuous, with steady gait, of clear form, without agitation,
Not to be grasped [by desire] due to her freedom from passion, [yet] fit to be received by the gods, blameless,
Always devoted to righteous duties, eating fruits that grew without cultivation --

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tāmamucad rāmo yugyā''yāta iva śramam.
children.translated_text: Seeing her, <s>Rāma</s> shed his fatigue as if one yoked [to a burden] had arrived [at rest].
He said to her: 'I hope that at the new-moon conjunction

children.text: pit ṇāṃ kuruṣe kāryama-pākyaiḥ svādubhiḥ phalaiḥ
children.translated_text: You perform the rites for the ancestors with delicious fruits that need no cooking?
Do you perform the obligatory ablutions with the waters that are the gods' share?
Do you honor the <s>soma</s> that is to be pressed at sacrifices by the twice-born?

children.text: ācāmyaṃ saṃdhyayoḥ kaccit satyak te na prahīyate,
children.translated_text: I hope the <s>ācamana</s> (sipping) that must be performed at the two <s>sandhyās</s> (junctions) is not neglected by you?
Do you honor a guest at the proper time as one should honor the fire?

children.text: na praṇāyyo janaḥ kaccin nikāyyaṃ te 'dhitiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: I hope no one who should be turned away stands at your dwelling,
One who would obstruct divine rites, a traitor to <s>Dharma</s>, at a great festival!
I hope you always delight in conversations with those who maintain the sacrificial fires, those who build the fire-altars,
And those who deserve reverence, O auspicious one!

children.text: vardhate te tapo bhīru ! vyajeṣṭhā vighna-nāyakān,
children.translated_text: 'Your <s>tapas</s> (austerity) grows, O timid one! You have conquered the leaders of obstacles,
You have conquered desire and delusion, or have attained them through discipline.
You do not become weary in your austerities; you have fully pleased your elders;
You have not wished to defeat the restraints; you are pleased with your own <s>tapas</s>.'
Then, having offered the <s>arghya</s> (honorific water), <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-mixture), and the rest, she with respect
Worshipped the two worship-worthy ones with fruits and everywhere inquired about their wellbeing.

body.translated_text: Henceforth begins the section on the <s>kṛd</s>-[suffixes].

children.translated_text: '<s>Sugrīva</s>, the delight of the monkeys, will be the agent of your alliance.
You will soon see <s>Maithilī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>).' Having spoken thus, she vanished.
The delightful [groves], the pleasure grounds of the great sages, the [abodes] of forest-dwellers --

children.text: vanāni bhejatur vīrau tataḥ pāmpāni rāghavau.
children.translated_text: The two heroic <s>Rāghavas</s> then frequented the forests of <s>Pampā</s>.
'See, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>! With the songs of bees, cuckoos, and cranes,
Delightful, <s>Pampā</s> is adorned -- piercing our hearts!
See these water-born [lotuses] that outshine the stars, that churn the minds,
That shine forth in the water -- they torment the man without a beloved!
Everywhere, delight is clearly dependent on the beloved,
So that in the absence of the beloved, what do the swans and cuckoos say?
With birds delighted by youth, with trees scattering blossoms --

children.text: a-jño yo, yasya vā nā 'sti priyaḥ, praglo bhaven na saḥ.
children.translated_text: Only one who is ignorant, or who has no beloved, could fail to be moved.
By these upsurges of sounds, by these upheavals of intoxication, greatly...
We are wearied by birds that smell the fragrance of flowers,
by those that bear waves of blossoms, by those able to torment people,
by trees — alas! — we are struck again by those that agitate the hearts,
by those that give grief to ones such as me, by those that nourish the finest fragrance,

children.text: limpairiva tanor vātaiś cetayaḥ syāj jvalo na kaḥ.
children.translated_text: by winds that seem to smear the body — who would not be ablaze with passion?
Dewdrops shedding streams of moisture, beautiful with the lustre of pearls,
gathered on the tips of trembling leaves, cause the mind to melt.
When indeed shall I become the end of this suffering?

children.text: na jīvasyā 'vahāro māṃ karoti sukhinaṃ yamaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s> (Death), carrying away life, does not make me happy.

children.text: dahye 'haṃ madhuno lehair dāvairugrair yathā giriḥ,
children.translated_text: I burn from the caresses of spring, as a mountain burns from fierce forest fires;

children.text: nāyaḥ ko'tra sa, yena syāṃ batā 'haṃ vigata-jvaraḥ
children.translated_text: alas, who is that guide here, by whom I might become free from this fever?
As if seized by a planet, as if by a crocodile in the vast ocean,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā gṛhān smarasyeva vanā'ntān mama mānasam
children.translated_text: seeing the forest retreats like the abodes of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), my mind —
the trees, their branches swaying from the blows of wind, are like dancers,
and surrounded by the humming songs of bees, they are truly unbearable.
The two best of the <s>Raghu</s> lineage, moving like year-old deer,
went to <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s> mountain.
The monkey <s>Sugrīva</s>, thinking those two to be spies of <s>Vālin</s>,
reflected: 'I who am at war with my kinsman — how shall I remain alive?'

children.text: sa śatru-lāvau manvāno rāghavau malayaṃ girim
children.translated_text: He, considering the two <s>Rāghava</s>s to be slayers of enemies, went to <s>Malaya</s> mountain
with his retinue, as if it had risen up touching the sky like an illusion.
The bull among monkeys, situated in a difficult place, dispatched
<s>Māruti</s> (Hanumān), the elephant among monkeys, as a messenger who gives comfort, eager to dispel grief.
He, whose disguise inspired confidence, who knew the way, being focused,
who could read the minds of those desiring conquest, flew up to the sky,
past trees swaying as if staggering from drinking <s>surā</s> (wine), struck by the wind,
and reached <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s>, where bees hummed as if <s>Sāma</s>-chanters were singing.
The monkey, having come to that captivating mountain, spoke pleasantly to the two heroes
who steal armour — a mendicant whose form was worthy of alms.
'You two, powerful as <s>Indra</s>'s elephants, have come to this lord of mountains.
Tell me — why have you come to a place inaccessible even to <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
pervaded by cruel flesh-eating creatures lurking in caves, together with night-stalkers,
covered by trees on lofty peaks, beyond the reach of humans?
Equal in lustre to suckling lions that make creatures tremble,
how have you two come through these rough, stony paths full of buzzing sounds?

children.text: attīrṇau vā kathaṃ bhīmāḥ saritaḥ kūlamudvahāḥ,,
children.translated_text: Or how have you crossed the terrible rivers that overflow their banks?

children.text: āsāditau kathaṃ brūtaṃ na gajaiḥ kūlamudrujaiḥ.
children.translated_text: Tell me — how have you arrived without being assailed by elephants that break the banks?'
<s>Rāma</s> said to <s>Hanumān</s>: 'We two have come to this mountain touching the clouds,

children.text: aiva vidvan! pituḥ kāmāt pāntāvalpaṃ-pacān munīn.
children.translated_text: O learned one, from our father's wish, as travellers, to the sages who cook little food.
Know our father, the supreme lord who cooks immeasurable offerings, the enjoyer of all,

children.text: āvayoḥ pitaraṃ viddhi khyātaṃ daśarthaṃ bhuvi.
children.translated_text: to be the renowned <s>Daśaratha</s> on earth.
By deceit, by a <s>Rākṣasa</s> (demon) that pierces our hearts,
our beloved, whose form never sees the sun, has been abducted — we seek her.'
<s>Māruti</s> replied to <s>Rāma</s>: 'There is a monkey named <s>Vālin</s>,
who in battle could extinguish even the sun that scorches the forehead.
<s>Sugrīva</s>, his brother, has been cast out by that fierce-gazing one.
I have come as a messenger of him who seeks friendship, an obedient servant.
O scorcher of foes, though I am one who speaks pleasantly, I do not speak falsely!
Through alliance with him, you shall slay the ten-headed <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the tormentor of enemies.
I am one who restrains speech in falsehood — I speak the truth to you.

children.text: ehi, sarvaṃ-sahaṃ mitraṃ sugrīvaṃ kuru vānaram."
children.translated_text: Come, make the monkey <s>Sugrīva</s> your friend, one who endures all.'
The monkey, taking <s>Rāma</s> — a wish-fulfilling tree with branches of all-pervading fame —
went to the fruitful <s>Malaya</s> mountain, scraping the clouds.
Seeing <s>Rāma</s> approaching like a cloud-bringing season, weary,
<s>Sugrīva</s> thought him not to be <s>Vālin</s>, the fear-inspiring sun.
The two, who do what is pleasing, made friendship before the fire;
then they deliberated upon actions that bring welfare.
The sitting, the shouting, the prancing, the lying down, the standing —
<s>Kākutstha</s> (Rāma) greatly respected all that the monkeys did of their own accord.
Then <s>Sugrīva</s> spoke to <s>Rāma</s>, the lord who sustains the monkey world, resembling the subduer of <s>Bali</s>,

children.text: sugrīvaḥ prābravīd rāmaṃ vālino yudhi vikramam
children.translated_text: about the prowess of <s>Vālin</s> in battle:
'In the entire earth there is no warrior equal to <s>Vālin</s>;
I tell you what is heart-felt, not out of cowardice.
You, with arrows that go far and pierce deep, are one who attains glory beyond measure —

children.text: api saṃkrandanasya syāt kruddhaḥ, kimuta vālinaḥ
children.translated_text: when angered, you could overcome even <s>Saṃkrandana</s> (Indra), let alone <s>Vālin</s>.

children.text: vareṇa tu muner vālī saṃjāto dasyuho raṇe
children.translated_text: But <s>Vālin</s>, by the boon of a sage, has become a slayer of brigands in battle,
with an unstoppable advance, like the sun rising at dawn, dispelling darkness.

children.text: atipriyatvān na hi me kātaraṃ pratipadyate
children.translated_text: Yet because of my great love, my heart does not accept cowardice
regarding the killing of <s>Vālin</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, which is at hand and will remove suffering.
Beholding you, who have arrived as a head-smiter of enemies,
I consider the fortune of <s>Vālin</s> to be like that attended by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, fallen upon by a husband-slaying fate.
An elephant-slayer in battle who slays foes, who hurls real mountains,
angry, he is to be conquered by you through stratagem, assisted by artisans skilled with hands.
With valour that enriches the great, of the buffalo-demon, the enemy of the gods,
he accomplished the difficult slaying, dear to <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: priyaṃbhāvukatāṃ yātas taṃ kṣipan yojanaṃ mṛtam
children.translated_text: Having become beloved, he threw that dead one a <s>yojana</s> (league) away,
and though capable, being destined to be beloved in heaven too, he did not harm anyone fully.'
<s>Rāma</s>, to test the power of his weapons before the monkey of lesser understanding who wished to know,

children.text: abhīnat pratipattyarthaṃ sapta vyoma spṛśas tarūn.
children.translated_text: split seven sky-touching trees for the sake of conviction.
Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, the sacrificial beast of <s>Vālin</s> destined for slaughter, his fear conquered by <s>Rāma</s> the officiating priest,

children.text: abhyabhūn nilayaṃ bhrātuḥ sugrīvo ninadan dadhṛk.
children.translated_text: roaring mightily, approached the dwelling of his brother.

children.text: guhāyā niragād vālī siṃho mṛgamiva dyuvan
children.translated_text: <s>Vālin</s> came out of the cave like a lion seeing a deer,

children.text: bhrātaraṃ yuṅ bhiyaḥ saṃkhye ghoṣeṇā ''pūrayan diśaḥ
children.translated_text: yoking his brother to fear in battle, filling the directions with his roar.
Confused by the similarity of those two exerting themselves in combat,
the joy of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage drew back the arrow he had raised.
The monkey, exhausted, went quickly to <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s> like a deer,
from the <s>Kiṣkindhā</s> mountain cave, severely battered, breathing hot breath.
<s>Rāma</s> then made the monkey hostile to <s>Vālin</s> distinguishable with a garland.
The slayer of monkeys' foe summoned <s>Aṅgada</s>'s own to fight again in battle.
In the fierce combat of those two monkey generals, which tore the body,
<s>Rāma</s>, standing far off, released an arrow that stole <s>Vālin</s>'s life.
Seeing <s>Vālin</s> fallen, the slayer of enemies,
the monkeys, his kinsmen, crying out in grief, shelterless, fled to the ten directions.
'Shame on <s>Dāśarathi</s> (Rāma)!' said the sages dwelling in the forest.
The monkey-women, drinking honey-wine, came weeping to him.
<s>Rāma</s> was loudly reproached by the lord of monkeys, who prided himself on valour,
fading from the pain of his wound, deeming what was righteous to be unrighteous.
'You are falsely a performer of fire-sacrifices, O <s>Rāghava</s>, a sham ascetic!
Because you kill those engaged with another, you are equal in sin to a slayer of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s.

children.text: pāpa-kṛt sukṛtāṃ madhye rājñaḥ puṇyakṛtaḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: A sinner among the virtuous, son of a meritorious king —
O wicked one, having slain me who am sinless, what will you proclaim?
A king who built the fire-altars, who pressed <s>Soma</s>, who performed rituals beginning with the chariot-wheel sacrifice —
why was your father not heeded by you?
The deed even of a hunter who sells meat is condemned —
yet you, an evil-sighted one, have done this to me without hesitation while slaying me.

children.text: buddhipūrvaṃ dhruvan na tvā rāja-kṛtvā pitā khalam
children.translated_text: Surely your father did not knowingly make you, a wretch, king,
you who have slain me, a sinless one, while I was fighting another.

children.text: pañca pañcanakhā bhakṣyā ye proktāḥ kṛta-jair dvijaiḥ,
children.translated_text: Five five-clawed animals are declared edible by the twice-born sages —
O son of <s>Kausalyā</s>, I, a monkey, am not one of those, beginning with the hare.

children.text: kathaṃ duṣṭhuḥ svayaṃ dharme prajās tvaṃ pālayiṣyasi,
children.translated_text: How will you, yourself wicked in dharma, protect your subjects?

children.text: ātmā'nujasya jihreṣi saumitres tvaṃ kathaṃ na vā.
children.translated_text: Do you not feel shame before your younger brother <s>Saumitri</s> (Lakṣmaṇa)?
What do I think of you killing in battle, born of no <s>Kṣatriya</s> lineage —
O ill-born son inferior to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, O wicked one, sent against us by my younger brother!'
<s>Rāma</s> replied to <s>Vālin</s>: 'I have not done what was not to be done.

children.text: yajvabhiḥ sutvabhiḥ pūvair jaradbhiś ca kapīṣvara !
children.translated_text: By sacrificers, by Soma-pressers, by ancestors who grew old, O lord of monkeys —

children.text: te hi jālair gale pāśais tiraścāmupaseduṣām
children.translated_text: they indeed, with nets and nooses on the neck, approached animals
that dwelt with others' wives, and sought their destruction.

children.text: ahaṃ tu ṣuṣruvānbhrātrā striyaṃ bhuktāṃ kanīyasā
children.translated_text: But I have heard that you, whose wife was enjoyed by your younger brother,
are condemned by the learned — O beast of the creepers!
Then <s>Vālin</s> followed <s>Rāghava</s> as if possessed of shame.

children.text: nyakṣipac cā'ṅgadaṃ yatnāt kākutsthe tanayaṃ priyaṃ
children.translated_text: And with great effort he entrusted his dear son <s>Aṅgada</s> to <s>Kākutstha</s> (Rāma).
Dying, he spoke to <s>Sugrīva</s>, having come to a state of true feeling:
'You and I were nourished by one mother — you know this.

children.text: avasāva nagendreṣu, yat pāsyāvo madhūni ca,
children.translated_text: We lived on the great mountains, and the honey we used to drink together —

children.text: abhijānīhi tat sarvaṃ, bandhūnāṃ samayo hyayam.
children.translated_text: remember all that, for this is the covenant of kinsmen.

children.text: daivaṃ na vidadhe nūnaṃ yugapat sukhamāvayoḥ,
children.translated_text: Fate did not ordain happiness for us both at once;

children.text: śaśvad bahūva tad duḥsthaṃ yato na" itihā 'karot.
children.translated_text: that which was perpetually ill-placed was abundant' — thus he spoke.

children.text: dadau sa dayitāṃ bhrātre mālāṃ cā'gryāṃ hiraṇmayīm,
children.translated_text: He gave his beloved wife to his brother, and the finest golden garland,

children.text: rājyaṃ saṃdiśya bhogāmś ca mamāra vraṇa-pīḍitaḥ
children.translated_text: and having bequeathed the kingdom and enjoyments, he died, afflicted by his wound.
Having completed the funeral rites for him, by <s>Rāghava</s>'s command, <s>Sugrīva</s>
set his mind to enter the cave of <s>Kiṣkindhā</s> mountain quickly.

children.text: nāma-grāhaṃ kapibhiraśanaiḥ stūyamānaḥ samantā- danvag-bhāvaṃ raghu-vṛṣabhayor vānarendro virājan
children.translated_text: The lord of monkeys, being praised softly by name by the monkeys all around, resplendent in attendance upon the two bulls of the <s>Raghu</s> lineage,
entered <s>Kiṣkindhā</s> mountain — whose peaks had become leaf-streams at the time of the waters' descent, buzzing with bees intoxicated by honey — when the rains drew near.
Then the wind of the rainy season blew, making the forest tremble, and the rain-clouds rose up, filling the sky.
The clouds released pure water, the nourishment of crops that are productive,
luminous, with thunder,
as if they had burst open; moving about, shining, adorned with lightning,
refusing to reveal the sun, spreading across the sky on all sides,
adorning it as they moved.
Seeing them, <s>Rāma</s>, unable to endure, lamented as if in ecstatic madness,
dwelling on <s>Mālyavat</s> mountain, victorious yet fading, as if lacking boldness:
'The wind, mingled with <s>kadamba</s> blossoms, even of the tranquil ones
produces extreme weariness, cool with the spray of clouds.
The darkness, as if with a feverish, weary mind, is
hostile, mingling with fireflies, unbearable to the eyes, stealing their sight.
The lightnings, roaming about, cause lamentation,
mixed with <s>cātaka</s> birds that repeatedly strike with cries and laments.
Even the cool spray appears as if it were a burning companion;
the peacocks, playful and quarrelsome, are impossible to bear.
These rain-streams, as if devoted to the gods yet hostile to the passionate,
fall upon innocent people, tormenting them.
This season, thundering, surrounding one with waters, could make
even a <s>yogin</s>, a renouncer of pleasure and pain, deluded.
The <s>cātaka</s> bird, boastful, begs water from the rain-cloud repeatedly,
without trust, as if cutting the mind.
When indeed will these become mournful prattlers, departing?'
The wicked frogs, tormentors of the separated, are harmful.
Despising the day, considering night — the night tormenting —
<s>Kākutstha</s> (Rāma) passed the rainy season somehow, lamenting.
Then, as autumn approached, he saw flocks of <s>krauñca</s> (curlew) birds,
with their calls that increase longing, filling the bright sky.
Looking at the shining moon, he said to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> in sorrow:
'See the geese wandering about, eager for the lotuses.
That monkey, though still roaming, does not become eager today;

children.text: kurvanti kopanaṃ tārā maṇḍanā gaganasya mām.
children.translated_text: the stars that adorn the sky make me angry.
Does the monkey not know that the sun is the nourisher
and illuminator of lotuses at the beginning of day, who has dispelled the mass of darkness?

children.text: atīte varṣuke kāle, pramattaḥ sthāyuko gṛhe
children.translated_text: The rainy season having passed, that <s>Sugrīva</s>, heedless, staying at home,
addicted to pleasures, has surely gone the path traveled by <s>Vālin</s>.
Sitting with talkative women, while you, the swift one,

children.text: gatvā lakṣmaṇa ! vaktavyo jayinā niṣṭhuraṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: "Go, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>! Speak harsh words to that victorious one —
To the monkey reclining on the mountain, swiftly, the disrespectful one,
The transgressor of propriety — tell the sinful, unfeeling monkey.
The monkey who is lustful for women, slothful, devoid of compassion,

children.text: śraddhāluṃ bhrāmaraṃ dhāruṃ sadrumadrau vada drutam."
children.translated_text: Credulous, fickle, unsteady — speak quickly to the one on the wooded mountain."
<s>Sṛmara</s> (swift), of wavering intellect, taking up the radiant bow,

children.text: viduro jitvaraḥ prāpa lakṣmaṇo gatvarān kapīn.
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, far-seeing and quick-tempered, reached the swift monkeys.
Him, ever watchful in affairs, the enemy of serpents — the monkey,

children.text: a-kampraṃ mārutir dīpraṃ namraḥ prāveśayad guhām
children.translated_text: <s>Māruti</s> (son of the Wind), unwavering and radiant, humbly led into the cave.
Surrounded by lovely women, hoping for his own welfare,

children.text: icchuḥ prasādaṃ praṇayan sugrīvaḥ prāvadan nṛpam.
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s>, desiring favor and showing submission, addressed the prince.
"I, O lord, by the grace of sleep, together with your worshippers,
Fearlessly dwelt with radiant women, being a master.
Not knowing the passing of the sun's splendor, the shining of the hare-marked moon,
Engrossed in pleasures bestowed by <s>Rāma</s>, I did not perceive [the time].

children.text: eṣa śoka-cchido vīrān prabho ! samprati vānarān
children.translated_text: Now, O lord, these heroic monkeys who cut away grief,
Who can reach the ends of the earth, mountains, and oceans — I shall dispatch them.

body.translated_text: Then, acting as one who removes neglect of duty,

children.translated_text: The foremost of monkeys, a doer of <s>Rāghava</s>'s work,
Commanded the swift arrival of all the monkey armies.
"We shall go this very day, filled with eagerness, to see <s>Rāma</s>,
As agents of our friend's purpose, for the recovery of <s>Sītā</s>," he said."
Then hosts of monkeys, for the welfare of <s>Rāghava</s>, with joy,
Filling all ten directions with terror, came together.
They approached <s>Sugrīva</s>, saying "We shall destroy the enemy,"
As if they would suddenly make the world free of the ten-faced one.
Understanding that "My task will be accomplished by these who have arrived," he
Approached the shade of the tree of the son of <s>Kākutstha</s>, which was touched by <s>Sītā</s>'s [memory].
Seeing the assembly of monkeys, substantial as the task itself,
<s>Rāghava</s> perceived as if the destruction of the ten-faced one were already accomplished.
Then, in that assembly of monkeys, having arrived at a single determination,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, like a teacher, instructed the study of the directions —
<s>Hanumān</s>, together with <s>Aṅgada</s>, resounding like clouds with water,
<s>Jāmbavān</s> accompanied by <s>Nīla</s>, of beautiful swift movement — he addressed:
"Go, you all, to the southern direction, the abode of <s>Yama</s>, with skill and guidance,
Observing the water-streams of the great ocean, threatening it,
Ascending the heights, reaching the slopes of the mountains,
Making explorations of the forests, with beautiful valor at will,
Having eaten well the fruits, always fragrant when ripe,
And from the heaps of grain, taking nothing beyond what is needed,
As if hearing the chanting of the <s>Chandoga</s>s (Sāmaveda singers) at a great sacrifice —
The humming of the honey-drinking bees, sleeping on beds of flowers,
Surveying the vast expanse of waters of the southern ocean,
Tasting the fruit-juice pressed in the grip of your fists.

children.text: nyāyyaṃ yad yatra, tat kāryaṃ paryāyeṇā 'virodhibhiḥ,
children.translated_text: Whatever is proper wherever — that should be done in turn, without conflict;
Night-rest should be made together, and fruit-gathering in company.
<s>Sītā</s> is to be sought among the <s>Rākṣasa</s> hosts, even by those of small stature, by stratagem,
By those who have reached the borders of the enemy hosts through disguise.

children.text: sāṃrāviṇaṃ na kartavyaṃ, yāvan nā''yāti darśanam,
children.translated_text: No alarm should be raised until she comes into sight;
But once <s>Vaidehī</s> is found, your restraint of the enemy will bear fruit.
<s>Maithilī</s> is to be searched for with the means fashioned like bridle-reins for vessels,
And she should be recognized by her gestures as one meditating on <s>Rāghava</s>'s return.
Like a sacrificial altar, well-prepared and adorned by twice-born priests with rituals,
She should be seen by the end of a month — she who bears a formerly unblemished appearance.
She who surpasses even the sages who eat wild rice, fruits, and roots,

children.text: yasya guṇā niruddrāvās tāṃ drutaṃ yāta, paśyata.
children.translated_text: Whose virtues are irrepressible — go quickly and find her.
Of lofty stature, deep-voiced like a rain cloud, monkey-born,
<s>Rāma</s>, mighty as an elephant, spoke to <s>Hanumān</s> of far-reaching leaps:
"As farmers in drought pray for rain,
So pray for <s>Sītā</s> — go, under <s>Sugrīva</s>'s command.

children.text: vaṇik pragrāha-vān yadvat kāle carati siddhaye,
children.translated_text: Just as a merchant with his wares travels at the right time for success,
So you, attending to the region, go — take this ring as a token."
Taking the token of recognition, they leapt up to the sky,
Like the horses of the sun's chariot released from their reins.

children.text: udak śatavaliṃ koṭyā, suṣeṇaṃ pakṣimāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: The king of monkeys, acting with haste, dispatched <s>Śatavali</s> with a company northward,
And <s>Suṣeṇa</s> with the winged ones to [another] direction likewise.
Meanwhile, <s>Vinata</s>, undistracted, went with monkeys to the east,
Like the sun with unreined horses that travel far.
The monkeys, led by the son of the Wind, went toward the <s>Vindhya</s> mountains,
Concealed like autumn clouds with excellent coverings, to find <s>Sītā</s>.
Treating the lords of beasts with contempt on the mountain peaks,
They roamed the <s>Vindhya</s>, on the path of the fierce-rayed sun, in a manner resembling contempt.
They wandered over lofty mountain ranges, crossed deep rivers,

children.text: āśaṃsavo lavaṃ śatroḥ sītāyāś ca viniścayam
children.translated_text: Hoping for a trace of the enemy and certainty about <s>Sītā</s>,
They traveled with care even over difficult terrain, without obstruction,
Pervading the directions, engaging other monkeys in service.
Some roamed together with laughter, some wandered silently,
Some with self-control like ascetics, while others uttered declarations.
Then, exhausted and voiceless from fatigue, like men whose stakes are lost,
Without intoxication, all the monkeys sat together on a slope of the mountain.
Then, with sudden excitement, they observed birds there
Emerging from a cave entrance, as if with a gathering of animals.
Seeing the approach of the heroes, the monkeys, calling to one another, entered the cave,
Skilled in battle, seeking provisions.
Making calls to their companions, desiring to quench their thirst,
They swiftly entered the entrance of the cave, dark as a mass of darkness.
Inside that cavern, they saw the portico of a palace mansion.
With iron-dense, firm pillars, [they saw] an elegant woman free from impurity,
She, with footsteps that crushed grass-stalks, radiant as the moon without blemish,
With arms round as iron bars, spoke laughingly, welcoming the monkeys.
She satisfied the mountain-cave-dwelling monkeys who had come together in groups,
With fruits of various flavors, wonderful, and with sweet, cool waters.
In that place, covered with abundant trees, with those excellent fruits,
The monkeys, satisfied, asked the shining woman — "Whose city is this?"
"Why do you keep guard? Tell us with effort, O auspicious one!

children.text: svapne nidhi-vadābhāti tava saṃdarśanaṃ hi naḥ.
children.translated_text: Your appearance seems to us like a treasure seen in a dream."
Then she replied to the ocean-deep monkeys:
"This is the city of the <s>Dānava</s> (demon) king, created by <s>Viśvakarman</s>.

children.text: jihataś ca sthitiṃ bhindan dānavo'sau jala-dviṣā,
children.translated_text: And that <s>Dānava</s>, who abandoned his station, was destroyed by the enemy of water [<s>Indra</s>],
I am the daughter of <s>Merusāvarṇi</s>, by name <s>Svayamprabhā</s>.

children.text: jūtimicchatha cet tūrṇaṃ, kīrtiṃ vā pātumātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: If you desire to go swiftly, or wish to preserve your fame,
I shall bring you outside — close your eyes with your hands."
With wisdom, she transported the monkeys whose eyes were shut,
As knowledge [transports] those who have performed their rites — the monkeys who wished to go from that wandering place.
Having emerged from the netherworld by her instruction, with modesty,
Knowing that the month had been exceeded, they fell into distress.
Full of anxiety, they held counsel, fearful of the king's displeasure and reproach:
"Without having accomplished the king's task, how shall we obtain honor?"
<s>Aṅgada</s>, the son of <s>Vālin</s>, thinking that peace [lay] in fasting unto death,
Having yoked himself to <s>yoga</s>, sat on the mountain, revealing the pain in his heart.

children.text: praskandikāmiva prāpto dhyātvā brūte sma jāmbavān
children.translated_text: Then, having deliberated, as though having obtained a means of escape, <s>Jāmbavān</s> said:
"Shame on pleasures that resemble wooden dolls, attractive only to fantasy!
Whatever task this prince undertakes,
I too shall undertake that very task" — having spoken thus, he also sat down.
<s>Māruti</s> (Hanumān) spoke to the old one, to the female ascetic among the monkeys there:
"I shall undertake the fast-unto-death that has come to me by turn;
In the absence of you all, whoever survives here — let his life be accursed."

children.text: ityuktvā sarva evā 'sthur baddhvā yogā''sanāni te.
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, all of them sat, having assumed the postures of <s>yoga</s>.
They recounted the killing of <s>Kabandha</s>, painless, ending in fire without a sword;
"Alas, our terrible fall, ending in decay, as if lordless!"
Then a slow-moving bird, their fast-unto-death
Seeming like a thunderbolt — great, inauspicious in approach,
With beak-tip [ready] to tear their bodies — seeing that bringer of ill-omen,
The monkeys lamented themselves, fallen into the range of evil, again and again.
"<s>Jaṭāyu</s>, the meritorious bird, wanderer of the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,
Who, having accomplished <s>Rāghava</s>'s purpose, ascended to heaven, consecrated by fire —
This is a descent of hell that has come before us visibly;
Without effort, we shall be consumed here unjustly by this one.
With a form like a rising wound in the heart, resembling the approach of Death,
With beak-tip ready to tear the body — having obtained this one, peace is hard to find.
Even slightly enriching himself, this one performs no evil deed in the next world;
He comes here to devour us, exhausted with hunger."

children.text: saṃprāpya vānarān pakṣī jagāda madhuraṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Having reached the monkeys, the bird spoke sweet words:
"Who are you, in this difficult place, even in thought, on this mountain peak?
You lament for yourselves while making conversation about <s>Rāma</s>,
And you praised <s>Jaṭāyu</s>, born of the same womb as us, with reverence."
The monkeys, with words of suspicion and caution, replied to the bird:
"We are messengers of <s>Rāma</s>, the king, whose arrow destroys enemies.
By some base wretch, the beloved of noble lineage, of great family,
Has been stolen from one of great nobility — we seek to recover her.
Considering the thirtieth day to have passed as the deadline for return,
Without having accomplished our purpose, despairing, we worship the next world.
We shall die, we shall not go — unable to find the beloved of <s>Kausalyā</s>'s son,
Not seeing the youthful one — O best of birds!"
The bird said to the monkeys — "You have surely not found a firm resolve,
Since you shrink back at this very time and determine [to die].
This is not a time for those like you to recoil from a master's task —

children.text: hṛta-bhārye cyute rājyād rāmo paryutsuke bhṛśam.
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s>, deprived of his wife, fallen from his kingdom, is exceedingly agitated.

children.text: yatnaṃ prorṇavituṃ tūrṇaṃ diśaṃ kuruta dakṣiṇām,
children.translated_text: Quickly make efforts to extend your search toward the southern direction;

children.text: prorṇuvitrīṃ divas tatra purīṃ drakṣyatha kāñcanīm.
children.translated_text: You shall see there the divine city of gold, extending to the heavens.

children.text: laṅkāṃ nāmnā girer mūrdhni rākṣasendreṇa pālitām
children.translated_text: <s>Laṅkā</s> by name, on a mountain peak, protected by the lord of <s>Rākṣasas</s>,
Which the celestial women beheld when, having conquered <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), it was brought [there];
Which came to rest upon the lord of mountains, as if crushing <s>Indra</s>'s domain,

children.text: kuṣitvā jagatāṃ sāraṃ saikā śaṅke kṛtā bhuvi.
children.translated_text: As if gathering the essence of the worlds — I think that one alone was made on earth.
Without crushing the thousand-eyed <s>Indra</s>, torturing [all] with its own splendors,

children.text: uditvā 'laṃ ciraṃ yatnāt saikā dhātrā vinirmitā.
children.translated_text: Rising long with great effort — that alone was fashioned by the Creator.

children.text: muṣitvā dhana-daṃ pāpo yāṃ gṛhītvā ''vasad dviṣan,
children.translated_text: Having robbed the Lord of Wealth, the sinful one who, having seized it, dwelt [there] as an enemy —
Go to that <s>Laṅkā</s>, abandoned as if wept over by <s>Śakra</s> (Indra).
Knowing your own power, you who wish to seize <s>Rāvaṇa</s> —

children.text: uktaṃ pipṛcchiṣūṇāṃ vo mā sma bhūta suṣupsavaḥ.
children.translated_text: It has been said to you who wish to ask — do not be [like] those who wish to sleep.
Prosperity does not approach one who does not wish to know, a man who wishes to weep;
Why go like those who wish to die? — do not go with the desire of not retaliating against the enemy.

children.text: bubhutsavo drutaṃ sītāṃ bhutsīdhvaṃ, prabravīmi vaḥ,
children.translated_text: Desiring to know about <s>Sītā</s> quickly, seek to know — I tell you;

children.text: mā ca bhuddhvaṃ mṛṣoktaṃ naḥ, kṛṣīḍhvaṃ svāmine hitaṃ
children.translated_text: And do not think our words are false — strive for what is beneficial to your master.
Come together before the enemy, delight <s>Rāma</s>, the best of the <s>Raghu</s>s;
Do not approach fear — <s>Daśānana</s> (the ten-faced one) did not approach <s>Sītā</s> [by force].
Then the monkeys quickly set forth toward the great mountain <s>Mahendra</s>,
All shouting battle cries, and assumed abundant courage.

children.text: nikuñje tasya vartitvā ramye prakṣveditāḥ param
children.translated_text: Having rested in a lovely grove of that [mountain], supremely joyful,
They beheld the ocean, resting upon gems and jewels,
As if enraged, striking the shore-mountains with its impure waves,
Full of splendor, brilliant, as if tossing about with intoxication,

children.text: pūtaṃ śītair nabhasvadbhir granthitveva sthitaṃ rucaḥ
children.translated_text: Purified by cool winds, standing as if bound by rays of light.
As if stringing together and casting aside waves on all sides again and again,
As if deceiving even the sky far away, while remaining within himself,
As if ever thirsting, drinking the sweet waters of the rivers,
As if shining, augmented at night by the moon's rays,
As if striving to conquer the splendor of <s>Meru</s>, blazing aloft again and again.

children.text: vilokya saliloccayānadhi-samudramabhraṃlihān bhraman-makara bhīṣaṇaṃ samadhigamya cā 'dhaḥ payaḥ
children.translated_text: Beholding the masses of water above the ocean, touching the clouds, terrifying with roaming <s>makara</s>s (sea-creatures), and having reached the waters below,

children.text: gamā''gama-sahaṃ drutaṃ kapi-vṛṣāḥ paripraiṣayan gajendra-guru-vikramaṃ taru-mṛgottamaṃ mārutim.
children.translated_text: The bull among monkeys swiftly dispatched <s>Māruti</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>), the best among tree-dwelling animals, possessing the mighty stride of a great elephant, capable of swift going and returning.
<s>Hanumān</s>, of massive body, then ascended to the sky,
Neither <s>Suparṇa</s> (Garuḍa), the sun, nor the winds could surpass his speed.
He shone as the sun does when it rises well at the beginning of autumn;
There was nothing ungone before him as he strode forward — all was traversed.
In the sky, the forms of the monkey and the ocean stretched out,
And he crossed the supreme path frequented by the lord of stars (<s>Arkendra</s>) and the moon.

children.text: vyatijigye samudro'pi na dhairyaṃ tasya gacchataḥ
children.translated_text: Even the ocean was surpassed, yet the fortitude of him who was going did not wane;

children.text: vyatyagacchan na ca gataṃ pracaṇḍo'pi prabhañjanaḥ.
children.translated_text: Even the fierce wind did not outpace what he had traversed.
The son of the wind slew a <s>Rākṣasī</s> (demoness) who was striking and being struck back —
He entered her mouth and emerged swiftly, splitting open her belly.

children.text: anyonyaṃ sma vyatiyutaḥ śabdān śabdais tu bhīṣaṇān
children.translated_text: They exchanged terrible sounds with one another —
The ocean churned by the wind, and the dying <s>Rākṣasī</s>.
He gazed down upon the abode of <s>makara</s>s (sea-creatures), teeming with great crocodiles,
She alone becoming the source of food for many crocodiles.
The mountain that had risen to repay the kindness done by <s>Vāyu</s> (the Wind),
Protected by his father from <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) — he beheld <s>Mainākā</s> mountain.
That mountain, elevating the son of the wind, as if conquering the sky,
Spoke: "May you conquer the enemy after resting upon me!
Take these wonderful fruits, sport upon my peaks,
Behold the flocks of birds playing beautifully.
Rest here for a moment, O blessed one, and then you shall depart again;

children.text: na tat saṃsthāsyate kāryaṃ dakṣeṇorīkṛtaṃ tvayā.
children.translated_text: That task undertaken by you, O skilled one, shall not be hindered.

children.text: tvayi nas tiṣṭhate prītis tubhyaṃ tiṣṭhāmahe vayam,
children.translated_text: Our affection rests in you; we stand ready for you;

children.text: uttiṣṭhamānaṃ mitrā'rthe kas tvāṃ na bahu manyate.
children.translated_text: Who does not highly esteem you, who rise up for the sake of a friend?
The <s>Dvija</s>s (twice-born) who worship the sun with <s>mantra</s>s at the three <s>sandhyā</s>s (twilight junctions),

children.text: rakṣobhis tāpitās te'pi siddhiṃ dyāyanti te'dhunā.
children.translated_text: Even they, tormented by <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, now meditate upon your success.
Rest here without distraction, O hero! I am the friend of <s>Vāyu</s>;
The sun spreads excessive heat — having rested with me, proceed.
This fierce heat is unbearable to endure,
As if being struck on all sides repeatedly with blazing firebrands.

children.text: saṃśṛṇuṣva kape ! matkaiḥ saṃgacchasva vanaiḥ śubhaiḥ,
children.translated_text: Listen, O monkey! Enjoy my beautiful forests,
My cherished desires have been fulfilled by your arrival.

children.text: ke na saṃvidrate, vāyor mainākā'drir yathā sakhā,
children.translated_text: Who does not tremble? — just as <s>Mainākā</s> mountain is the friend of <s>Vāyu</s>,
I call upon you with effort, being trusting — declare what you wish to say."
To that mountain, which seemed to be measuring the sky, the monkey spoke,
Greatly honoring him who was offering help, as a dependent would.
"I go to see ten-faced <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who has seized
The wife of our noble family — I am in haste, O lord of mountains! Do not assist anyone else.

children.text: yo'pacakre vanāt sītāmadhicakre na yaṃ hariḥ,
children.translated_text: He who stole <s>Sītā</s> from the forest, whom the monkey-lord has not yet overcome —
Exerting my powers and voice today, I shall destroy his strength.
I shall wreak havoc in the city of that sinful enemy of <s>Raghu</s>'s line today;
I shall either take away his dear life-breaths, or I shall carry back glory.
Or I shall destroy my anger by striding into the assembly of enemies."

children.text: ityuktvā khe parākraṃsta tūrṇaṃ sūnur nabhasvataḥ.
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the son of <s>Nabhasvat</s> (the Wind) swiftly leaped through the sky.
A <s>Rākṣasī</s> began to test his valor,
As if ascending to the heavens — a terrifying comet-star.
<s>Hanumān</s> entered the mouth, which spanned a hundred <s>yojana</s>s (leagues), of her who was advancing through the water,
And emerged undetected, having become minute.
As he was advancing to see <s>Sītā</s>, at the shore of the ocean,
He was approached by a host of terrible <s>Niśācara</s>s (night-roamers) advancing in ranks.
Concealing himself, reduced to the size of a hare, he passed the day,
The wise one, skilled in action, resolved: 'I shall reconnoiter at night.'
Recognizing and slaying many of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s followers,
He entered <s>Laṅkā</s> at night — the fortress impenetrable to enemies — while killing them.
He was not addressed by anyone, nor did he speak to anyone,
Hearing from the people who were conversing about the virtues of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
With chatter, shouts, songs, dances, smiles, and prancing,
<s>Laṅkā</s> seemed to resound like the city before a sacrificial festival.
He saw her (Laṅkā) joined with <s>Brahma-Rākṣasa</s>s who were quarreling,
And also with <s>Piśāca</s>s (ghouls) who were devouring flesh and blood.

children.text: yathā-svaṃ saṃgirante sma goṣṭhīṣu svāmino guṇān,
children.translated_text: In gatherings they were recounting the virtues of their lord as was their custom;
Drunkards fond of drink wandered the streets in groups, intoxicated.
Others moved about in vehicles — elephants, horses, chariots, and such;
Others offered beautiful flowers and fruits to bards.
Some women, out of anger, did not accept the wine offered by their lovers,
And the lovers swore to those women who wished to test their love.
He did not wish to see the dances nor listen to the singers —
That monkey wished only to remember <s>Rāma</s>, who was afflicted by the sorrow of separation.
As if wishing to observe the sight of <s>Laṅkā</s>, the moon
Rose in the eastern quarter, freed from darkness, with unobstructed rays.

children.text: āśuśrūṣan sa maithilyā vārtāṃ harmyeṣu rakṣasām
children.translated_text: He was listening for news of <s>Maithilī</s> (Sītā) in the mansions of the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s,
Wandering suspiciously while the darkness was fading.
The monkey beheld a guard of a hundred thousand <s>Rākṣasa</s>s in the midst,
So terrifying that even Death himself would die upon approaching it.
Then, as the moon was ascending to the middle of the sky,
The city gleamed exceedingly with its white, brilliantly shining palaces.
People drank the moon transferred into their cups as if it were <s>amṛta</s> (nectar),
Uttering sweet words, the people being devoted to their gatherings.
As if dispelling their longing, the young host of <s>Rākṣasa</s>s drank pure liquor,
Their minds dissolving in the moonlight.
They made their beloveds drink clear honey-wine with <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus) beside them,
Repeatedly generating confidence for the enjoyment of love-play.
Those <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, skilled in battle, who had terrified <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) himself,
The monkey roamed from house to house without astonishing them.
Wishing to see <s>Sītā</s>, hidden, he disregarded the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s,
And deceived the illusions of the man-haters with his own illusions.
As he was concealing himself from the enemies, the thought occurred to him:
"The lord of the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s is falsely having proclamations made through his spies."
Concealing his own greatness, having traversed the council of ministers,
He went to the house of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who was slandering men,
Filled with divine women who illuminated the directions,
Supreme women claiming the most excellent beauty,
Ever rising to the tasks of love and enjoyment,
Well-versed in the playful gestures of coquetry and amorous charms,

children.text: svaṃ karma kārayannāste niścinto yā jhaṣa-dhvajaḥ,
children.translated_text: Where <s>Jhaṣadhvaja</s> (the god of love, <s>Kāma</s>) sits unconcerned, having his work done for him;
Women who made the young men, intoxicated with passion, serve their own purposes,
Bearing their own radiance, worshipping their own forms,
Drinking as if with their eyes the mental resolve of those who gazed upon them.
Passing by those women, <s>Hanumān</s> proceeded toward <s>Puṣpaka</s>,
The aerial chariot that seemed to imitate the splendor of Mount <s>Mandara</s>.
In it, resembling <s>Kailāsa</s>, with <s>Bhaja</s> trees as its peaks,
He beheld <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who seemed to hurl away the mountain's splendor,
Sleeping surrounded by his retinue, constantly exuding fragrance,
Who was being tended by his servants and who had been engaged in supreme love-play.
He from whose warfare <s>Sahasradṛk</s> (thousand-eyed <s>Indra</s>) had retreated in terror;
For a moment, the son of <s>Māruta</s> (the Wind) ceased from his sight.

children.text: upāraṃsīc ca saṃpaśyan vānaras taṃ cikīrṣitāt
children.translated_text: The monkey desisted from his intention upon beholding him,
Lovely as <s>Meru</s> with its forests shaken by the wind's waves.
Seeing <s>Daśānana</s> (ten-faced <s>Rāvaṇa</s>) alone with his beloved,
The son of <s>Vāyu</s>, disheartened, concluded: '<s>Sītā</s> is not here.'
Then he climbed a wall without waking the night-guards,
Though capable, he did not fight, being eager to see <s>Sītā</s>.
He reflected: 'How can I, a servant of <s>Rāghava</s>, dispel his sorrow?
Or how might I generate the supreme joy of <s>Vaidehī</s> (Sītā)?
Having seen the beloved of <s>Rāghava</s>, I shall then put the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s to flight;

children.text: tasyā hi darśanāt pūrvaṃ vikramaḥ kārya-nāśa-kṛt.
children.translated_text: For before seeing her, any display of valor would be destructive to the mission.'
Thinking thus, he saw nearby the <s>Aśoka</s> grove,
Which seemed to make the sky ascend with its lofty forests, adorned with flower-clusters.
The tiger among monkeys entered it, gently swaying the treetops,
Without frightening the forest-dwelling birds sleeping on the branches.

children.text: avād vāyuḥ śanair yasyāṃ latāṃ nartayamāna-vat
children.translated_text: The wind blew gently in that grove, as if dancing with the creepers;
The seasons, trembling, did not weary one another with their mutual abundance.
Moonlight, nectar, the moon, pools with blossoming <s>utpala</s> (blue lotuses) —
All these fully nourished that grove always, by the command of the ten-faced one.
In that grove, captive women who had been gathered there
Were kindling <s>Puṣpeṣu</s> (the flower-arrowed god of love), surrounded by bewildering <s>Rākṣasī</s>s.

children.text: yasyāṃ vāsayate sītāṃ kevalaṃ sma ripuḥ smarāt
children.translated_text: In that grove the enemy kept <s>Sītā</s> solely out of desire,
But she did not find herself pleasing, even though her beauty had increased fourfold.
The monkey, with slowing pace, surveyed the verdant, towering trees,
Where the branches were rustling everywhere, shaken by the wind.
Moon-gems gleamed without chariots; <s>kumuda</s> (night-lily) pools shone;
Heaps of flower-clusters, scattered by the wind, were rolling about.
As the monkey was about to approach <s>Sītā</s>'s vicinity, certain of the success to come,
Auspicious birds gently cheered him, following along.
<s>Sītā</s> then perceived that she herself would be as if in her husband's presence,
Through true and auspicious omens.

children.text: "niravartsyan na ced vārtā sītāyā, vitathaiva naḥ
children.translated_text: "If news of <s>Sītā</s> were not to be brought back, all our effort
Would have been in vain" — thus <s>Hanumān</s> reflected.

body.translated_text: [Thus ends the section on <s>Ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) conjugations.]

children.text: vṛkṣād vṛkṣaṃ parikrāman rāvaṇād bibhyatīṃ bhṛśam
children.translated_text: Leaping from tree to tree, seeing the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> who greatly feared <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
Who saw no protection from the enemy — unseen himself —

children.text: tāṃ parājayamānāṃ sa prīte rakṣyāṃ daśā''nanāt
children.translated_text: Her who was being humiliated, who was to be rescued from <s>Daśānana</s> (the ten-faced one) with love,
Who was hiding from the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, soiled, with wilted hair,
He who had received the message from <s>Rāma</s>, born of <s>Vāyu</s>, whose smile had faded —
The elephant among monkeys beheld her, like a radiance emanating from the sun.
The lord of <s>Rākṣasa</s>s then came there, displaying his glory to the ill-intentioned demons,
Boasting of himself before the other women.
Deluded by desire, he swore to <s>Sītā</s> while concealing his true nature,
And as if not offering her treasures, he approached her.
Desiring her, he spoke many sweet words to her,
And with gentle persuasion toward <s>Sītā</s>, he neither grew angry nor jealous.

children.text: "saṃkrudhyasi mṛśā kiṃ tvaṃ didṛkṣuṃ māṃ mṛgekṣaṇe !,
children.translated_text: "Why do you vainly rage against me who desires to see you, O doe-eyed one?
Gazing upon other men's wives is the natural law of <s>Rākṣasa</s>s.
The mediocre answer back to those who speak to them, O timid one! — not the noble;
Others reciprocate praise to those who praise them when their purpose is unfulfilled — not those like me.
Desire, O one who plays with affection, the pleasures and the lord of the worlds;
I have been purchased for your enjoyment — I shall do you no harm.

children.text: āssva sākaṃ mayā saudhe, mā'dhiṣṭhā nir-janaṃ vanam
children.translated_text: Sit with me in the palace; do not dwell in the uninhabited forest;
Do not sit upon the ground — recline upon the bed, O one eager for love.
Just as you have captivated my mind beyond resistance,

children.text: tavā'pyadhyāvasantaṃ māṃ mā rautsīr hṛdayaṃ tathā.
children.translated_text: So too, do not reject my heart as it dwells upon you.
Do not despise the lord of the world who bows to you, O ignorant one of duty!
Having beheld me, what woman would desire the unfortunate <s>Kākutstha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>)?

children.text: yaḥ payo dogdhi pāṣāṇaṃ, sa rāmād bhūtimāpnuyāt,
children.translated_text: He who would milk a stone might obtain prosperity from <s>Rāma</s>;
Lead <s>Rāvaṇa</s> to love — him who instructs you in what is beneficial and harmful."
Pleased, I will feed you [with] the three worlds;
why do you cause [her] to weep excessively? Make <s>Rāvaṇa</s> sleep at [her] side.
Have [your] commands carried out by the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, do not offer [mere] pleasantries —
who would not desire the salutation made by <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) [with hands raised] above his head?

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the <s>Kāraka</s> (case-relations).

children.translated_text: Following the words of the lord of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, the devoted wife, angered,
sinful <s>Sītā</s> spoke these words to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who had settled [near her]:

children.text: "na bhavānanu rāmaṃ cedupa śūreṣu vā, tataḥ
children.translated_text: "If you are not [equal] to <s>Rāma</s>, or even to [those who are merely] near-heroes, then
having carried me off by deceit, removing [me from] the two heroes, for what purpose did you bring me here?
"Your conduct is not [that of one] near-heroic — how [can it be so], O lowest of night-wanderers!
Since now, out of fear, your dwelling is in <s>Laṅkā</s>, [hiding] from those who look back [in search of you].

children.text: ā rāma-darśanāt pāpa ! vidyotasva striyaḥ prati
children.translated_text: Until the sight of <s>Rāma</s>, O sinful one, display yourself before women [if you dare]!
An evil-doer [pursuing] the wives of others, having conceived desire, [pursuing] those of good conduct —
<s>Rāma</s> will shine forth upon you before long, right here,
he whose arrows are raised in battle, who stands opposed even to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Where will you sit [in safety], O cruel one, slain by his arrows?
You have not spoken well, O one of exceedingly fierce mind, [you who are] intoxicated with pride, [speaking against] <s>Rāma</s>!

children.text: pariśeṣaṃ na nāmā 'pi sthāpayiṣyati te vibhuḥ,
children.translated_text: That mighty one will not leave even a remnant of you, not even [your] name.

children.text: api sthāṇuṃ jayed rāmo, bhavato grahaṇaṃ kiyat.
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> could conquer even <s>Sthāṇu</s> (Śiva); how trifling is your capture!
Even if you praise [yourself], even if you ward us off — what has been spoken is true, O man-eater!

children.text: api siñceḥ kṛśānau tvaṃ darpaṃ, mayyapi yo 'bhikaḥ.
children.translated_text: Even if you were to sprinkle water on fire — [can you quench] pride? And [quench the pride] that [is directed] even against me?
<s>Rāma</s> [rules] supreme — he who has shown valor will bring about your destruction."
Having spoken thus, <s>Maithilī</s> (Sītā) fell silent before the ten-headed one.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, of cruel form, raising his sword,
enraged, hissing, spoke to <s>Vaidehī</s> (Sītā) for a moment:
"For a long time you have been addressed favorably, [yet remain] averse to compliance —

children.text: na māse pratipattāse māṃ cen, martāsi maithili !"
children.translated_text: if you will not comply with me within a month, you shall die, O <s>Maithilī</s>!"
Returning to his palace, he commanded the fearsome <s>Rākṣasīs</s>:

children.text: "bhayāni datta sītāyai sarvā yūyaṃ kṛte mama."
children.translated_text: "All of you, give <s>Sītā</s> terrors, for my sake!"

children.text: gate tasmin samājagmur bhayāya prati maithilīm
children.translated_text: When he had gone, the <s>Rākṣasīs</s> came together to frighten <s>Maithilī</s>,
and for the pleasure of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, they spoke cruel and threatening words repeatedly:

children.text: "rāvaṇāya namaskuyāḥ, syāt sīte ! svasti te dhruvam
children.translated_text: "You should bow to <s>Rāvaṇa</s> — then, O <s>Sītā</s>, your welfare would be assured!
Otherwise, we would be glad to make you our breakfast."

children.text: tṛṇāya matvā tāḥ sarvā vadantīs trijaṭā 'vadat
children.translated_text: Regarding all those speakers as [mere] straw, <s>Trijaṭā</s> spoke:
"Destroy yourselves, O wicked ones! Make a meal of your own flesh!

children.text: adya sītā mayā dṛṣṭā sūryaṃ candramasā saha
children.translated_text: Today in a dream I saw <s>Sītā</s>, together with the sun and moon,

children.text: svapne spṛśantī madhyena tanuḥ śyāmā sulocanā.
children.translated_text: touching [them], her body slender, dark-complexioned, with beautiful eyes."

children.text: tās tayā tarjitāḥ sarvā mukhair bhīmā yathā''gatam
children.translated_text: All those frightful ones, threatened by her, as they had come,
went [back] to their beds desiring to sleep, [cowed] by her frightful words and actions.
When they had gone, the son of the Wind (<s>Hanumān</s>), recognizing <s>Maithilī</s>,
having arrived and remained hidden for a long time while the ten-headed one [was present],
like one freed from a debt upon the departure of the enemy of sacrifices (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>),
began a conversation about <s>Rāma</s> to awaken [hope] in <s>Maithilī</s>.
Seeing him, <s>Sītā</s> thought: "For whose sake [has] this <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
descended from a tree and approached nearby, [this one] of monkey form?
He appears different from before, in his manner praising the son of <s>Daśaratha</s> —

children.text: ṛte krauryāt samāyāto māṃ viśvāsayituṃ nu kim ?
children.translated_text: has he come, apart from cruelty, to win my trust perhaps?
If this one is different from <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, a follower of <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: sa-phalāni nimittāni prāk prabhātāt tato mama.
children.translated_text: then the omens before dawn were fruitful for me.

children.text: uttarāhi vasan rāmaḥ samudrād rakṣasāṃ puram
children.translated_text: Living to the north, <s>Rāma</s> [must cross] the ocean to [reach] the city of the <s>Rākṣasas</s> —
how [could he have sent someone] across the salt waters to [this place] situated to the south?
South of the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> [forest], crossing rivers, mountains, and forests,
and even the ocean, I was carried off [here] by a male [demon].

children.text: pṛthaṅ nabhasvataś caṇḍād vainateyena vā vinā
children.translated_text: Apart from the fierce wind or <s>Vainateya</s> (Garuḍa),
no one is able to come here — let alone a monkey!"
Thus approaching the troubled, thinking [Sītā] with difficulty, the monkey-chief,
[finding her] momentarily released from the <s>Rākṣasīs</s>, spoke: "I am <s>Rāma</s>'s servant.
Distant from <s>Mahendra</s> [mountain], not far from <s>Vindhya</s> mountain,
not in the vicinity of the ocean — your beloved [abides], O <s>Mālyavatī</s> (Sītā)!
Before the ten-necked one arrived, I entered this grove.
When he had departed, having resolved to see you, I approached.

children.text: tasmin vadati ruṣṭo 'pi nā 'kārṣaṃ devi ! vikramam
children.translated_text: While he was speaking, though angry, I did not, O queen, make a show of prowess,
considering the pros and cons, for the sake of not destroying the [larger] purpose.
Among the monkeys, the chief monkey, friend of the lord among men,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, born [as an ally] of <s>Rāma</s> — from him I have come as a messenger.
Having surveyed the entire city of the lord of the night-stalkers,
skilled in searching, I was assigned to the task of a messenger.
Seeing the most beautiful among women, even among divine women,
having arrived and driven away the most terrible <s>Rākṣasas</s>, worse than serpents —
<s>Rāma</s>, eager for you, intent on reunion with you,
having performed the water-oblation to [his] ancestors during the <s>Maghā</s> [month], dispatched me.
This is the token of recognition for <s>Maithilī</s> from <s>Kākutstha</s> (Rāma) — a signet ring,
entrusted to me with care by [him who is] exceedingly mindful of you.
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, devoted to <s>Rāma</s>, sends [his regard] — he grieves for you.
Let the two princes of kings prepare [to come]! [Wait] for [their] arrival here — do not fear!
Monkeys of terrible prowess will besiege <s>Rāvaṇa</s> here.
Support [yourself] with fortitude, O <s>Vaidehī</s>! Let [the fire of] anger cool itself.
When I have gone, <s>Rāma</s> will destroy the <s>Rākṣasas</s>'
lives — this <s>Rāvaṇa</s> brought you here having forfeited [his own life].
He has been deprived of the enjoyments of kinsmen; he has gambled away his own fortune.
A hundred times a day, the best of the <s>Raghus</s> remembers you alone.
As long as your attendant <s>Rākṣasīs</s> do not become aware,
send a message to [your] husband, the wielder of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, O <s>Maithilī</s>!"
Marveling at [this] entry into the city by the tree-dwelling monkey, she
gave the crest-jewel as a token of recognition, dear to <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: rāmasya śayitaṃ bhuktaṃ jalpitaṃ hasitaṃ sthitam
children.translated_text: Having asked <s>Hanumān</s> repeatedly about <s>Rāma</s>'s sleeping, eating,

children.text: prakrāntaṃ ca muhuḥ pṛṣṭvā hanūmantaṃ vyasarjayat.
children.translated_text: talking, laughing, standing, and walking — she sent him off.
He, carrying the token, wishing to accomplish a terrible deed,
though eager to go to [his] master's presence, pondered for a moment in his mind:
"He who, having performed the assigned task, without contradicting the prior mission,
performs an additional deed — him they call the best messenger.
Having seen <s>Vaidehī</s>, having accomplished a deed difficult even for others,
I shall attain glory, one who conveys tidings, a reporter of news to the lord.
This grove, guarded by the lord of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, must be destroyed by me."
Having thus resolved, the monkey made it resemble [the garden of] <s>Nandana</s> [in ruins].
"[Wishing] well to the two <s>Rāghavas</s>, I am their messenger" — thus declaring,

children.text: hito bhanajmi rāmasya, kaḥ kiṃ brūte 'tra rākṣasaḥ,
children.translated_text: "I speak for the benefit of <s>Rāma</s> — what does any <s>Rākṣasa</s> say to that?"
With flower-pollen tawny from scattered [blossoms], with buds and leaves and flowers stilled, with the ground made colorful by the fall of flowers, with birds of the tree-tops falling noisily,

children.text: śakuna-nināda-nādi-kakub vilola-vipalāyamāna-hariṇaṃ hariṇa-vilocanā'dhivasatiṃ babhañja pavanā''tmajo ripu-vanam.
children.translated_text: with directions resounding with the cries of [those] birds, with deer darting about and fleeing, [that grove which was] the abode of doe-eyed [women] — the son of the Wind destroyed the enemy's grove.
Alarmed by the sound of crashing trees, with flocks of screaming birds agitated,
the night-wanderers reported to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>:
"Where the sun gradually sank, where the wind blew gently,
where [the air was] filled with the moisture of snow — the grove is being destroyed by a monkey."
Then the son of <s>Indrajit</s> [i.e. Rāvaṇa], maddened with rage, dispatched eighty thousand
<s>Kiṅkaras</s> (servants) to destroy the son of <s>Māruti</s> (Hanumān).
Wielding spears, lances, iron bars, javelins, maces, and hammers,
pervading the directions, [those] resembling poisonous glances reached the grove.
The monkey, bearing a fearsome iron bar like a thundercloud,
they too, with blazing weapons, roared like rain-clouds with lightning.
The <s>Rākṣasas</s> clashed with the monkey, steady as the ocean,
like rivers with swollen waters [clashing] with the sea in the rainy season.
Brandishing his upraised tail, lifting the heavy iron bar,

children.text: tasthau toraṇamāruhya, pūrvaṃ na prajahāra saḥ.
children.translated_text: he stood, having mounted the gateway — at first he did not strike.
Those <s>Rākṣasa</s> rain-clouds showered arrows like rain upon him,

children.text: na cā 'hvālīn, na cā'vrājīt trāsaṃ kapi-mahīdharaḥ
children.translated_text: yet the monkey-mountain neither faltered nor retreated in fear.
He cried out loudly, "Stand!" — the monkey hurled the iron bar

children.text: tathā, yathā raṇe prāṇān bahūnāmagrahīd dviṣām.
children.translated_text: in such a way that in battle he seized the lives of many enemies.
Through [their] wounds they vomited blood; with [their] bodies they covered the earth.
Other <s>Rākṣasas</s>, in fear of him, fled filling the directions.
Their courage spent, bodies shattered, [once] fond of life, they cried out,
and beasts feared the roars of the monkey as [they fear] the sound of a lion.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on <s>sic</s>-class verb conjugation.

children.translated_text: Even those lords of illusion, weapons in hand, in chariots,
turned back to kill the monkey — [yet they were] to be killed by the son of <s>Māruta</s> (Wind) once more.

children.text: tāṃś cetavyān kṣitau śritvā vānaras toraṇaṃ yutān
children.translated_text: That monkey, [seeing] those who were to be guarded [by their illusions] lying on the ground,
shaking his iron bar, struck them as they came together, [those] seeking to seize [him].
Then, wishing to protect their lives, wishing to retreat,
the surviving night-wanderers came to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s presence.
"By one alone, many heroes were displayed — as though [we were] careless —
we were turned to flight" — they said loudly in the presence of the ten-faced one.
Perceiving them shrunken from the loss of [their] flesh-enjoyments, agitated,
he, with rolling eyes, dispatched his own ministers, [his] friends.
Those [ministers], resolute, with their sons, of good heart, of great valor,
with unfaltering war-cries, went forth, with variegated weapons in hand.
Seeing them exceedingly firm, bold, arrived by the command of the chief,
the monkey [faced] the cruel ones, roaring terribly, with weapons clanging in hand.
Unscathed, [striking] those who resembled mountain peaks and had come near, he smashed [them] swiftly,
those who had wielded weapons, [men] of great enterprise, untamed even by the gods —
he, who had subdued enemies, whose prowess was stilled [only after victory], whose roars filled the directions,
enraged, struck the enraged ones, the swift one [striking those who had] swiftly come.
As they were being slain, with their ear-splitting battle cries,
the world in all directions was seized with immeasurable terror, its heart [trembling].
Their hair bristling with fear, then those [warriors], their enemies diminished,
in a moment, their valor exhausted, were led to destruction by the monkey.
Having slain the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, the son of <s>Māruta</s> went again to destroy
the <s>Aśoka</s> grove itself, [he] who had vanquished the enemy's authority.
As if to cover the sky, as if to ward off the wind that rose up,
the son of the Storm-god showed no mercy, destroying the grove.
Wishing to rain down blessings [through destruction] for <s>Maithilī</s>, hurling the wish-fulfilling trees,
the hurled trees covered the earth on all sides like a canopy.
Wishing to reveal his intention, wishing to swiftly make known his command,
the ten-faced one, unable to endure the intolerable, [resolved] to kill the monkey.
He said: "You must restrain [yourself]! Go, [face] the prowess of the enemy!
You must be bold in battle with illusions, directed against the enemy face to face!
You must quickly make [your war-cry] resound, fearless, in the foremost of battles!"

children.text: sa māyānāmagāt sotā kaper vidhavituṃ dyutim
children.translated_text: He, the champion of illusions, went to destroy the splendor of the monkey.
Having penetrated deep into the grove, that [<s>Akṣa</s>] drove the monkey into [it], the enemy of foes.
<s>Akṣa</s> began to crush — the crusher of the inhabitants of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
To extract the lives that were to be extracted from the son of the ten-faced one,
taking up the iron bar, [the monkey] stood, having uprooted trees from the grove.
The desired one, desired in battle, endured greatly, [having] endured thoroughly;
the angered one, having angered, opened wide [his mouth]; the enraged <s>Akṣa</s> [hurled] volleys of weapons.

children.text: śastrair dideviṣuṃ saṃkhye dudyūṣuḥ parighaṃ kapiḥ
children.translated_text: Wishing to strike with weapons in battle, the monkey, wishing to break [him] with the iron bar,
wishing to seize [his] fame and glory, struck [<s>Akṣa</s>] who sought [the same] with trees.
Again summoning him who wished to capture, the prince, wishing to deceive [him],

children.text: ahaṃs tataḥ sa mūrcchā-vān saṃśiśrīṣurabhūd dhvajam
children.translated_text: [the monkey] struck; thereupon he (<s>Akṣa</s>), swooning, wished to cling to [his] banner.
Having recovered, <s>Akṣa</s>, in a moment, as if wishing to sustain the worlds by [his] radiance,
in fury, showered the monkey — who appeared as if wishing to blaze forth — with arrows.
Wishing to block [him] in all directions with arrows, [the monkey,] wishing to strike <s>Akṣa</s> with trees,
the monkey performed what seemed an illusion, displaying [his] prowess in battle.
<s>Akṣa</s>, wishing to cover the monkey with weapons, shone forth,
Those who sought to cover him with stones and trees — the monkey shone forth,

children.text: svāṃ jijñāpayiṣū śaktiṃ bubhūrṣū nu jaganti kim
children.translated_text: wishing to make known his own power, desiring to destroy the worlds, as it were.
'With weapons!' — thus the two exerted themselves; the wise ones watched in the battle.
The <s>rākṣasa</s> (demon), having long troubled [<s>Hanumān</s>] with illusions, upon encountering the monkey whose actions were untroubled,
fell to the ground, struck by a mace.
Purified by favorable, cool winds, having blown across the ocean,
having grown hungry, he broke again with his wings the forest that was inhabited [by demons].
With tail raised high, as if nodding his head, moving about,
bearing a mane tossed by the winds, tawny as fire,
other trees fell by his speed as if aging rapidly,
and having hewn some, he brought down other trees by force, [leaving them] helpless.
Even after subduing the hosts of enemies, unwearied, the lion among monkeys
wandered through the forest, about to act, as if about to dance, unchecked.
Then, wishing to cross over, [declaring] 'Let the enemies return!'
he sported like a maddened elephant in the forest of the inhabitants of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
'If the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> himself had formed the intention to fight,
I would have dispatched even him today' — speaking thus, the monkey roamed about.

children.text: "hate tasmin priyaṃ śrutvā kalptā prītiṃ parāṃ prabhuḥ,
children.translated_text: 'When that one is slain and the lord hears the pleasant news, he will feel supreme joy;

children.text: toṣo 'dyaiva ca sītāyāḥ paraś cetasi kalpsyati."
children.translated_text: and even today, supreme happiness will arise in the mind of <s>Sītā</s>.'
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, having summoned <s>Indrajit</s> near, spoke:
'Raging in battles like a maddened great elephant in the forest,

children.text: yayātha tvaṃ dviṣāmantaṃ, bhūyo yātāsi cā 'sakṛt
children.translated_text: you have gone to the end of enemies; you have gone forth more than once.

children.text: śaśaktha jetuṃ tvaṃ devān, māyāḥ sasmartha saṃyati.
children.translated_text: You were able to conquer the gods; you remembered [the use of] illusions in battle.

children.text: tvaṃ sasarjitha śastrāṇi, dadraṣṭhā 'rīṃś ca duḥsahān,
children.translated_text: You discharged weapons; you beheld even formidable foes;
with weapons you seized the weapons even of the great.

children.text: sa tvaṃ haniṣyan dur-buddhiṃ kapiṃ vraja mamā ''jñayā,
children.translated_text: You — go by my command to slay this evil-minded monkey;

children.text: mā nā 'ñjī rākṣasīr māyāḥ, prastāvīr mā na vikramam.
children.translated_text: do not fail to employ <s>rākṣasa</s> illusions; do not fail to display your valor.

children.text: mā na sāvīr mahā'strāṇi, mā na dhāvīrariṃ raṇe,
children.translated_text: Do not fail to release great <s>astras</s> (divine weapons); do not fail to charge the enemy in battle;

children.text: vānaraṃ mā na saṃyaṃsīr, vraja tūrṇamaśaṅkitaḥ."
children.translated_text: do not fail to bind the monkey — go swiftly without apprehension.'
<s>Indrajit</s>, departing from the palace, bowed at his feet,
and having received blessings from him, attained supreme joy.
When he had gone, the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> ceased from his fury,
<s>Indrajit</s> being known for his valor, considering the monkey as good as conquered.
Desiring to smile, he went forth, wishing to display illusion against the enemy,

children.text: jagat pipaviṣur vāyuḥ kalpānta iva durdharaḥ
children.translated_text: irresistible like the wind at the end of a <s>kalpa</s>, desiring to drink up the world,
equal to <s>Kṛtānta</s> (Death) in the reversal [of fortunes], wishing to destroy the worlds,

children.text: vane cikariṣor vṛkṣān balaṃ jigariṣuḥ kapeḥ
children.translated_text: wishing to swallow the strength of the monkey who wished to fell the trees in the forest.

children.text: roditi smeva cā ''yāti tasmin pakṣi-gaṇaḥ śucā
children.translated_text: And as he came, the flock of birds wept, as it were, with grief,
crying aloud for the slain trees, like a kinsman upon the arrival of [news of] relatives [slain].
And as he came, the forest appeared to gasp for breath, as it were,
struck by the wind of his speed, with bright clusters shining, its foliage shaken.
'You shall not live, O wicked one! You are no master of illusions.

children.text: neḍiṣe yadi kākutsthaṃ" tamūce vānaro vacaḥ
children.translated_text: If you do not praise <s>Kākutstha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>)' — the monkey spoke these words to him.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the desiderative of the root īḍ.
