children.translated_text: With his army, covering [the sky] in battle, <s>Indrajit</s> advanced,

children.text: śaraiḥ kṣuraprair māyābhiḥ śataśaḥ sarvato muhuḥ
children.translated_text: with razor-edged arrows and illusions, by the hundreds, from all sides, repeatedly.
The monkey, resembling a great mountain, forcing his way through the shower of weapons,
fled through the darkness-like snares of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, seeking glory.
In battle, with his great mane like a celestial light, bearing bow and noose,
he charged forth, scattering the salutations offered by those led by the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
The monkey, with his power made manifest, wishing to go as the ransom for his master,
shone in battle, slaying enemies, free from wrongdoing.
Hurling trees in four directions, making enemies invisible in battle,
covering the expanse of the sky, he was seen roaming in many ways.
Making fourfold the repulsion of the blows of the enemy warriors who acted with hostility,
about to expel the enemies from the battle, tawny as fire,
illuminating, as it were, alone, he roamed in battle as if beyond price.
The foe of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), bow in hand, encountered him who was shortening [their] lives.
Shooting arrows that inflicted no pain, with radiance equal to the sun,
the glory-maker struck with arrows the monkey who desired glory.
The son of the wind, moving through the sky, did not stumble,
though pierced in many ways by darkness-like arrows aimed at the vital points.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the consonant groups with 'satva'.

children.translated_text: The horses yoked to the shafts of the chariot of the enemy of <s>Indra</s> —
the son of the Wind-god set them free, piercing their lives at the skin-joints.

children.text: suṣupus te yadā bhūmau, rāvaṇiḥ sārathiṃ tadā
children.translated_text: When they fell asleep upon the ground, the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> then
ordered [his charioteer] to bring others, harsh with terror that had departed.
Those who had praised [him before] now wished for battle again, desiring to conquer fear;
he mounted his own chariot, as if unwilling to encourage [his troops].
The monkey — a rain-cloud of apes — who wished to shower armies with trees,
<s>Indrajit</s>, desiring to conquer, again formed a battle array difficult to overcome.
Attacking the monkey in rage, they sprinkled themselves, as it were,
with the warm blood flowing from their wounds, born of the clash of battle.
About to preside over them in battle, having sat down at the gateway of the city,
not despairing, he propped up those who were steady, who were the heroes of men.
The angry <s>rākṣasas</s>, enduring [the onslaught], rained a net of weapons

children.text: yan na vyaṣahatendro 'pi; kapiḥ paryaṣahiṣṭa tat.
children.translated_text: which even <s>Indra</s> could not have endured; but the monkey bore it.
With blood streaming, reddened by the streams of blood,
the monkey, striding without stumbling, struck the enemies with a mace.
<s>Meghanāda</s> (<s>Indrajit</s>), leaping about, [caught] the one who was leaping about against his horse;
he bound the one who was without [means of] leaping with the noose of <s>Brahmā</s>, flashing [with power].
Seized by those who flashed [with weapons], rendered without strength, by the man-eaters,
though able to break free, he did not move, out of reverence for <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: kṛṣīḍhvaṃ bharturānandaṃ, mā na proḍhvaṃ drutaṃ viyat
children.translated_text: 'Perform the delight of your master! Do not carry the monkey swiftly
through the sky, but bring him!' — thus <s>Indrajit</s> loudly commanded his own [troops].
'You who have lost the finger-grasp, who have come here from a place of cowards —

children.text: khādiṣyāma" iti procur nayanto mārutiṃ dviṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: we shall devour you!' — thus the enemies spoke, leading the son of the Wind away.
'The one who protected the twice-born in the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> and other <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrificial rites —
this is the envoy of that human being!' — thus they also said.
'He who ravished <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s maternal aunt's daughter and [others],

children.text: mātuḥ svasuś ca tanayān kharā''dīn vijaghāna yaḥ
children.translated_text: who slew the sons of his mother's sister — <s>Khara</s> and others,
before whom terrors do not manifest at the encounter of <s>rākṣasas</s> —
this spy has come on behalf of that <s>kṣatriya</s> of evil birth.
This wicked one, of crooked intention, seeing the king of kings soundly asleep,
skilled in espionage, entered the pleasure-grove.
Of well-spun threads [of conduct], of complexion equal to the <s>kapiṣṭhala</s> (wood-apple),
established in the conduct of the twice-born, at night he beheld the princess of <s>Mithilā</s>,
foremost in all womanly virtues, seated on a spread, steadfast as a cow,
lying on a bad ground, like a star in the sky, spotless,
of sweet hymns, slender amid all splendors, most luminous, auspicious,
as if scorching herself, turning the forest into light,
with bees made tawny swarming around filaments turned to honey,
with blossoming flowers, auspicious, like a golden jeweled creeper,
releasing tears from her eyes, performing a circumambulatory ablation, as it were,
of her heart scorched by the fire of grief — [she] of supreme vow.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tāmabhanag vṛkṣān dviṣo ghnan parisedhataḥ
children.translated_text: Having seen her, he broke trees, slaying enemies who tried to prevent him,
he scattered them all around, angry, like the wind itself.
Him of unstoppable valor, unresisted in the great battle,
him who had endured [all] weapons — <s>Meghanāda</s> (Thunder-voice) paralyzed him.'
Those <s>rākṣasas</s>, learning that he was about to dry up [their] blood, distressed,
bound the one who was swelling [with rage] with yet more ropes, chains, and the like.
<s>Indrajit</s> was vexed, realizing that the action of another binding upon one already bound
[was futile], since one under a divine bond does not endure another bond.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the consonant groups with ṣatva.

children.translated_text: The <s>rākṣasas</s>, having seized the monkey, approached the ten-necked one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>),
of broad chest, as if stealing the splendor [of all] from before them.
Fearsome ones like <s>Kharaṇasa</s> and others, with their vital parts pierced in many places,
while the moon-disc was present in the western [sky] at the front of the vanguard,
'This one has destroyed the garden, including the <s>Āmravaṇa</s> (mango-grove) and others,
mixed with the <s>devadāru</s> groves' — thus spoke the enemies of the monkey.
The delighted <s>rākṣasas</s>, in the forenoon, bringing the monkey,
attended upon the lord of the blood-drinkers, who was a vehicle of wrath.
Intoxicated with the drinking of wine, the one who stole the pride of enemies,
the abductor of another's wife — the wine-drinkers presented him conspicuously.
The enemies of the thirty [gods], their feet suited for combat, bowed,
sending forth <s>Hanumān</s>, who was crushing the wits of the enemies.
'Cut off the head of the monkey, the destroyer of the forest, upon the ground!' —
thus the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, enraged, addressed the assembly.
He spoke as one who slays the one who is [already] slaying, like a thundercloud rumbling.
Then <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, devoted to his own cause, [addressed] the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>:
'Calm down, O ten-necked one! Cease your anger;

children.text: praṇijānīhi, hanyante dūtā doṣe na satyapi."
children.translated_text: understand — envoys are not to be killed, even when they are at fault.'
The lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> said to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> who was seeking to spare the enemy:
'This evil one shall not live, who destroyed the pleasure-grove.
He caused the <s>rākṣasas</s> stationed in my forest to be slain;

children.text: na prahaṇmaḥ kathaṃ pāpaṃ vada pūrvā'pakāriṇam.
children.translated_text: how shall we not strike this sinner? Tell me — he who first committed the offense.
For one who is about to kill my enemy inside the palace, out of anger —
do not make an obstruction; consider him worthy of departure.
Those who would not make an enemy who has arrived [at their door] bereft of life —

children.text: nyāyyāyā api te lakṣmyāḥ kurvantyāśu prahāpaṇam
children.translated_text: they bring about the swift departure even of rightful prosperity.
Who in the world, having provoked the wrath of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, though of evil mind,
is capable of preserving his life — even if he were <s>Indra</s> himself?
This wicked one, who swings through the forest-edges, a devourer of fruits,
this one shall crush us again, having despised us, [stealing] our honeys.

children.text: hareḥ pragamanaṃ nā 'sti, na prabhānaṃ hima-druhaḥ,
children.translated_text: There is no departure for a monkey, no destruction of the enemy of snow (the sun),
no excessive trembling of the wind — when the forest is guarded by me.
But the excellent sweet wine of flowers in the forest, gathered by bees,
is difficult to drink again, [now that it has been] by this monkey of ruined discipline.'
When the one of face terrible with rage thus spoke, stirring [all],
the monkey spoke words of conciliation to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, for the fulfillment of his own purpose.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the ṇatva [rules].

children.translated_text: 'Seeing a single monkey-envoy, bound and brought to the palace,
how can the anger of one who is lord of the three worlds be as light as straw for you?
For one before whom people who maintain the sacred fires bow, who has turned away from the desire to conquer,

children.text: kasmād vā nīti-niṣṇasya saṃrambhas tava tāpase.
children.translated_text: why should there be fury in you, O ascetic, who are versed in statecraft?
Neither women auspicious throughout the night, nor jeweled lands,

children.text: yaṃ vinirjitya labhyante, kaḥ kuryāt tena vigraham.
children.translated_text: are obtainable by conquering him — who would wage war with such a one?
Unite with <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Sugrīva</s> for the prosperity of the world,
like the two oceans, full of jewels — the <s>Himavān</s> [connecting] the eastern and western [seas].
<s>Rāma</s> and <s>Sugrīva</s> [will be] friends, the monkey-chiefs [will be] servants;
these are obtainable merely by the restoration of another's wife — release <s>Maithilī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>)!
By returning <s>Sītā</s>, you restore <s>dharma</s>; through friendship with <s>Rāma</s>, you gain wealth;
and by giving <s>Sītā</s> with willing trust, gain all three — <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>.
By <s>Virādha</s>, <s>Tāṭakā</s>, <s>Vāli</s>, <s>Kabandha</s>, <s>Khara</s>, and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>,

children.text: na ca na jñāpito yādṛḍ mārīcenā 'pi te ripuḥ
children.translated_text: and even by <s>Mārīca</s> — have you not been made aware of what your enemy is?
And do not consider the killing of <s>Khara</s> and the others a cause for enmity,

children.text: ātmānaṃ rakṣituṃ yasmāt kṛtaṃ tan na jigīṣayā".
children.translated_text: since that was done to protect himself, not out of a desire to conquer.'
Then, with his lotus-cluster of faces trembling from the onset of the wind of anger,

children.text: mahā-hrada iva kṣubhyan kapimāha sma rāvaṇaḥ.
children.translated_text: like a great lake being churned, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> spoke to the monkey:
'Of one whose <s>rākṣasa</s> warriors have been slain, whose garden-branches have been broken,
who says "I am an envoy" — what in you is befitting an envoy?
Slaying the lame, children, and women — <s>Kabandha</s>, <s>Khara</s>, <s>Tāṭakā</s> —

children.text: tapasvī yadi kākutsthaḥ, kīdṛk ? kathaya pātakī.
children.translated_text: if <s>Kākutstha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) is an ascetic, of what kind? Tell me — he is a sinner!'
Knowing that arrogance is the fruit [of pride], how did you speak of [your] greatness?
Since it is devoid of the gain of jewels and the like, the war with <s>Rāma</s> is fruitless.
The taking away of another's wife — is this indeed the <s>dharma</s> of cannibals?
You have spoken as if you had a face [i.e., as if shameless]; what? Is there no apprehension in you?
Tell me, O <s>Hanūman</s>! What kind of friendship is there between men, monkeys, and <s>Rākṣasa</s>s,
who are separated far apart in lineage, conduct, and deeds?
<s>Virādha</s>, though defeated by the two, was one [who was] not worth mentioning;

children.text: hataś chalena mūḍho'yaṃ, tenā 'pi tava kaḥ ? smayaḥ
children.translated_text: this fool was killed by a trick — what pride, then, do you have from that?
And <s>Mārīca</s>, dispatched by my command, intent on fleeing,
devoid of desire to fight, died in the forest, deceiving <s>Rāma</s>.
<s>Rāma</s> truly killed the illusory deer while it was engaged with another —

children.text: tvameva brūhi saṃcintya, yuktaṃ tan mahatāṃ yadi.
children.translated_text: you yourself tell me, having reflected: is that fitting for great ones?
The killing of kinsmen by a man, using [them as] bait, to protect himself —
will the ten-headed one tolerate this? Where indeed is your wicked mind heading?"
The monkey spoke: "I am a messenger; as a stratagem for seeing you,
I deliberately caused the destruction of the trees and the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s.
Those of yours who made the world motionless up to <s>Trikūṭa</s> —
O ten-necked one! How do you say they should not be slain by the king?
What you said about arrogance being the fruit of war with <s>Rāma</s> —
by that [very arrogance], hundreds of families of <s>Asura</s>s and <s>Rākṣasa</s>s have perished.
That you regarded your own <s>dharma</s> as <s>adharma</s> and considered the enemy <s>Rāma</s> weak,

children.text: ripau rāme ca niḥ-śaṅko, naitat kṣemaṃkaraṃ ciram
children.translated_text: and were fearless — this will not bring wellbeing for long.
Just as friendship between those separated by lineage and other [differences] is undesirable,
you should not have carried on enmity either with men and monkeys [so separated].

children.text: virādhaṃ tapasāṃ vighnaṃ jaghāna vijito yadi
children.translated_text: If <s>Rāma</s>, the best among bowmen, killed <s>Virādha</s>, an obstacle to austerities, though [he was] already conquered,

children.text: varo dhanur-bhṛtāṃ rāmaḥ, sa kathaṃ na vivakṣitaḥ ?
children.translated_text: how is he not worth mentioning?
Even while perishing, the great illusionist <s>Mārīca</s> could not escape the range of arrows
of <s>Rāma</s> the elephant — this was stated by you yourself.

children.text: anyā''saktasya yad vīryaṃ na tvaṃ smarasi vālinaḥ
children.translated_text: That you do not remember the valor of <s>Vālin</s> while he was engaged with another —

children.text: mūrcchā-vān namataḥ saṃdhyāṃ dhruvaṃ tad bāhu-pīḍitaḥ.
children.translated_text: surely, while bowing at twilight, you were crushed by his arms and fainted.
Abandon the fight with offerings [i.e., the futile struggle], which is the invention of false kinsmen;
surrender <s>Sītā</s> to the one who is to be honored — through treasury, army, self, and territory."
As the son of the Wind spoke thus in the assembly, with words openly harsh and unbearable,

children.text: parijanamabhito vilokya dāhaṃ daśa-vadanaḥ pradideśa vānarasya.
children.translated_text: the ten-faced one, looking about at his retinue, ordered the burning of the monkey.
Then he, wrapped in bark, silk, and blankets, with his tail blazing and upraised,
flew up into the sky, watched by the enemies of men with eyes full of alarm.
That one, honored by <s>Rāma</s>, skilled in battle, made a tumult in the city of the chief enemy of the gods;

children.text: jvaladagni rāvaṇa-gṛhaṃ ca balāt balahaṃs-rāmama-hitaḥ kṛtavān.
children.translated_text: and he, the swan-like one, hostile to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, forcefully set <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s house ablaze with blazing fire.

children.text: nikhilā 'bhavan na sa-hasā sahasā jvalanena pūḥ prabhavatā bhavatā
children.translated_text: The entire city was not [destroyed] all at once, [but] suddenly by the blazing fire, powerful as it was;

children.text: vanitā-janena viyatā viyatā tri-purā'padaṃ nagamitā gamitā.
children.translated_text: the assembly of women, being separated, was separated — carried to the calamity of <s>Tripura</s>, [they were] carried away.

children.text: sarasāṃ sa-rasāṃ parimucya tanuṃ patatāṃ patatāṃ kakubho bahuśaḥ
children.translated_text: The waters of the lakes, being flavorful, having shed their [cool] bodies, falling in many directions from the quarters,

children.text: sa-kalaiḥ sakalaiḥ paritaḥ karuṇai- ruditai ruditairiva khaṃ nicitam.
children.translated_text: the sky was filled on all sides with the sounds of their [own] partial, piteous cries, as if with weeping.

children.text: na ca kāṃcana kāñcana-sadma-citiṃ na kapiḥ śikhinā śikhinā samayaut,
children.translated_text: Nor did the monkey spare any golden mansion-pile with any fire-crested [flame];

children.text: na ca na dravatā dravatā parito hima-hāna-kṛtā na kṛtā kva ca na.
children.translated_text: nor was there anywhere that was not flowing with people fleeing on all sides, nor any [place] not frozen by the loss of snow [i.e., coolness].

children.text: avasitaṃ hasitaṃ prasitaṃ, mudā vilasitaṃ hrasitaṃ smara-bhāsitam,
children.translated_text: Composure ended, laughter ended, endeavor ended; joyful sport ended, love's charm diminished;

children.text: na sa-madāḥ pramadā hata-saṃmadāḥ, pura-hitaṃ vihitaṃ na samīhitam.
children.translated_text: the proud women were no longer proud, their delight destroyed — what was done for the city's welfare was not what was desired.
<s>Laṅkā</s>, with her shelters ablaze, blazing in form, the lord of the mind [i.e., Rāvaṇa] —
[Same line read differently:] With her firewood-shelters burning, sufficient for the body — desiring the ornament of lordship.
Among the flesh-eaters, after the ten[th lord], the condition of distress increased, as things became evident;

children.text: halatā janena bahudhā caritaṃ caritaṃ mahattva-rahitaṃ mahatā.
children.translated_text: the conduct practiced by the multitude in many ways was devoid of greatness, [though performed] by one [supposedly] great.

children.text: na gajā naga-jā dayitā dayitā, vi-gataṃ vigataṃ, lalitaṃ lalitam,
children.translated_text: The elephants were not mountain-born; the beloved ones were [no longer] beloved; what had gone was gone; what was graceful was graceful [no more];

children.text: pramadā pra-madā ''ma-hatā, mahatā- ma-raṇaṃ maraṇaṃ samayāt samayāt.
children.translated_text: the proud women, due to pride, by great [calamity] — death upon death, by the turn of fate upon fate.
Not [a city] conquered by great monkeys of terrible prowess,

children.text: na vā naraiḥ parākrāntāṃ dadahā nagarīṃ kapiḥ.
children.translated_text: nor [a city] conquered by men — the monkey burned the city.

children.text: drutaṃ drutaṃ vahni-samāgataṃ gataṃ mahīmahīna-dyuti-rocitaṃ citam
children.translated_text: Swiftly, swiftly — the fire having come, having gone; the earth, of undiminished radiance, [was] pleasing; the pyre

children.text: samaṃ samantādapa-gopuraṃ puraṃ paraiḥ parairapyanirākṛtaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: was evenly surrounded on all sides, the city without its gate-towers — made even by enemies, [yet] not repelled.
The lord of the monkeys saw the companies
of charming women, of charming women, being destroyed.
Neither did the golden pools of pure water drive away the bodily sufferings of the women,
nor did approaching the trees, whose leaves and flowers were surrounded by fire, bring the women comfort.
Then, with its garlands of birds scattered, its <s>aśana</s>, <s>bāṇa</s>, <s>keśara</s>, and <s>tamāla</s> trees broken,

children.text: sa vanaṃ vivikta-mālaṃ sītāṃ draṣṭuṃ jagāmā'lam.
children.translated_text: he went to the secluded, garlanded grove, enough to see <s>Sītā</s>.
Distinguished by leaping over dense mountains, the one born of the forest, with eyes bright as forest-blooms,
the esteemed daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, lying on the forest ground, was seen by the tree-dwelling monkey.
The beloved, proud one, in sorrow, her ornaments fallen —
separated from <s>Rāma</s>, the beloved, enduring with [dignified] self-regard.

children.text: mitamavadadudāraṃ tāṃ hanūmān mudā 'raṃ raghu-vṛṣabha-sakāśaṃ yāmi devi ! prakāśam
children.translated_text: <s>Hanūman</s> spoke to her in measured and noble words with delight: 'O Queen! I shall go openly to the presence of the bull of the <s>Raghu</s> dynasty;

children.text: tava vidita-viṣādo dṛṣṭa-kṛtsnā''miṣādaḥ śriyamaniśamavantaṃ parvataṃ mālyavantam.
children.translated_text: your grief is known to me; I have seen the entire flesh-eater; [I shall go to] Mount <s>Mālyavat</s>, which always possesses splendor.'
He flew up into the sky, [his] advance [being] admired by enemies as having massive, noble prowess;

children.text: rucita-mun nati-mat pṛthu-sattva-vat pratividhāya vaṇur bhaya-daṃ dviṣām.
children.translated_text: [Same read differently:] Having warded off the admired ones' homage, the broad and noble one, he struck fear into the foes like a thunderbolt.

children.text: babhau marutvān vi-kṛtaḥ sa-mudro, babhau marutvān vikṛtaḥ sa-mudraḥ,
children.translated_text: The windy one [<s>Hanūman</s>] shone, transformed, with the ocean; the windy one shone, transformed, with the ocean;

children.text: babhau marutvān vikṛtaḥ samudro, babhau marutvān vikṛtaḥ sa mudraḥ.
children.translated_text: the windy one shone, [with] the ocean transformed; the windy one shone, transformed, he the seal [of <s>Rāma</s>'s promise].

children.text: abhiyātā varaṃ tuṅgaṃ bhū-bhṛtaṃ ruciraṃ puraḥ karkaśaṃ prathitaṃ dhāma sa-satvaṃ puṣkarekṣaṇam.
children.translated_text: He approached the excellent, lofty, splendid mountain in front — rough, renowned, radiant, filled with beings, with lotus-like eyes.

children.text: abhiyā 'tā''varaṃ tuṅgaṃ bhū-bhṛtaṃ ruciraṃ puraḥ karkaśaṃ prasthitaṃ dhāma sa-satvaṃ puṣkare kṣaṇam.
children.translated_text: [Same read differently:] He who was of not-inferior, lofty, earth-bearing, beautiful, rough [nature] set forth — his abode being noble, with the lotus [lake] for a moment.
Marvelous! As if he had come to a picture, wonderful was the mountain with its varied [appearance];
the monkeys, having reached it quickly, were frightened and dazed again and again.

children.text: gacchan sa vārīṇyakirat pāyodheḥ, kūla-sthitāṃs tāni-tarūnadhunvan,
children.translated_text: Going, he scattered the waters of the ocean; those on the shores — the trees — shook them off;
the flower-carpets spread bodily pleasure; upon those, the <s>Kiṃnara</s>s, love-struck, stood.

children.text: sa giriṃ taru-khaṇḍa-maṇḍitaṃ samavāpya tvarayā latā-mṛgaḥ
children.translated_text: The tree-dwelling monkey, reaching the mountain adorned with clusters of trees, swiftly,
with a smile showing his resolve for the task, adorned it with the joyful monkey-army.
Although <s>Garuḍa</s>, the Wind, and the Sun are considered [the swiftest] in speed among flying beings,
even they considered him, who had arrived having accomplished his purpose in a short time, as exceedingly [swift].
With weapon-serpents lurking in wound-caverns, with broad chest-plateau and rough thigh-walls,
with mineral-colors fixed by dripping blood — that monkey-mountain then shone splendidly.

body.text: asyaiva bhedā apare catvāraḥ etad viśiṣṭopamā-yuktaṃ rūpakam
body.translated_text: Of this [figure], there are four other varieties. This is a metaphor combined with distinguished simile (<s>viśiṣṭopamā</s>):

children.translated_text: With waving tawny-maned golden creepers, with rows of open jewel-like eyes clustered together,

children.text: kaladhaita-sānava ivā 'tha gireḥ kapayo bahūḥ pavana-jā''gamane.
children.translated_text: the monkeys, at the arrival of the son of the Wind, were like the golden peaks of a mountain.

body.translated_text: This is <s>avataṃsaka</s> (pendant metaphor), where the remainder conveys the meaning:

children.translated_text: The moon-lord of the monkey-oceans, having delighted them with his sweet appearance,
spreading the moonbeams of [his] words of nectar, made [them shed] tears of joy surrounding their eyes.
Having wearied the creepers of the <s>Vindhya</s>, having drunk the pure waterfall-streams,
the monkey-elephants then shook the honey-forest, joyful, at the command of <s>Aṅgada</s>.

body.translated_text: This is <s>lalāmaka</s> (crest metaphor) combined with meaningful simile:

children.translated_text: The monkey-sun, dispelling the darkness of grief of the tree-dwelling animals, with rays of dear words awakening the lotus of meaning,

children.text: udaya-girimivā 'driṃ saṃpramucyā 'bhyagāt khaṃ nṛpa-hṛdaya-guhā-khaṃ ghnan pra-mohā'ndhakāram.
children.translated_text: having left the mountain as if it were the rising-mountain, took to the sky, striking the darkness of delusion in the cave of the king's heart.
<s>Hanūman</s> went to <s>Raghu</s>'s son, who was in the ascetics' grove, wearing matted locks, deerskin, and bark —
as to the Supreme Person, joined with a man, [both] alike in the appearance of tranquility and <s>samādhi</s>, together with his younger brother.

children.text: kara-puṭa-nihitaṃ dadhat sa ratnaṃ pariviralā'ṅguli nirgatā'lpa-dīpti
children.translated_text: Holding in the cup of his hands the jewel, with fingers spread apart and slight luster,
just as the slender moon held in a thin tawny cloud — he bowed to the king with bent knees and head.
Beautiful, lofty, with the gravity of a jewel, with the full orb of nectar-rays,
the crest-jewel of [his] bride appeared together with <s>Rāma</s>, as the hope of life itself.
Seeing him come from the forest, of diminished luster, dusty and unkempt,
without <s>Maithilī</s> (Sītā), bearing only the gravity of [her memory] — as if [he were looking at] himself.

children.text: sāmarthya-saṃpādita-vāñchitā'rthaś cintā-maṇiḥ syān na kathaṃ hanūmān,
children.translated_text: How would <s>Hanūman</s> not be a wish-fulfilling gem, having attained the desired object through [his own] capability?

children.text: sa-lakṣmaṇo bhūmi-patis tadānīṃ śākhā-mṛgā'nīka-patiś ca mene.
children.translated_text: At that time, the lord of the earth together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and the lord of the monkey-army, both so regarded [him].
"Treating you mindless ones as winds of destruction, and <s>Sītā</s> as a spark, the scoundrel
rests in the forest of <s>Laṅkā</s> like a lion, intending to die" — thus spoke <s>Hanūman</s> [of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>].

children.text: "ahṛta dhaneśvarasya yudhi yaḥ sameta-māyo dhanaṃ, tamahamito vilokya vibudhaiḥ kṛtottamā''yodhanam
children.translated_text: "He who carried off in battle the wealth of the Lord of Wealth [<s>Kubera</s>], along with [his] illusions — seeing him from here, the gods prepared for the highest battle;

children.text: vibhava-madena nihnuta-hriyā 'timātra-saṃpannakaṃ, vyathayati sat-pathādadhigatā 'thaveha saṃpan na kam.
children.translated_text: one whose modesty is concealed by the intoxication of power, excessively prosperous — does not the wealth acquired from the righteous path disturb anyone here?"

children.text: ṛddhi-mān rākṣaso mūḍhaś, citraṃ nā'sau yaddudhataḥ,
children.translated_text: The wealthy <s>Rākṣasa</s> is foolish — it is no wonder that he is agitated;

children.text: ko vā heturanāryāṇāṃ dharmye vartmani vartitum.
children.translated_text: what reason indeed have the ignoble to walk upon the path of righteousness?

children.text: tasyā 'dhivāse tanurutsukā 'sau dṛṣṭā mayā rāma-patiḥ pra-manyuḥ,
children.translated_text: "In her dwelling, this body is anxious; I have seen her — the lord of <s>Rāma</s> [<s>Sītā</s>] is wrathful;

children.text: kāryasya sāro 'yamudīrito vaḥ, proktena śeṣeṇa kimuddhatena.
children.translated_text: this is the essence of the matter told to you — what use is the rest of what has been said, inflated [as it is]?"

children.text: samatāṃ śaśi-lekhayopayāyā- davadātā pra-tanuḥ kṣayeṇa sītā,
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s>, though fair and slender, by her wasting, approached equality with a crescent moon;

children.text: yadi nāma kalaṅka indu-lekhā- mativṛtto laghayen na cā 'pi bhāvī.
children.translated_text: but if a stain should exceed the crescent moon, it would diminish it — and that [stain] is not to come [upon Sītā].
"She was seized by one who acts without deliberation, who has not served the wise and elderly,

children.text: a-virodhita-niṣṭhureṇa sādhvīṃ dayitāṃ trātumalaṃ ghaṭasva rājan !"
children.translated_text: who has not been opposed by the cruel — O King, strive well to rescue the noble beloved woman!"
And that great lake, filled with trembling beings, drying up,
was scorched all around by anguish; and the desired water [i.e., <s>Sītā</s>] had fallen away without clouds [i.e., without hope].
Then the monkeys met and followed <s>Rāma</s>, who was equal to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> in beauty and appearance, whose foremost hand extended with the command to march,
whose respectful command was received by the bowing <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: kapi-pṛṣṭha-gatau tato narendrau. kapayaś ca jvalitā'gni-piṅgalā'kṣāḥ
children.translated_text: Then, the two kings mounted on the backs of monkeys; and the monkeys with eyes tawny as blazing fire

children.text: mumucuḥ, prayayur, drutaṃ samīyur, vasudhāṃ, vyoma, mahīdharaṃ mahendram
children.translated_text: released, proceeded, and swiftly gathered upon — the earth, the sky, and the great mountain <s>Mahendra</s>.
As if stationed to protect the earth on all sides from the flooding of the ocean waters,
stretching his body between the surface of the sky and the earth, able to endure the force of the ocean —
Rooted in the abode of serpents, its hundreds of peaks brushing the world of the gods,
its dense and wide slopes filling the directions, with beautiful groves adorned with fruit-and-flower-laden trees,
With the hummings of bees echoing the voices of beloveds, with lotuses [mirroring] the beauty of the smiles of darlings' faces,
bearing supreme delight openly enchanting — [such was the scene] for the lord of men (<s>Rāma</s>), suddenly [arising].
The hip of the sky, wearing a girdle of planets and gems, endowed with great and unsurpassed beauty,
its dense garment of clouds having slipped, delightful to the mind — as if touched by the finger-peaks [of mountains] with desire,
Avoiding the fickle, unsteady multitude, unable to bear the weight, unequal and lacking in vigor,
as if having made its dwelling near the ocean-shore — the firm, incomparably exalted, lofty, towering cloud.
With mansions of crystal gems, with jewelled lamps, and with the melodious songs of young <s>Kinnaras</s>,
giving the impression of the city of the immortals to the celestial women — free from sorrow, with abundant wish-fulfilling trees.
Then, the monkey armies together with <s>Sītā</s>'s lord (<s>Rāma</s>) and the sons of <s>Raghu</s> saw the direction bounded by the ocean,
grey with billowing smoke, pointed out by the finger of the son of the Wind (<s>Hanumān</s>), looking southward.
They went to the ocean from <s>Mahendra</s>'s grove, their luster concealed by the accumulated [clouds] hiding the fierce-rayed [sun],
[the ocean] whose shores were unbroken even by the great waves of water, able to bear the weight of the world.
With the luster of great gems born in pearl-oysters, broad and heavy, darkness gathered from the nether regions having been exhausted,
the activity of the sun's rays being obstructed, with high-floating nets of diamonds, very light,
Its waters augmented by the growing, pure river-waters on moonlit nights,
clearly revealing the cloud-laden waters and the moon-jeweled, gem-studded peaks of <s>Mahendra</s>,
Bearing the vast bodies of massive, radiant, gem-laden [mountains], whose glory cannot be surpassed, capable of supporting the world's weight,
with tortoises and crocodiles exhausted and dissolved in weariness, and mighty serpents too with raised hoods,
They beheld great waves — releasing vast sprays of droplets, bearing <s>Indra</s>'s bows formed from the luster of pure gems,
sounding deep and steady like rain-clouds, removing the heat of the earth.
The crests of the shore-ridges, adorned with coral and gem ornaments, their surfaces beautified by clusters of pearls,
were broken by the water-<s>Nāgas</s> (serpents) — where [this occurred].
Bearing the entire nether world, containing gems, its sky hidden by waves equal to mountain-peaks —

children.text: kuta iha paramā'rthato jalaugho jala-nidhimīyurataḥ sametya māyām
children.translated_text: how could this truly be a mere mass of water? The oceans must have attained <s>māyā</s> (illusory power).
Though deprived of the moon, yet of abundant luster; though its glory was taken by the gods, yet of undiminished beauty;
though churned by the gods, [still] overwhelming with its waves and of unimpaired might —

body.translated_text: [Illustration of] <s>vyājastuti</s> (praise under the guise of blame).

children.translated_text: Bearing the earth, the principal mountains, <s>Śeṣa</s>, and the elephants of the directions as if they were a boat floating on water,
surpassing even the great boar [<s>Varāha</s>], who bore <s>Vidhura</s>'s earth, though He was mountain-heavy in bulk — with its resources.
Beholding the ocean — holding a mass of water between the restless rivers flowing around mountains, delightful to the mind —
<s>Rāma</s> [saw it] as if fallen from the earth, wearing white Chinese silk from the breast of the mountain-bearer.
The ocean, endowed with endless, great, wondrous, variegated, pure, and impassable [beings] — trees, lions, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and the lord of the earth —
free from stain, shone supremely, having been attained [by them].

children.text: na bhavati mahimā vinā vipatte- ravagamayanniva paśyataḥ payodhiḥ
children.translated_text: As if demonstrating that greatness does not exist without adversity — the ocean, before the onlookers,
was unceasingly, moment by moment, with its waves spreading wide on mountain-peaks, then becoming calm.

children.text: mṛdubhirapi bibheda puṣpa-bāṇaiś calaśiśirairapi mārutair dadāha
children.translated_text: He burned the son of <s>Raghu</s> with soft flower-arrows, and scorched him with cool, trembling breezes —

children.text: raghu-tanayamanartha-paṇḍito 'sau, na ca madanaḥ kṣatamātatān, nā 'rciḥ
children.translated_text: that expert in calamity, <s>Madana</s> (the god of love), yet neither the wound extended nor the flame.
Then at day's end, of soft, dusky hue, near the ocean, having transcended the world,
imitating each other's forms — the Sun and the scion of <s>Raghu</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) both declined.

children.text: apaharadiva sarvato vinodān dayita-gataṃ dadhadekadhā samādhim
children.translated_text: As if removing all diversions from everywhere, holding concentrated meditation on the beloved alone,
the darkness grew thicker, rich in hue, together with the arising of love in the son of <s>Raghu</s>.

children.text: adhi-jaladhi tamaḥ kṣipan himāṃśuḥ paridadṛśe 'tha dṛśāṃ kṛtā'vakāśaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the cool-rayed moon, casting out darkness over the ocean, appeared, making room for the eyes,

children.text: vidadhadiva jagat punaḥ pralīnam. bhavati mahān hi parā'rtha eva sarvaḥ.
children.translated_text: as if making the world, once dissolved, come forth again. For truly, every great one exists only for the benefit of others.
'This is a thunderbolt — but whence, in a cloudless sky? This is a shower of sharp arrows — but impossible, for there is no <s>Śārṅga</s> bow.'

children.text: iti madana-vaśo muhuḥ śaśā'ṅke raghu-tanayo, na ca niścikāya candram.
children.translated_text: Thus, under the power of love, the son of <s>Raghu</s> repeatedly [doubted] the moon, yet did not ascertain it to be the moon.
Among the beds of night-lotuses, scattering his rays, in the faces of the direction-brides with their darkness destroyed,

children.text: viyati ca vilalāsa tad-vadindur, vilasati candramaso na yad-vadanyaḥ.
children.translated_text: and in the sky — the moon sported in a manner like himself; as the moon sports, no other does.
Darkness, as if gone to the refuge of the groves, screened from moonbeams by the trees, at night,
situated in the interstices of broad, uneven rocks, with the appearance of a rain-cloud — sank as if in fear.
Then, delightful to the eye and mind, charming, born in the heart like <s>Smara</s> (Love) himself, yet of gentle disposition,
the younger brother of the son of <s>Raghu</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>) spoke words whose sound was like rain-clouds with thunder,
"Make the wives of the enemy loose-haired through the slaying of their husbands, their lip-rouge and eye-collyrium washed away by tears from their eyes.

children.text: kuru ripu-vanitā, jahīhi śokaṃ, kva ca śaraṇaṃ jagatāṃ bhavān, kva mohaḥ
children.translated_text: Abandon grief! Where are you, the refuge of the world, and where is delusion?
Alas! He who has attained greatness in the human world sinks even more so when heedless.
The lord of elephants, whose body is like a great mountain-peak, mighty, sinks in the mire — not a piece of wood.

children.text: boddhavyaṃ kimiva hi, yat tvayā na buddhaṃ, kiṃ vā te nimiṣitamapya-buddhi-pūrvam,
children.translated_text: What indeed is there to be understood that you have not understood? What action of yours is without deliberation, even a mere blink?

children.text: labdhā''tmā tava sukṛtairaniṣṭa-śaṅkī snehaugho ghaṭayati māṃ tathāpi vaktum."
children.translated_text: You who are self-possessed, through your merits, without apprehension of the unwanted — yet the flood of affection compels me to speak."

children.text: saumitreriti vacanaṃ niśamya rāmo jṛmbhā-vān bhuja-yugalaṃ vibhajya nidrān
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of the son of <s>Sumitrā</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>), <s>Rāma</s>, yawning, spreading apart his two arms, shaking off sleep,

children.text: adhyaṣṭhāc chiśayiṣayā pravāla-talpaṃ rakṣāyai prati-diśamādiśan plavaṅgān.
children.translated_text: mounted the coral couch with the desire to rest, posting monkeys as guards in every direction.
Then, as the moon set, faint in luster, as if by the exhaustion of merit in the treasury of digits,

children.text: samālalambe ripu-mitra-kalpaiḥ padmaiḥ prahāsaḥ kumudair viṣādaḥ
children.translated_text: laughter arose with lotuses — [which are] like enemies [of the moon] — and sadness with night-lotuses — like friends.

children.text: dūraṃ samāruhya divaḥ patantaṃ bhṛgorivenduṃ vihitopakāram
children.translated_text: As the moon fell, descending from a great height in the sky, like one who had been helped by <s>Bhṛgu</s>,
the host of stars, having gathered their brilliant fame, followed swiftly, their affection fixed.

children.text: kva te kaṭākṣāḥ, kva vilāsavanti proktāni vā tāni mameti matvā
children.translated_text: 'Where are your sidelong glances? Where are those playful words spoken to me?' — thinking thus,
the moon went to set, having climbed, as if to awaken the women of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
Women who had spent the night with faces turned away on their beds out of jealous pride, pretending sleep,
distressed by the passage of the night, reconciled their husbands even when a fault was seen.
Broken by jealousy, firmly rooted, with all auspicious shoots cast off,
watered by showers of tears from the eyes — the love-trees of the beloveds grew again.
Then the world, fearing separation and with passion renewed and unslaked,

children.text: smarasya santaṃ punarukta-bhāvaṃ nā ''vartamānasya viveda lokaḥ.
children.translated_text: did not perceive the redundancy in the existing nature of love that does not return [once gone].

children.text: vṛttau prakāśaṃ hṛdaye kṛtāyāṃ sukhena sarvendriya-saṃbhavena
children.translated_text: When the activity [of love] was manifest in the heart, through the happiness born from all the senses,
the eye, unable to bear contraction, stood deceived in its pride, as if powerless.

children.text: pīne bhaṭasyorasi vīkṣya bhugnāṃs tanu-tvacaḥ pāṇi-ruhān su-madhyā
children.translated_text: The slender-waisted woman, seeing her nails bent on the broad, strong chest of her warrior,

children.text: icchā-vibhaṅgā''kula-mānasatvād bhartre nakhebhyaś ca ciraṃ jujūre.
children.translated_text: being agitated in mind by the curvings of desire, quarreled long with her husband because of her nails.
With limbs gone slack, eyes closed, life discernible only through sweat-drops and horripilation,
all brilliance and sharpness utterly destroyed — the people, tightly embraced by their beloveds, thus became.

children.text: tamaḥ, prasuptaṃ maraṇaṃ, sukhaṃ nu, mūrcchā nu, māyā nu manobhavasya,
children.translated_text: 'Is this darkness? Is it sleep? Is it death? Is it pleasure? Is it fainting? Is it the <s>māyā</s> (illusion) of <s>Manobhava</s> (Love)?

children.text: kiṃ tat kathaṃ vetyupalabdha-saṃjñā vikalpayanto 'pi na saṃpratīyuḥ.
children.translated_text: What is it? How?' — even though having regained consciousness, deliberating, they could not determine.

children.text: vakṣaḥ stanābhyāṃ, sukhamānanena gātrāṇi gātrair ghaṭayanna-mandam
children.translated_text: Pressing chest against breasts, face against face, fitting limbs to limbs unceasingly —

children.text: smarā'turo naiva tutoṣa lokaḥ, paryāptatā premṇi kuto viruddhā.
children.translated_text: the people, afflicted by love, were never satisfied; for how could sufficiency be opposed to love?
With limbs gone limp, being embraced, though being looked at yet with eyes withdrawn,
the newly-wed, being carried to the bed, remained as if her sole essence were the service of another.
The amorous delight of the bride became lovely in its friction when she was suddenly embraced by the bashful lover —
she, though fearful, followed by desire, at the beginning of love, was won over and put at ease by his very boldness.

children.text: sāmonmukhenā ''cchuritā priyeṇa datte 'tha kācit pulakena bhede
children.translated_text: One woman, approached by her lover with face upturned, at first giving resistance through horripilation,
then, the inner anger having subsided, became playful and was conquered by his sheer prowess alone.
Another, assuming heaviness and harshness, though beautiful, when touched by the moon-like hands of her lover,

children.text: prahlāditā candra-śileva tūrṇaṃ kṣobhāt sravat-svedajalā babhūva.
children.translated_text: was delighted like moonstone, and quickly began to exude perspiration from her agitation.
Then the sky, dark and as if senseless with fainting at the departure of the moon-lord,

children.text: tataḥ sakhīva prathitā'nurāgā prābodhayat dyāṃ madhurā'ruṇaśrīḥ
children.translated_text: was awakened by the sweet crimson glory of dawn, like a friend of well-known affection.
Then the people, their thirst for each other unslaked, the end of night having come as if in a mere instant,
left reluctantly from their resting places, as if powerless, full of longing.
Some, half-risen, embraced and again submerged, held back, not wishing to go, once more returning,

children.text: vyājena niryāya punar nivṛttas tyaktā'nya-kāryaḥ sthita eva kaścit.
children.translated_text: though having gone out on some pretext, turned back again, abandoning all other business, and simply stayed.
In the royal palaces, young women sang auspicious songs at dawn, with beauty achieved through rhythmic melody,

children.text: padair gatā'rthaṃ nṛpa-mandireṣu prātar jagur maṅgala-vat taruṇyaḥ.
children.translated_text: with auspicious content, with passion bound to musical notes, with words conveying meaning.

children.text: duruttare paṅka ivā 'ndhakāre magnaṃ jagat santata-raśmi-rajjuḥ
children.translated_text: The world, sunk in impassable darkness as in mud, was as if raised up by the rising sun
with its continuous rays as ropes, the distinctions of forms having been lost.
With lip-rouge drunk away, collyrium removed, faces radiant with disheveled locks —

children.text: prātaḥ kṛtā'rthāni yathā virejus tathā na pūrvedyuralaṃkṛtāni.
children.translated_text: in the morning, having achieved their purpose, they shone thus, not as they had been adorned the evening before.
With eyes reddened from wakefulness, without collyrium, without leaf-designs of <s>alaktaka</s> (lac-dye),
they appeared equal to each other — slender with fatigue, garments displaced — those women who had enjoyed love.
With a slight trace of eye-collyrium still clinging, bearing abundant betel-redness,
even the beautiful lip of the women who had spent the night with their husbands acquired a seeming cheapness.

children.text: cakṣūṃṣi kāntānyapi sā'ñjanāni tāmbūla-raktaṃ ca sa-rāgamoṣṭham
children.translated_text: People made the eyes — beautiful even without collyrium — and the lip — red even without betel —

children.text: kurvan sa-vāsaṃ ca su-gandhi vaktraṃ cakre janaḥ kevala-pakṣa-pātam.
children.translated_text: and the fragrant face — fragrant even without perfume — serve as mere partisanship [for beauty].
The wounds from teeth — received unknowingly during the time of union, noticed in the morning —
the transgressions done to each other, [they bore] without suspicion, through excessive passion, even though separation was far off.
With arrows of eyes fitted with lash-feathers, drawn to the corners of the ears, carrying great tresses as spears,
with breasts and thighs as wheels, with ear-ornaments as bowstrings — the chief warrior-women went about victorious.
Seeing the breasts smeared with sandal-paste and the garments of unwiped cleanliness,

children.text: strīṇāṃ sa-patnyo jahṛṣuḥ prabhāte mandāyamānā'nuśayair manobhiḥ
children.translated_text: the co-wives of the women rejoiced at dawn, their minds having diminished jealous feelings.

children.text: smarā''ture cetasi labdha-janmā rarāja lolo'pi guṇā'pahāryaḥ
children.translated_text: Born in the heart afflicted by love, though fickle, yet irresistible in its qualities,
passion, stationed at the window of the eye, shone out of curiosity, as if gazing at each other's faces.
When love had gone beyond all bounds, employed without forethought, consciousness lost,

children.text: ātmā'nubhūtānapi nopacārān smarā''turaḥ saṃsmarati sma lokaḥ
children.translated_text: the people afflicted by love could not even remember the courtesies they themselves had experienced.
With garments of moderately delightful colors, with unguents distinguished by fragrance,

children.text: āsyaiś ca lokaḥ paritoṣa-kāntai- rasūcayal labdha-padaṃ rahasyam.
children.translated_text: and with faces lovely with satisfaction — the people showed forth the intimacy that had found its place.
In the early morning, with bodies anointed with sandalwood, covering their lower lips with their hands, speaking,

children.text: śāmyan-nimeṣāḥ sutarāṃ yuvānaḥ prakāśayanti sma nigūhanīyam.
children.translated_text: With subsiding blinks, the young men especially revealed what should have been concealed.

children.text: sāmnaiva loke vijite 'pi vāme ! kimudyataṃ bhrū-dhanur-prasahyam,
children.translated_text: "When the world is conquered by gentleness alone, O wayward one! Why is the bow of the eyebrow raised forcefully,

children.text: hantuṃ kṣamo vā vada locaneṣur digdho viṣeṇeva kimañjanena.
children.translated_text: Or tell me, is the arrow of the eye capable of killing, smeared with poison, as it were, with collyrium?"
"On the lip-cover blazing like fire, the stain of betel, equal to a bundle of straw,

children.text: nyastaḥ kimityūcurupeta-bhāvā goṣṭhīṣu nārīs taruṇīr yuvānaḥ.
children.translated_text: Is placed — for what reason?" Thus spoke the enamored young men to the young women in their gatherings.
Easy to enter, endowed with beauty, pure, removing sorrow, spacious,
With lotuses of the faces of awakened women, the homes shone like lakes at dawn.
With floors swept and sprinkled, adorned with beautiful flowers, with shares of fragrant aromatic substances,

children.text: lakṣmīr vijigye bhavanaiḥ sa-bhṛṅgaiḥ sevyasya devairapi nandanasya.
children.translated_text: By these houses, buzzing with bees, the beauty of <s>Nandana</s> (the garden of the gods), served even by the gods, was surpassed.

children.text: akṣṇoḥ patan nīla-saro-ja-lobhād bhṛṅgaḥ kareṇā 'lpa-dhiyā nirastaḥ
children.translated_text: A bee falling upon the eyes out of greed for blue lotuses, pushed away by the hand of one of little intellect,
With intent upon the copper-colored lotus, boldly bit even the palm of the hand, being distressed with contempt.

children.text: vilola-tāṃ cakṣuṣi hasta-vepathuṃ bhruvor vibhaṅgaṃ stana-yugma-valgitam
children.translated_text: The restlessness of the eye, the trembling of the hand, the furrowing of the brows, the heaving of the pair of breasts,

children.text: vibhūṣaṇānāṃ kvaṇitaṃ ca ṣaṭ-pado gurur yathā nṛtya-vidhau samādadhe.
children.translated_text: And the jingling of the ornaments — the six-footed one (the bee), like a teacher, produced [these effects] as in the instruction of dance.

children.text: athā 'nukūlān kula-dharma-saṃpado vidhāya veśān su-divaḥ purī-janaḥ.
children.translated_text: Then, having made the favorable arrangements of family customs and wealth, on an auspicious day, the people of the city,
At the time of waking, with anger toward the enemy abated, proceeded toward the king's palace.

children.text: śailendra-śṛṅgebhya iva pravṛttā vegāj jalaughāḥ pura-mandirebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Like torrents of water rushing from the peaks of the lord of mountains, from the mansions of the city,
Filling the streets like rivers, the floods of people filled the ocean of the king's courtyard.
From the time of waking of the enemy of the lord of the thirty [gods], those withering upward and drying,
Both the small and the great, having attained equality, were seen by the eyes of the men standing at the doors, with contempt.
With heavy thighs, swinging trunks, ears, and tongues, grasped by the tips of the foremost fingers with contempt,
The great elephants, with clusters of bees clinging to their cheeks, whose ornaments had been effortlessly removed, stood as guardians.
With forehooves smeared with the flesh cut from the frontal globes of maddened elephants, mixed with scattered pearls,
Horses were brought in rows, bound together by their tails, and with others as well.

children.text: upekṣitā deva-gaṇais trasadbhir niṣā-carair vīta-bhayair nikṛttāḥ
children.translated_text: Disregarded by the trembling hosts of gods, fearlessly slain by the night-wanderers,
In that place were seen scattered clusters of blossoms with nets from the trees of the gods.
Scorning the foremost <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, contemptuous of all virtues through excessive delusion,
The ten-faced one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), of evil intent, had formerly honored the foremost <s>Brahma-rākṣasa</s>s for the sake of prosperity.
Accompanied by illusionists who terrified people, by trusted ones devoted to acquisition,
By those whose sole delight was the destruction of the good, he surveyed the assembly hall in a region of shaken earth.

children.text: vighṛta-niśita-śastrais tad yutaṃ yātudhānai- ruru-jaṭhara-mukhībhiḥ saṃkulaṃ rākṣasībhiḥ
children.translated_text: Filled with night-wanderers wielding drawn, sharpened weapons, crowded with <s>rākṣasī</s>s having huge bellies and mouths,

children.text: śvagaṇi-śata-vikīrṇaṃ vāgurā-van mṛgībhir vanamiva sa-bhayābhir deva-bandībhirāsīt.
children.translated_text: Strewn with hundreds of packs of jackals, like a forest with nets set for deer, it was [filled] with frightened captive gods.

children.text: jalada iva taḍitvān prājya-ratna-prabhābhiḥ prati-kakubhamudasyan nisvanaṃ dhīra-mandram
children.translated_text: Like a cloud with lightning-flashes of abundant jewel-radiances, rising on each side, with a deep, steady rumble,

children.text: śikharamiva sumerorāsanaṃ haimamuccair vividha-maṇi-vicitraṃ pronnataṃ so 'dhyatiṣthat
children.translated_text: He sat elevated upon a golden throne like a peak of <s>Sumeru</s>, variegated with diverse gems, lofty,

children.text: tato vi-nidraṃ kṛta-devatā'rcaṃ dṛṣṭyaiva citta-praśamaṃ kirantam
children.translated_text: Then his mother addressed <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, who was awake, who had performed worship of the deities, who by his very glance scattered peace of mind,
Who was handsome with the adornment of his limbs displayed, and spoke these words:
"O wise one, you who are the delight of the heaven-dwellers, of your brother who is oppressing the worlds, who is exceedingly proud and arrogant —

children.text: ānandano nāka-sadāṃ praśāntiṃ tūrṇaṃ viṣasyā'mṛta-vat kuruṣva.
children.translated_text: Quickly bring about peace, like <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) to poison.

children.text: kuryās tathā, yena jahāti sītāṃ viṣāda-nīhāra-parīta-mūrtim
children.translated_text: Act so that he releases <s>Sītā</s>, whose form is enveloped in the mist of despair,

children.text: sthitāṃ kṣitau śānta-śikhā-pratānāṃ tārāmiva trāsa-karīṃ janasya.
children.translated_text: Standing on the ground with her flame-crests extinguished, like a star that terrifies people.

children.text: yāvan na saṃtrāsita-deva-saṃghaḥ piṇḍo viṣasyeva hareṇa bhīṣmaḥ
children.translated_text: Before he who has terrified the hosts of gods, like a mass of poison, is fearfully

children.text: saṃgrasyate 'sau puruṣā'dhipena, drutaṃ kulā''nanda ! yatasva tāvat.
children.translated_text: Swallowed by the Lord of Men (<s>Rāma</s>) — quickly strive, O joy of the family!

children.text: hatā janasthāna sado nikāyāḥ, kṛtā jitotkhāta-bhaṭa-drumā pūḥ,
children.translated_text: The assemblies of <s>Janasthāna</s> have been slain, the city has been made like a garden with its warrior-trees uprooted and conquered,

children.text: sadāṃsi dagdhāni, vidheyamasmin yad bandhunā, tad ghaṭayasva tasmin."
children.translated_text: The assemblies have been burned — whatever should be done for a kinsman, accomplish that for him."

children.text: cikīrṣite pūrva-taraṃ sa tasmin, kṣemaṃ-kare 'rthe muhurīryamāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: In that matter he had wished to accomplish earlier, always delaying in this beneficial purpose,

children.text: mātrā 'timātraṃ śubhayaiva buddhyā ciraṃ sudhīrabhyadhikaṃ samādhāt.
children.translated_text: Urged by his mother with an exceedingly auspicious intellect, the deeply wise one deliberated even longer.
With the gate-keeper's rebuffed messenger of <s>Indra</s>, with attendant world-guardians arrived with gifts,
Frightening with fearsome <s>Rākṣasa</s> guards who entered boldly, he went to the door of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s palace.
From a distance, bowed to by the door-keeper, asking for news, having entered unannounced,
Given respectful passage by the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, he beheld the enemy of <s>Indra</s> as though it were a mountain peak,
Mounted high upon a throne of fiery stature, terrible as a cloud of dissolution,
Naturally fierce, sparking from the eyes, like a mass of smoke from the fire at the end of an age,
Even when gazing with affection, bearing fear like the lord of serpents,
Though of a form like a mass of darkness, surpassing all the illustrious ones of renown by his might.
The radiant night-wanderers, who had conquered the world of the dead, approached him who was a giver of jewels,
Like the chief gods approaching a rain-cloud that has released its pearls and gems, seized with thirst.
A seat arranged by attendants skilled in reading gestures, positioned among those previously arrived so as to be close,
Leaning his beautiful arm on the arm of the lion-throne, he sat on the seat, having made his obeisance.
Then the ten-faced one, like a disturbed serpent, with a gem concealed by a brightly ringed finger,
Extending his hand with many gleaming nail-lustre tongues, addressed the assembly:
"With capable allies whose affairs have been well-considered, by those learned in political science who are wise,
By those like yourselves who know the means — well-counseled affairs are accomplished.

children.text: upekṣite vāli-kharā''di-nāśe, dagdhe pure, 'kṣe nihate sa-bhṛtye,
children.translated_text: When the destruction of <s>Vālin</s>, <s>Khara</s> and others has been disregarded, the city burned, <s>Akṣa</s> slain with his retinue,

children.text: sainye dviṣāṃ sāgaramuttitīrṣā- va-nantaraṃ brūta, yadatra yuktam."
children.translated_text: And the army of the foes wishes to cross the ocean — speak without delay what is proper here."

children.text: bhujāṃ'sa-vakṣaḥ-sthala-kārmukā'sīn gadāś ca śūlāni ca yātudhānāḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, touching their arms, shoulders, chests, bows, swords,
Maces, and tridents, renowned for their pride, with <s>Prahasta</s> at their head, addressed the ten-faced one:
"You whose honor is unbreakable, who shattered <s>Indra</s>, who think yourself wise, who wield the supreme rod of punishment,

children.text: narā''bhiyogaṃ nṛ-bhujāṃ pradhāna ! mantronmukhaḥ kiṃ nayase gurutvam.
children.translated_text: O foremost of the strong-armed! Why do you, facing a council, take the matter of a human attack so seriously?

children.text: niryat-sphuliṅgā''kula-dhūma-rāśiṃ kiṃ brūhi bhūmau pinaṣāma bhānum,
children.translated_text: What need to say — shall we crush the sun upon the earth, a mass of smoke packed with flying sparks?
Shall we spit out the moon pressed between our teeth, like the bone of a dry sugarcane stalk?

children.text: sa-rāghavaiḥ kiṃ bata vānarais tair yaiḥ prātarāśo 'pi na kasyacin naḥ
children.translated_text: What indeed of those monkeys together with <s>Rāghava</s>, by whom not even the morning meal of any one of us [would be provided]?
Command us — shall <s>Kailāsa</s> together with <s>Sthāṇu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) be held? Shall heaven be below and the earth in the sky?

children.text: cāpalya-yuktasya hareḥ kṛśānuḥ samedhito vāladhi-bhāk tvadīyaiḥ
children.translated_text: The fire of the fickle monkey, kindled by your people with his tail,

children.text: śastreṇa vadhyasya galannadhākṣīd rājan ! pramādena nijena laṅkām."
children.translated_text: Who was to be slain by weapons, burned <s>Laṅkā</s>, O king! — by your own negligence."
Then, with chest raised and eyes uplifted, making his body inclined as if to speak,
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, with palm turned outward and purpose well-prepared, addressed the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s:

children.text: "yuddhāya rājṇā subhṛtair bhavadbhiḥ saṃbhāvanāyāḥ sadṛśaṃ yaduktam,
children.translated_text: "What has been spoken by you, well-maintained warriors of the king, is befitting your rank,

children.text: tat prāṇa-paṇyair vacanīyameva, prajñā tu mantre 'dhikṛtā, na śauryam.
children.translated_text: And it is indeed to be spoken by those whose lives are at stake; but in counsel, wisdom is sovereign, not valor.
And as for the claim that the human attack deserves gravity from one whose practice of counsel has been neglected,
<s>Hanumān</s> — who subdued <s>Indra</s>, who prevailed in this matter — has destroyed all the city.

children.text: agniḥ pramādena dadāha laṅkāṃ vadhyasya dehe svayamedhitaś cet,
children.translated_text: If fire burned <s>Laṅkā</s> through negligence, being kindled by itself upon the body of one who was to be slain,

children.text: vimṛśya tad deva-dhiyā 'bhidhatta brahmā'stra-bandho'pi yadi pramādaḥ
children.translated_text: Then consider with divine wisdom — if there is negligence even in the binding of the <s>Brahmāstra</s>,
The worlds are inconceivable and capable of wonderful transformations, and people whose pride has been conquered are various;

children.text: kārye tu yatnaṃ kuruta prakṛṣṭaṃ, mā nīti-garbhān su-dhiyo 'vamandhvam.
children.translated_text: Therefore exert supreme effort in the matter at hand — do not despise the wise who are pregnant with statecraft.
One who, desiring victory, carefully observes the course of affairs in their states of growth, decline, and stability,

children.text: ghaṭeta sandhyā''diṣu yo guṇeṣu, lakṣmīr na taṃ muñcati cañcalā 'pi.
children.translated_text: And strives in the qualities of peace and the rest — even fickle <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune) does not abandon him.
The growth of an enemy, whose political wisdom is lost, whose senses are unconquered,
Who is possessed of pride and the rest, is itself the cause of dispassion — which in the end destroys him root and all — and is to be overlooked.
Even one's own decline, accompanied by popular goodwill, bearing good fruit, is to be overlooked by a wise king
Who has accepted peace, having conquered the six-fold group of passions beginning with desire.

children.text: yadā vigṛhṇan na ca saṃdadhāno vṛddhiṃ kṣayaṃ cā 'nuguṇaṃ prapaśyet,
children.translated_text: When neither making war nor making peace, one sees growth and decline as appropriate,

children.text: āsīta rājā 'vasara-pratīkṣas tadā prayāsaṃ vitathaṃ na kuryāt.
children.translated_text: Then the king should remain waiting for the opportune moment and not make futile effort.

children.text: saṃdhau sthito vā janayet sva-vṛddhiṃ hanyāt paraṃ vopaniṣatprayogaiḥ
children.translated_text: Or, while remaining in peace, he should generate his own growth, or strike the enemy through secret stratagems,

children.text: āśrāvayedasya janaṃ parair vā vigrāhya kuryādavahīna-saṃdhim.
children.translated_text: Or cause his people to hear from others, and having split [them], make a peace without loss.
Displaying the quality of affection to his own enemies, sowing discord, he should break their circle;
Having thus and otherwise made arrangements, peace should be the means of approach to growth.
Considering his own people to be patient and not susceptible to the enemy's incitement, and having established fortresses surrounded by water,
Inaccessible with trees, mountains, difficult to cross, impregnable — the king should grow through war with the enemy.

children.text: śaknoti yo na dviṣato nihantuṃ, vihanyate nā 'pya-balair dviṣadbhiḥ,
children.translated_text: One who cannot slay the foe, yet is not destroyed even by weak enemies,

children.text: sa śvā-varāhaṃ kalahaṃ vidadhyā- dāsīta durgā''di vivardhayaṃś ca.
children.translated_text: Should engage in a conflict like that between a dog and a boar, and should remain strengthening his fortifications and the like.

children.text: prayāṇa-mātreṇa pare prasādye varteta yānena kṛtā'bhirakṣaḥ,
children.translated_text: When the enemy is to be pacified by the mere march, one should proceed with a march while maintaining one's own protection;

children.text: a-śaknuvan kartumarer vighātaṃ sva-karma-rakṣāṃ ca paraṃ ṣrayeta.
children.translated_text: Unable to accomplish the destruction of the enemy, one should seek another to protect one's own affairs.

children.text: ekena saṃdhiḥ, kalaho 'pareṇa kāryo 'bhito vā prasamīkṣya vṛddhim,
children.translated_text: Peace with one, war with another — this should be done on both sides, having considered the growth;
Thus should a conqueror who knows statecraft and his own essence employ these policies, knowing them to be beneficial.

children.text: tvayā tu loke janito virāgaḥ, prakopitaṃ maṇḍalamindra-mukhyam,
children.translated_text: But by you, disaffection has been generated in the world; the circle headed by <s>Indra</s> has been provoked;

children.text: rāme tu rājan, viparītametat paśyāmi, tenā 'bhyadhikaṃ vipakṣam.
children.translated_text: With <s>Rāma</s>, however, O king, I see the opposite — therefore the adversary is exceedingly [powerful].

children.text: ekena vālī nihataḥ śareṇa suhṛt-tamas te, racitaś ca rājā
children.translated_text: <s>Vālin</s> was slain by a single arrow — your best ally — and the monkey <s>Sugrīva</s> was made king by the other;

children.text: yadaiva sugrīva-kapiḥ pareṇa, tadaiva kāryaṃ bhavato vinaṣṭam.
children.translated_text: From that very moment, your cause was lost.

children.text: prākāra-mātrā''varaṇaḥ prabhāvaḥ kharā''dibhir yo nihatais tavā'bhūt,
children.translated_text: The power that was yours when <s>Khara</s> and others were slain, which was a mere wall of defense,
Now languishes excessively even from the burning of <s>Laṅkā</s>, the slaying of <s>Akṣa</s>, and the breaking of the trees.
Subject to the six passions, with deluded kinsmen, with allies cut off, attended by the unvirtuous —

children.text: mā pāda-yuddhaṃ dvi-radena kārṣīr nama kṣitīndraṃ praṇatopabhogyam.
children.translated_text: Do not wage a foot-battle with an elephant! Bow to the lord of the earth who is to be enjoyed by those who bow.

children.text: rāmo 'pi dārā''haraṇena tapto, vayaṃ hatair bandhubhirātma-tulyaiḥ,
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> too is tormented by the abduction of his wife; we are tormented by kinsmen slain who were equal to ourselves;

children.text: taptasya taptena yathā ''yaso naḥ saṃdhiḥ pareṇā 'stu, vimuñca sītām.
children.translated_text: Let peace be made between the tormented and the tormented, that our fame may not suffer — release <s>Sītā</s>.
The fiercely burning fire of the king's power, fanned by the savage winds of the circle [of allies],

children.text: sāmā'mbhasā śāntimupaitu rājan ! prasīda, jīvāma sa-bandhu-bhṛtyāḥ.
children.translated_text: Let it be quenched with the waters of conciliation, O king! Be gracious — let us live, kinsmen and servants together.
Like two unfired pots, both subject to breaking, O king, let both go to death as equals;

children.text: vīrye sthitaḥ kiṃtu kṛtā'nurāgo rāmo bhavaṃś cottama-bhūri-vairī.
children.translated_text: But <s>Rāma</s>, established in valor and possessed of affection, and you — are supreme and abundant in enmity.

children.text: daṇḍena kośena ca manyase cet prakṛṣṭamātmānamares tathāpi
children.translated_text: If you think yourself superior to the enemy by means of punishment and treasury, even so,

children.text: riktasya pūrṇena vṛthā vināśaḥ pūrṇasya bhaṅge bahu hīyate tu.
children.translated_text: The destruction of the empty by the full is in vain; in the breaking of the full, much is indeed lost.
One whose servants and self are afflicted, whose wealth must be sought, who is proud and striving in a doubtful matter —

children.text: saṃdehamārohati yaḥ kṛtā'rtho, nūnaṃ ratiṃ tasya karoti na śrīḥ.
children.translated_text: One who mounts doubt when he has already succeeded — surely <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) does not take delight in him."
One should undertake actions that are free from others' faults, bear great fruit, and bring them to completion with devotion —

children.text: karmāṇi rājā vihitā'nurāgo, viparyaye syād vitathaḥ prayāsaḥ.
children.translated_text: A king should be engaged in prescribed duties; in the opposite case, the effort would be in vain.

children.text: jetuṃ na śakyo nṛ-patiḥ su-nītir doṣaḥ kṣayā''diḥ kalahe dhruvaś, ca
children.translated_text: A king of good policy cannot be conquered; in conflict, the fault of destruction and the like is certain,

children.text: phalaṃ na kiṃcin na śubhā samāptiḥ, kṛtā'nurāgaṃ bhūvi saṃtyajā 'rim.
children.translated_text: There is no fruit, nor an auspicious conclusion — abandon the enemy on earth with affection.

children.text: tvan-mitra-nāśo, nija-mitra-lābhaḥ, sameta-sainyaḥ sa ca mitra-kṛcchre
children.translated_text: The destruction of your ally, the gain of his own ally — and he, with assembled armies, when an ally is in distress,

children.text: bhogyo vaśaḥ paśya śareṇa śatroḥ prasādhito vāli-vadhe na ko 'rthaḥ
children.translated_text: Is to be enjoyed as a vassal — behold, the enemy was accomplished by a single arrow in the slaying of Vālin; is there no purpose in that?

children.text: lobhād bhayād vā 'bhigataḥ kapīndro na rāghavaṃ, yena bhaved vibhedyaḥ,
children.translated_text: The lord of monkeys did not approach <s>Rāghava</s> out of greed or fear, whereby he could be divided;

children.text: sthitaḥ satāṃ vartmani labdha-rājyaḥ prati-priyaṃ so 'bhyagamac cikīrṣuḥ.
children.translated_text: Standing on the path of the virtuous, having obtained the kingdom, he came desiring to do a reciprocal favor.
Fruit-eaters, dwelling in waterfall-groves, ignorant of the pleasures of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Love) with divine women,
Of lowly birth, unobtainable even with the finest jewels — even the chief monkeys are not to be suborned.
Consecrated as heir-apparent to the kingdom by King <s>Sugrīva</s>, treated without distinction from his own son,

children.text: tārā-vidheyena kathaṃ vikāraṃ tārā-suto yāsyati rākṣasā'rtham.
children.translated_text: Under the guidance of <s>Tārā</s> — how would <s>Tārā</s>'s son undergo a change of allegiance for the sake of the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s?

children.text: paśyāmi rāmādadhikaṃ samaṃ vā nā 'nyaṃ, virodhe yamupāśrayema,
children.translated_text: I see none other superior or equal to <s>Rāma</s> whom we might take refuge in for opposition;

children.text: dattvā varaṃ sā'nuśayaḥ svayambhū- rindrā''dayaḥ pūrva-taraṃ viruddhāḥ.
children.translated_text: <s>Svayambhū</s> (Brahmā), having given a boon, repented, and <s>Indra</s> and the others were opposed long before.
Even for those sheltered in fortresses, O king, after a long time, the cause of rear-attacks and the like arises;

children.text: durgoparodhaṃ na ca kurvato 'sti śatroś cireṇā 'pi daśā''sya ! hāniḥ
children.translated_text: And for the enemy who does not lay siege to the fortress, there is no loss even after a long time, O Ten-faced One!

children.text: śastraṃ tarūrvī-dharamambu pānaṃ vṛttiḥ phalair, no gaja-vāji-nāryaḥ
children.translated_text: Their weapons are trees, their stronghold is the earth, their drink is water, their livelihood is fruits — they have no elephants, horses, or women;

children.text: rāṣṭraṃ na paścān, na jano'bhirakṣyaḥ, kiṃ duḥsthamācakṣva bhavet pareṣām.
children.translated_text: No kingdom behind them, no people to protect — tell me, what hardship could befall the enemy?
Therefore let there be a treaty of peace with the foe; no other expedient exists upon examination;

children.text: nūnaṃ vi-saṃdhau tvayi sarvametan neṣyanti nāśaṃ kapayo 'cireṇa."
children.translated_text: Surely, if there is no treaty with you, all this the monkeys will bring to destruction before long."

children.text: vibhīṣaṇoktaṃ bahu manyamānaḥ pronnamya dehaṃ pariṇāma-namram
children.translated_text: Greatly esteeming what <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> had said, bowing his body, bent with age,
With loosened wrinkles and head trembling with old age, the maternal grandfather spoke thus to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>:
"A single man on foot, armed with a bow, who alone destroyed fourteen thousand

children.text: rakṣaḥ-sahasrāṇi caturdaśā ''rdīt, kā tatra vo mānuṣa-mātra-śaṅkā.
children.translated_text: <s>Rākṣasa</s>s of many forms of <s>māyā</s> (illusion), sky-going — what doubt have you there about a mere mortal?
Surely, he has been fashioned by the <s>Brahmarṣi</s>s (Brahman-sages) together with the gods for the destruction of the night-wanderers —
In human form, endowed with a monkey army, an invincible stratagem on earth.
Of the <s>Asura</s> whose form was unbroken by the blows of the thunderbolt, great <s>Mahendra</s>

children.text: cakāra bhedaṃ mṛdubhir mahendro yathā, tathaitat kimapīti bodhyam.
children.translated_text: Caused the splitting of his head with the soft foam of waters — just as that happened, so let this too be understood.

children.text: kva strī-viṣahyāḥ karajāḥ, kva vakṣo daityasya śailendra-śilā-viśālam,
children.translated_text: What comparison between fingernails endurable by a woman and the chest of the <s>Daitya</s>, vast as the rocks of the king of mountains?

children.text: saṃpaśyataitad dyusadāṃ sunītaṃ, bibheda tais tan nara-siṃha-mūrtiḥ.
children.translated_text: Behold this good counsel of the celestials — He of the <s>Narasiṃha</s> (Man-Lion) form split it with those very nails.

children.text: pramāda-vāṃs tvaṃ kṣata-dharma-vartmā gato munīnāmapi śatru-bhāvam,
children.translated_text: You are heedless, straying from the path of <s>dharma</s>, and have gone to enmity even with sages;

children.text: kulasya śāntiṃ bahu manyase cet kuruṣva rājendra ! vibhīṣaṇoktam."
children.translated_text: If you value the peace of your lineage, O king of kings, do as <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> has said."
Awakened to consciousness by that sound, with eyes drowsy from sleep, having grasped the essence of the matter,
Like a flashing cloud with rain in the sky, <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> then spoke these words:
"The means undertaken for the commencement of action, the wealth of men and resources together with place and time,
The accomplishment of purpose equipped with remedies against misfortune — these five they declare as the limbs of counsel.

children.text: na niścitā'rthaṃ samayaṃ ca deśaṃ kriyā'bhyupāyā''diṣu yo 'tiyāyāt,
children.translated_text: He who, regarding the means and other aspects of action, would exceed the determined purpose, occasion, and place,

children.text: sa prāpnuyān mantra-phalaṃ na mānī kāle vipanne kṣaṇadā-carendra !
children.translated_text: That proud one shall not obtain the fruit of counsel when the time has passed, O lord of the night-wanderers!

children.text: auṣṇyaṃ tyajen madhya-gato 'pi bhānuḥ, śaityaṃ niśāyāmathavā hi-māṃśuḥ
children.translated_text: The sun, even when in the middle of the sky, might abandon its heat, or the moon its coolness at night;

children.text: anartha-mūlaṃ bhuvanā'vamānī manye na mānaṃ piśitāśi-nātha !
children.translated_text: But pride, which is the root of calamity and the contempt of the world — I think it cannot be abandoned, O lord of the flesh-eaters!

children.text: tathā 'pi vaktuṃ prasabhaṃ yatante yan mad-vidhāḥ siddhimabhīpsavas tvām
children.translated_text: Yet those like me, desiring success for you, strive to speak forcefully;

children.text: viloma-ceṣṭaṃ vihitā'vahāsāḥ parair hi tat sneha-mayais tamobhiḥ
children.translated_text: Those whose contrary actions have been made a laughingstock by others — that is indeed due to the darkness of affection.

children.text: krūrāḥ kriyāḥ, grāmya-sukheṣu saṅgaḥ, puṇyasya yaḥ saṃkṣaya-heturuktaḥ,
children.translated_text: Cruel deeds, attachment to vulgar pleasures — which is declared as the cause of the destruction of merit —
That has been indulged by you excessively; it surely bears unpleasant fruit, O king!

children.text: dattaṃ na kiṃ, ke viṣayā na bhuktāḥ, sthito 'smi vā kaṃ paribhūya noccaiḥ,
children.translated_text: What has not been given? What pleasures have not been enjoyed? Have I not stood on high, having overcome all?

children.text: itthaṃ kṛtā'rthasya mama dhruvaṃ syān mutyus tvadarthe yadi, kiṃ na labdham.
children.translated_text: For me who has thus fulfilled all purposes, if death comes for your sake — what has not been gained?

children.text: kiṃ durnayais tvayyuditair mṛṣā'rthair vīryeṇa vaktā 'smi raṇe samādhim."
children.translated_text: What use are your ill-counsels, uttered in vain? I shall speak through valor the resolution in battle."
When he had fallen asleep again, having spoken thus, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> addressed the lord of the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s:

children.text: "nimitta-śūnyaiḥ sthagitā rajobhir diśo, marudbhir vikṛtair vilolaiḥ
children.translated_text: "The directions are obscured by portentless dust-clouds, by distorted and unstable winds,
By the unnatural cries of beasts and birds — they seem to cry out as if their lord were stricken.

children.text: utpāta-jaṃ chidramasau vivasvān vyādāya vaktrā''kṛti loka-bhīṣmam
children.translated_text: The sun rises with this calamity-born defect, opening its mouth in a form terrifying to the world,

children.text: attuṃ janān dhūsara-raśmi-rāśiḥ siṃho yathā kīrṇa-saṭo 'bhyudeti.
children.translated_text: With its mass of dusty rays, as if to devour the people — like a lion with mane spread wide.
The clan-elder of the <s>Bhṛgu</s>s (<s>Śukra</s>) has gone to the path occupied by <s>Agastya</s> at the <s>Vindhya</s> peak,

children.text: saṃdṛśyate śakra-purohito 'hni, kṣmāṃ kampayantyo nipatanti colkāḥ
children.translated_text: The priest of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Bṛhaspati</s>) is seen by day, and meteors fall, causing the earth to tremble.

children.text: māṃsaṃ hatānāmiva rākṣasānā- māśaṃsavaḥ krūra-giro ruvantaḥ
children.translated_text: As if anticipating the flesh of slain <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, crying with cruel voices,

children.text: kravyā'śino dīpta-kṛśānu-vaktrā bhrāmyantya-bhītāḥ paritaḥ puraṃ naḥ
children.translated_text: Flesh-eating creatures with fire-blazing mouths roam fearlessly around our city.

children.text: payo ghaṭodhnīrapi gā duhanti mandaṃ vi-varṇaṃ vi-rasaṃ ca gopāḥ,
children.translated_text: The cowherds milk from udder-heavy cows only scant, discolored, and tasteless milk;

children.text: havyeṣu kīṭopajanaḥ sa-keśo na dīpyate 'gniḥ su-samindhano 'pi.
children.translated_text: Worms appear in the oblations, mixed with hair, and the fire does not blaze even when well-kindled.

children.text: tasmāt kuru tvaṃ pratikāramasmin snehān mayā rāvaṇa ! bhāṣyamāṇaḥ,
children.translated_text: Therefore act with a remedy in this matter, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, I speak to you out of affection;

children.text: vadanti duḥkhaṃ hyanujīvi-vṛtte sthitāḥ padasthaṃ pariṇāma-pathyam.
children.translated_text: Those who stand in the way of servants' welfare speak what is salutary in its outcome, though painful now.
Before the enemy satisfies the jackals with corpse-remains, with those who are broken, scattered, fallen, split,

children.text: yāvan narā'śair na ripuḥ śava'śān saṃtarpayatyānama tāvadasmai."
children.translated_text: Crushed, dragged, and cut by sharp weapons — bow to him while there is still time."
Knitting his brow, abandoning composure, with frightful and fierce eyes,

children.text: giraṃ jagādogra-padāmudagraḥ svaṃ sphāvayan śakra-ripuḥ prabhāvam.
children.translated_text: The lofty enemy of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) spoke a word of harsh syllables, displaying his own might:

children.text: "śilā tariṣyatyudake na parṇaṃ, dhvāntaṃ raveḥ syantsyati, vahnirindoḥ,
children.translated_text: "A stone will float on water and not a leaf; darkness will issue from the sun, fire from the moon —

children.text: jetā paro 'haṃ yudhi jeṣyamāṇas tulyāni manyasva pulastya-naptaḥ !
children.translated_text: My foe shall conquer, and I shall be conquered in battle — consider these as equal impossibilities, O grandson of <s>Pulastya</s>!
One who is discontented amid prosperity, harboring hidden enmity, who shows envy even when honored,

children.text: vibhinna-karmā''śaya-vāk kule no mā jñāti-celaṃ, bhuvi kasyacid bhūt
children.translated_text: Whose deeds, intentions, and speech are discordant — may such a kinsman-traitor never exist in any family on earth!

children.text: icchantyabhīkṣṇaṃ kṣayamātmano 'pi na jñātayas tulya-kulasya lakṣmīm
children.translated_text: Kinsmen constantly desire the destruction even of themselves rather than the prosperity of one of equal lineage;

children.text: namanti śatrūn, na ca bandhu-vṛddhiṃ saṃtapyamānair hṛdayaiḥ sahante.
children.translated_text: They bow to enemies, yet cannot endure a kinsman's growth, their hearts burning with torment.
By you today, with excessive delight at the prospect of <s>Laṅkā</s>'s subjugation, your inner soul has been excessively exposed as wicked;

children.text: dhik tvāṃ, mṛṣā te mayi dustha-buddhir" vadannidaṃ tasya dadau sa pārṣṇim.
children.translated_text: Fie upon you! False is your ill-disposed mind toward me" — saying this, he gave him a kick.

children.text: tataḥ sa kopaṃ kṣamayā nigrhṇan, dhairyeṇa manyuṃ, vinayena garvam,
children.translated_text: Then he, restraining anger with patience, fury with fortitude, pride with humility,
Delusion through the force of wisdom and courage, and weakness likewise — rose up together with his four ministers.

children.text: uvāca cainaṃ kṣaṇadā-carendraṃ "sukhaṃ mahā-rāja ! vinā mayā ''ssva.
children.translated_text: And he said to the lord of the night-wanderers: "Be well, O great king, without me!

children.text: mūrkhā''turaḥ pathya-kaṭūnanaśnan yat sā''mayo''sau, bhiṣajāṃ na doṣaḥ
