children.translated_text: A sick fool who does not take the bitter but wholesome medicine — that his disease worsens is not the fault of the physicians.
One who makes enmity when being plainly advised, yet is pleased by ear-pleasing but unwholesome words —
A master devoid of discernment, self-conceited — alas, this one is a great calamity for his friends.

children.text: krīḍan bhujaṅgena gṛhā'nupātaṃ kaścid yathā jīvati saṃśaya-sthaḥ,
children.translated_text: Just as one who plays with a serpent that has entered his house lives in a state of doubt,

children.text: saṃsevamāno nṛ-patiṃ pra-mūḍhaṃ tathaiva yaj jīvati, so 'sya lābhaḥ.
children.translated_text: So too, one who serves a deluded king — that he lives at all is his gain.

children.text: dattaḥ sva-doṣair bhavatā prahāraḥ pādena dharmye pathi me sthitasya,
children.translated_text: The blow given by you with your foot to me who stands on the righteous path was caused by your own faults;

children.text: sa cintanīyaḥ saha mantri-mukhyaiḥ kasyā ''vayor lāghavamādadhātu.
children.translated_text: Let it be pondered together with your chief counselors — upon whose honor does it confer lightness?
Thus, that one, addressing the lord of the night-wanderers with many virtuous words, forcefully and repeatedly,
Departed fearlessly from the city of the enemy of men, to bow at the feet of the king, the subduer of foes.
Then, having approached — his virtuous character known — by the words of the Son of the Wind, he whose heart was firm as a mountain,
The king gladdened him with his retinue rejoicing, with water-offerings befitting the lord of a city.
In the charming breeze, with the splendor of the rays of the deer-marked moon,
The night, bound with longing for <s>Rāma</s>, departed at the edge of the shore.
The fierce ocean, attached to the companionship of the day, was stirred by <s>Rāma</s> in the salt-water abode;
Suddenly the passionate fury, equal to the far-risen orb of the sun, rose in the surging waves.
In the great arrow born of the enemy, with smoke and water, and the pain of deeply-set heavy shafts,

children.text: āruḍhā saṃdehaṃ rāme sa-mahī-dhāra mahī sa-phaṇi-sabhā.
children.translated_text: The earth with its mountain-bearers, together with the serpent-assembly, rose to doubt about <s>Rāma</s>.
The salt-water abode, dense with terrible aquatic elephants, great mud, tumultuous, with resounding waters,
The salt-water, churned up, with terrible serpent-lords pierced by the blazing fruit-arrows,
Fearfully avoiding the assemblage of waters brilliant with the movement of great serpents,
The salt-water rose to the shore, its caves agitated by the arrival of the monkey army,
With deer-herds among the swaying trees, the abode of <s>Rāma</s> adorned with garlands of many flowers,
With nets of monkey-leaf trees, with tall, blazing, excellent trees giving cool shade,
The excellent elephant of the ocean, with its mass of water, blocking the circle of the mountain-earth,
Worthy of the earth, its earthen current diminished by contact with tall waves.

children.text: praṇipatya tato vacanaṃ jagāda hitamāyato patir vārīṇām
children.translated_text: Having bowed, the lord of the waters then spoke beneficial and extensive words
To <s>Rāma</s>, who stood in the shade of thick, great monkey-<s>tamāla</s> trees, his arms reaching to the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
"The mountains are lofty with great peaks, the water impassable, the wind steals the essence,

children.text: a-himo ravi-kiraṇa-gaṇo, māyā saṃsāra-kāraṇaṃ te paramā.
children.translated_text: The sun's rays are without cold, and <s>māyā</s> (illusion) is the supreme cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> — such is your nature.
O <s>Aruṇa</s> (the Dawn), born of exertion! Withdraw your arrow that bears the shadow equal to the destroyer <s>Hima-hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>);
Meet with the assembled waters, the ancient, beautiful-bodied abode.
The water-bed, difficult for monkeys to traverse, of deep extent, obstructed by dense mud —
Tell me, is the waterless path easy to cross, terrifying with sea-creatures, conches, and aquatic elephants?
To go to the shore of <s>Laṅkā</s> easily through a passage built over the great waters,
Let the deer-monkeys carry mountains and tree-nets, bearing the heavy body sustained by mountain-loads.
Let <s>Rāma</s>'s arrows, blocked by <s>Hara</s>'s laughter in their course, sever the throats of the enemy host in the commencement of great battle,

children.text: chindantu rāma-bāṇā gambhīre me jale mahā-giri-baddhe.
children.translated_text: Cutting through my deep waters bound by great mountains.
Let the beautiful-smiling ones, heroic in sentiment, whose bond of fear has been broken,
Go suddenly to slay the many-armed, strong <s>Rākṣasa</s> elephants of great mountain-like bodies.

children.text: jigamiṣayā saṃyuktā bahūva kapi-vāhinī mate dāśaratheḥ
children.translated_text: The monkey army, united with the desire to advance, grew in the purpose of <s>Dāśarathi</s> (<s>Rāma</s>),
With minds set upon the ocean, eagerly engaged in the task of carrying mountains.
<s>Rāma</s>'s army, capable of carrying huge, excellent mountains, tawny as the foe-destroying fire,
Rose suddenly into the sky, deep as the clear waters of <s>Varuṇa</s>'s abode,
Immersed in mountain-ranges, with the movement of the gods blocked by tall, great walls,
Fearsome with the roar of fearless monkeys, with beautiful, dense cave-waters fragrant with elephant-musk,
With flowers swaying with swarms of bees, with flocks of joyful <s>kurara</s> birds and <s>kāraṇḍava</s> ducks on lotus-waters,
With terrible caves infested with serpents, with pieces of juicy earth uprooted by elephant tusks —
With water made golden by lotus pollen, charming with the sounds of cranes, clear, abundant, and beautiful,
With abundant incense of divine trees formed from the meeting of the sun-gem-born [heat] and the snow-destroyer [fire],
With deep and resonant sounds produced by elephants excited by the cries of <s>Hari</s> (monkeys),
With great boars of mighty thighs and abundant strength, muddied at the confluence of snouts.

children.text: uccakhnuḥ parirabdhān kapi-saṅghā bāhubhis tato bhūmi-bhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the monkey hosts uprooted mountains with their arms, embracing them,
Their remaining peaks crushed, their summits scattering the sun's rays and the constellations.
Bearing great lofty mountains, with shattering picks grasped in their arms, in many ways,
Desiring to dam the salt water, they ascended into the sky of great circumference,
With many white clouds, having the appearance of a great sword of pure iron,
Bound with garlands of birds, like the snow-mountain bound with the cries of excited <s>kurara</s> birds,
With sounds produced by beautiful swans in abundance and fierce-moving cranes,
Bearing the fragrance of flower-pollen, with a pure expanse from the contact of seasonal waters.
Suddenly those [monkeys], bearing mountains along with trees and deer, at the commencement of damming the salt water,
Ascended the mountains on the shore, blocking the fearful movement of the enemy at <s>Rāma</s>'s approach.

children.text: tataḥ prāṇītāḥ kapi-yūtha-mukhyair nyastāḥ kṛśānos tanayena samyak
children.translated_text: Then, led by the chiefs of the monkey troops, properly placed by the son of <s>Kṛśānu</s> (Fire),
With their front slopes and flanks unshakeable, the mountains were plunged into the great ocean.

children.text: tene 'dri-bandhyo, vavṛdhe payodhis, tutoṣa rāmo, mumude kapīndraḥ,
children.translated_text: The bridge of mountains was built, the ocean swelled, <s>Rāma</s> was pleased, the monkey-lord rejoiced,

children.text: tatrāsa śatrur, dadṛśe suvelaḥ, prāpe jalānto, juhṛṣuḥ plavaṅgāḥ.
children.translated_text: The enemy trembled, <s>Suvela</s> was seen, the water's end was reached, the monkeys exulted.

body.translated_text: [This is] with alternating narration, and faultless.

children.text: bhremur, vavalgur, nanṛtur, jajakṣur, juguḥ, samutpupluvire, niṣeduḥ,
children.translated_text: They wandered, they leaped, they danced, they laughed, they sang, they jumped up high, they sat down,
They clapped their hands, they roared aloud, they shone, they rejoiced, they dispersed, they gathered.
With a body beautiful from mountain-mud, with fragrance sweetened by <s>kakkola</s> and cloves,
With many dense and great waves — the salt water rose up at its banks.
Swelling at the approach to the shore, vast in circumference with pure and lofty waves bound in the sky,
Able to bear the weight of the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the salt water was dammed by the excellent bridge of mountains.
And <s>Suvela</s> was ascended, with its network of excellent mountains charming with garlands of trees,
<s>Rāma</s>'s army, terrifying to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s heart, with tawny, waving manes,
With deep and great thickets and caverns filled with the tumultuous sound of <s>Laṅkā</s>'s dwellings,
With great <s>tamāla</s> tree shade filled with hosts of gods at the confluence of <s>vīṇā</s> music's delight,
With dense shade formed by <s>hintāla</s> palms with abundant and beautiful sprouts and filaments,
With the excitement of elephants bound by the fragrant wind carrying the scent of <s>Airāvaṇa</s>'s ichor,
With a network of soft, beautiful, waving tender shoots growing on lofty tree-shade,
With pomegranate groves of wavering beauty, resembling a blazing forest with flowers terrifying to deer,
With the melodious cries of sweet-throated birds, with great <s>sāla</s> trees crowded at the great water-dam,
Bound with trembling sprouts, bearing a net of jewels made of water-drops,
With a network of rays from lofty gems, with deep sounds produced by the clash of mountain waters,
With assemblies in beautiful cave-openings, equal to the city of the gods, with the sweet sounds of immortals and <s>Cāraṇa</s>s,
With pure great gem-studded [walls], with walls made tawny by marks of vermilion,
With nocturnal wanderings blocked by the fear of encounters with heroic lions and elephants,
With fearsome serpent-holes, with terrible and tumultuous sounds of abundant birds,
With great <s>sāla</s> forests crowded with excellent elephants, boars, lions, herds of cattle, and spotted deer,
With graceful trembling sprouts, with earth made golden by the pollen of beautiful ground-lotuses,
With flower-filament arrows of <s>Kāma</s> (Love), with beautiful smiles of young clove-tree creepers,
With pure gem and gold settings, with the passage of <s>ruru</s> deer blocked by lofty great walls,
With gods ascending its slopes — like <s>Meru</s> with its abundant and beautiful <s>Mandāra</s> trees,
With excellent trees heavy with fruit, with beautiful flowers growing not far off, pressing close,
With deep caves filled with abundant waters born from moon-marked gems.
With a body of beautiful white caverns filled with golden streams and water-loving elephants,
With <s>ruru</s> deer licking the flickering rays of beautiful gems, their hue like that of sprouts and parrots,
Able to withstand fierce winds, with the clash of lofty rain-clouds of terrible sound,
With the play of snow-bearing mountain-peaks bound by garlands of white clouds.
The salt-water dam being delightful, with bodily fatigue relieved by the abundance of tree-fruits,
<s>Rāma</s>'s army ascended to the gate-guardians of <s>Laṅkā</s>, eager for battle.
With the terrible sounds of heavy drums, flutes, humming strings, kettledrums, and fearsome <s>jhallarī</s> drums,
Tumultuous with <s>ḍhakkā</s> drums and bells, the enemy army was arrayed, able to endure the toil of battle,
Fierce with arrows raised, with stout bodies covered by nets of pure iron,
With beautiful girth produced by the clash of restless horses and elephants,
With swords, lances, spears, great <s>paṭṭiśa</s> axes, excellent javelins, heavy arrows, and massive clubs,
Adorned with the <s>vīra rasa</s> (heroic sentiment), with the earth trembling from the heavy movement of horses and elephants,

children.text: te rāmeṇa sa-rabhasaṃ paritaralā hari-gaṇā raṇa-samārambhe
children.translated_text: Those monkey hosts, impetuous and eager, were marshaled by <s>Rāma</s> at the commencement of battle,
Restrained at the environs of <s>Laṅkā</s>, eager to shatter the surrounding mountains, with steady roar.
A couplet: dwelling in the openings of thickets on mountain walls, crags, and lofty trees on the water's shore,
The fearsome army of monkeys and deer, restless under the well-kindled rays of the sun.
To observe <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s army — having the color of rain-clouds heavy with water —
It had ascended upon watchtowers, tree-platforms, pavilions, archway-garlands, and assembly halls.
Then the ten-faced one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), his mind bewildered by passion, his enemy's strength revealed by spies,
Having deluded [them] with an illusory head of <s>Rāma</s>, dispatched <s>Sītā</s>'s army to fight.
Then they blew conch shells, kettledrums were struck with drumsticks,
Flutes were filled, humming strings buzzed when struck by hand,
<s>Ḍhakkā</s> drums were made to sound, <s>paṇava</s> drums resounded when beaten,

children.text: kāhalāḥ pūrayāṃcakruḥ, pūrṇāḥ peraś ca sasvanuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kāhalā</s> trumpets were made to fill [the air], and <s>pera</s> drums, when filled, resounded.

children.text: mṛdaṅgā dhīramāsvenur, hatair svene ca gomukhaiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛdaṅga</s> drums sounded steadily, and <s>gomukha</s> horns sounded when struck,

children.text: ghaṇṭāḥ śiśiñjire dīrghaṃ, jahrāde paṭahair bhṛśam.
children.translated_text: Bells jingled long, and it thundered greatly with kettledrums.

children.text: hayā jiheṣire harṣād, gambhīraṃ jagajur gajāḥ,
children.translated_text: Horses neighed with excitement, elephants trumpeted deeply,
Frightened young camels bellowed, foot-soldier ranks shouted,
Terrified horses snorted, bulls bellowed exceedingly,

children.text: nāryaś cukṣubhire mamlur mumuhuḥ śuśucuḥ patīn.
children.translated_text: Women were agitated, grew faint, were bewildered, and grieved for their husbands.

children.text: jagarjur, jahṛṣuḥ, śurā rejus tuṣṭuvire paraiḥ,
children.translated_text: Warriors roared, rejoiced, shone, and were praised by others,
They tied on finger-guards, anointed [themselves], and marched forth.
They strung their bows, mounted chariots and the rest,
Drew forth gleaming swords, and raised heavy maces,
They whirled tridents, took up auspicious arrows,

children.text: bhremuś, cukurdire, resur vavalguś ca padātayaḥ
children.translated_text: They roamed, brandished, bellowed, and the foot-soldiers leaped.
They were urged forward by whip-blows, and were restrained by reins —

children.text: aśvāḥ, pradudruvur mokṣe raktaṃ nijagaruḥ śrame.
children.translated_text: The horses; they galloped when released, and sank down with fatigue.
They gave armor to the elephants, spread blankets over them,
They fastened girths, and raised banners with high crests.
They sought to reassure and embraced their women,

children.text: ājaghnur mūrdhni bālāṃś ca cucumbuś ca suta-priyāḥ.
children.translated_text: They struck their children on the head and kissed them, dear to their sons.
The elephants, uninjured and understanding deep [signals], received commands,

children.text: vavṛdhe śuśubhe caiṣāṃ mado, hṛṣṭaiś ca pupluve.
children.translated_text: Their ichor increased and gleamed, and it flowed from the excited ones.

children.text: mṛgāḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ sasruḥ, śivāḥ samyag vavāśire,
children.translated_text: Deer ran to the right, jackals howled auspiciously,
Their bodies throbbed on the right side, and their mental dispositions were serene.
<s>Prahasta</s> desired to lead the vanguard by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s command.
<s>Mahāpārśva</s> and <s>Mahodara</s> rushed to the southern gate.
<s>Indrajit</s> went westward; he himself (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) went to the northern [gate].
<s>Virūpākṣa</s> desired to occupy together the eastern [gate].

children.text: śuśrāva rāmas tat sarvaṃ, pratasthe ca sa-sainikaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> heard all that, and set forth with his army,
He strung his weapon and then fastened his quiver.
Then he surveyed <s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>), recognized the [enemy] forces,
Paid homage to the gods, and released his bed of leaves.
The monkeys shone brightly, stood up, roared, and seized the directions,

children.text: vānarā, bhūdharān, redhur, babhañjuś, ca tatas tarūn.
children.translated_text: They uprooted mountains, broke them, and then [uprooted] trees.

children.text: dadāla bhūr, nabho raktaṃ goṣpadapraṃ vavarṣa ca,
children.translated_text: The earth split, the sky became red, and it rained as if [from] a cow's hoof-print,
Deer ran to the left, and birds uttered inauspicious [cries].

children.text: ulkā dadṛśire dīptā, ruruvuś cā'śivaṃ śivāḥ,
children.translated_text: Blazing meteors were seen, and jackals howled inauspiciously,

children.text: cakṣmāye ca mahī, rāmaḥ śaśaṅke cā'śubhā'gamam.
children.translated_text: The earth trembled, and <s>Rāma</s> apprehended the approach of evil.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, having heard that the enemies had approached the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s,
Himself desired to fight, having seated himself at the top of the rampart.
The <s>Rākṣasa</s>s discharged arrows, hurled tridents and <s>paṭṭiśa</s> axes,

children.text: asīṃś ca vāhayāṃcakruḥ pāśaiś cā''cakṛṣus tataiḥ
children.translated_text: And wielded swords, and dragged with outstretched snares,

children.text: bhallaiś ca bibhidus tīkṣṇair vividhus tomarais tathā.
children.translated_text: And split with sharp crescent-headed arrows, and pierced with lances likewise.

children.text: gadābhiś cūrṇayāṃcakruḥ, śitaiś cakraiś ca cicchiduḥ.
children.translated_text: They crushed with maces, and cut with sharp discuses.

children.text: vānarā muṣṭibhir jaghnur dadaṃśur daśanais tathā,
children.translated_text: The monkeys struck with fists and bit with teeth likewise,

children.text: nirāsuś ca girīṃs tuṅgān, drumān vicakarus tathā.
children.translated_text: And hurled lofty mountains, and uprooted trees likewise.

children.text: lāṅgūlair loṭhayāṃcakrus, talair, ninyuś ca saṃkṣayam,
children.translated_text: They battered with tails, with palms, and brought to destruction,

children.text: nakhaiś cakṛtatuḥ, kruddhāḥ pipiṣuś ca kṣitau balāt.
children.translated_text: They scratched with nails, and enraged, crushed [them] on the ground by force.
Headless trunks arose, rivers of blood flowed,
Warriors floated [on them] like lotus-faces, and with banners it appeared like foam,

children.text: rakta-paṅke gajāḥ sedur, na pracakramire rathāḥ,
children.translated_text: Elephants sank in the mire of blood, chariots could not advance,

children.text: nimamajjus turaṅgāś ca, gantuṃ notsehire bhaṭāḥ.
children.translated_text: Horses were submerged, and warriors were unable to proceed.
Each gate of the city was besieged by a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) of enemies,
And thirty-six <s>koṭi</s>s of monkeys surrounded the monkey-king,

children.text: tastanur, jahvalur, mamlur, jaglur, luluṭhire kṣatāḥ,
children.translated_text: They stretched out, trembled, grew faint, swallowed, rolled on the ground wounded,

children.text: mumūrcchur, vavamū raktaṃ, tatṛṣuś cobhaye bhaṭāḥ
children.translated_text: Fainted, vomited blood, and thirsted — warriors on both sides.
<s>Sampātin</s> fought with <s>Prajaṅgha</s> — he, struck by a tree,

children.text: cakampe, tīva cukrośa, jīvanāśaṃ nanāśa ca.
children.translated_text: Trembled, cried out violently, and met his death, dying.
When he was uprooted by <s>Nala</s>, his eyes quivered with flashing heat;

children.text: jambumālī jahau prāṇān grāvṇā mārutinā hataḥ.
children.translated_text: <s>Jambumālī</s> gave up his life, struck by a rock by the son of <s>Māruta</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>).
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> crushed <s>Mitrighna</s>'s body with a mace.

children.text: sugrīvaḥ praghasaṃ nebhe, bahūn rāmas tatarda ca.
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> struck down <s>Praghasa</s>, and <s>Rāma</s> pierced many.
The head of <s>Vajramuṣṭi</s>, struck by <s>Mainda</s>, was severed,

children.text: nīlaś cakarta cakreṇa nikumbhasya śiraḥ sphurat.
children.translated_text: <s>Nīla</s> cut off the quivering head of <s>Nikumbha</s> with a discus.
<s>Virūpākṣa</s> gave up his life, pierced by <s>Saumitri</s>'s (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s) arrows,
<s>Dvivida</s> caused the thunderbolt-like one (<s>Aśaniprabha</s>) to release his life-breaths.

children.text: gadā śatru-jitā jighye, tāṃ pratīyeṣa vāli-jaḥ
children.translated_text: The mace of <s>Śatrujit</s> was broken; the son of <s>Vālin</s> (<s>Aṅgada</s>) sought it [in return],
Then <s>Aṅgada</s> crushed his chariot along with its horses with a tree-branch.

children.text: tat karma vāli-putrasya dṛṣṭvā viśvaṃ visiṣmiye,
children.translated_text: Seeing that deed of <s>Vālin</s>'s son, the whole world was astonished,

children.text: saṃtresū rākṣasāḥ sarve, bahu mene ca rāghavaḥ.
children.translated_text: All the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s trembled, and <s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) esteemed [him] highly.
<s>Sugrīva</s> rejoiced, the gods said "Well done!" with wonder,
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> praised [him], and the monkeys applauded.

children.text: hī citraṃ lakṣmaṇenode, rāvaṇiś ca tirodadhe
children.translated_text: "Ah, wonderful!" exclaimed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>; and the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> (<s>Indrajit</s>) vanished.

children.text: vicakāra tato rāmaḥ śarān, saṃtatrasur dviṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> discharged arrows, and the enemies trembled,

children.text: vibhinnā jughurur ghoraṃ, jakṣuḥ kravyā'śino hatān,
children.translated_text: The shattered [foes] shrieked terribly, flesh-eating [creatures] devoured the slain,

children.text: cuṣcyota vraṇināṃ raktaṃ, chinnāś celuḥ kṣaṇaṃ bhujāḥ
children.translated_text: Blood dripped from the wounded, and severed arms moved for a moment.
Even when the heads of heroes were severed, his fierce anger did not abate;
The rest took flight, and those who had thought themselves brave felt ashamed.

children.text: rāghavo na dayāṃcakre, dadhur dhairyaṃ na kecana,
children.translated_text: Rāghava showed no mercy; none maintained their courage;

children.text: mamre pataṅgavad vīrair hāheti ca vicukruśe.
children.translated_text: Heroes perished like moths, and cried out "Alas! Alas!"
The sun was obscured, and night took possession of the field;

children.text: jagrase kāla-rātrīva vānarān rākṣasāmś ca sā.
children.translated_text: Like the night of universal dissolution, it swallowed both monkeys and <s>Rākṣasas</s>.
<s>Indrajit</s> raged furiously and invoked the <s>Sarpāstra</s> (serpent-weapon);
Having become invisible, he invoked it against the enemy army, and laughed.

children.text: babādhe ca balaṃ kṛtsnaṃ, nijagrāha ca sāyakaiḥ
children.translated_text: He assailed the entire army and restrained them with his arrows;

children.text: utsasarja śarāṃs, te'sya sarpa-sāc ca prapedire.
children.translated_text: He released his shafts, and they reached the serpent-state upon him.

children.text: ācicāya sa taiḥ senāmācikāya ca rāghavau,
children.translated_text: He overwhelmed the army with those, and targeted the two <s>Rāghava</s>s;

children.text: babhāṇa ca, "na me māyāṃ jigāyendro'pi, kiṃ nṛbhiḥ".
children.translated_text: And he declared: "Not even <s>Indra</s> has conquered my <s>māyā</s> (illusion) — what then of mere humans?"

children.text: ācikyāte ca bhūyo 'pi rāghavau tena pannagaiḥ
children.translated_text: And the two <s>Rāghava</s>s were further bound by his serpents;
Those two became unconscious and agitated, and fell upon the earth.
Then they cried out "<s>Rāma</s>!" trembled, and lamented;

children.text: niśaśvasuś ca senānyaḥ, procur dhigiti cā''tmanaḥ.
children.translated_text: The army commanders sighed deeply and exclaimed "Shame!" upon themselves.

children.text: manyuṃ śekur na te roddhuṃ, nā 'sraṃ saṃrurudhuḥ patat,
children.translated_text: They could not restrain their anguish, nor hold back their falling tears;
They could not find <s>Indrajit</s>'s path, and the monkeys wandered about.
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> then washed <s>Sugrīva</s>'s eyes with water,

children.text: vidāṃcakāra dhautā'kṣaḥ sa ripuṃ khe, nanarda ca.
children.translated_text: And with cleansed eyes, he spotted the enemy in the sky and roared.
Then a monkey lifted a mountain to slay <s>Indrajit</s>;
The son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, abandoning that place, went near his father.

children.text: ācacakṣe ca vṛttāntaṃ, prajaharṣa ca rāvanaḥ
children.translated_text: He reported the events, and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> rejoiced greatly,
Embraced him tightly, and kissed him upon the head.

children.text: dhvajānuddudhuvus tuṅgān, māṃsaṃ cemur, jaguḥ, papuḥ,
children.translated_text: They waved their lofty banners, ate meat, sang, drank,
Made love to their beloveds — the night-stalkers were then content.

children.text: darśayāṃcakrire rāmaṃ sītāṃ rājñaś ca śāsanāt,
children.translated_text: By the king's command, they showed <s>Sītā</s> the fallen <s>Rāma</s>;
Her eyes closed, and she rolled about in the belly of the <s>Puṣpaka</s> (aerial chariot).

children.text: prāṇā dadhvaṃsire, gātraṃ tastambhe ca priye hate,
children.translated_text: Her life-breaths were shattered, her body became rigid when her beloved was seen slain;

children.text: ucchaśvāsa cirād dīnā, rurodā 'sau rarāsa ca.
children.translated_text: She sighed deeply after a long time, wretched, and wept and wailed.
"Was my heart bound with iron fetters? Was it fashioned with a thunderbolt?

children.text: mano me, na vinā rāmād yat pusphoṭa sahasra-dhā.
children.translated_text: That it did not burst into a thousand pieces without <s>Rāma</s>!
You crossed the ocean for my sake, you sought to destroy the enemies,
And you endured me, most terrible — shame on a life made worthless!

children.text: na jijīvā 'sukhī tātaḥ prāṇatā rahitas tvayā,
children.translated_text: My unhappy father did not wish to live, deprived of breath by separation from you;
Even with you dead, what use is there for me, a worthless wife, continuing to live?"

children.text: sā jugupsān pracakre 'sūn, jagarhe lakṣaṇāni ca
children.translated_text: She felt revulsion toward her own life-breaths, and reproached the signs

children.text: dehabhāñji, tataḥ keśān luluñca, luluṭhe muhuḥ.
children.translated_text: Of her body; then she tore her hair and rolled about repeatedly.

children.text: jaglau, dadhyau, vitastāna, kṣaṇaṃ prāṇa na, vivyathe,
children.translated_text: She was exhausted, she brooded, she was bewildered, she could not breathe for a moment, she trembled,

children.text: daivaṃ nininda, cakranda, dehe cā 'tīva manyunā.
children.translated_text: She cursed fate, she wailed, and in her body [she felt] exceeding anguish.
Then <s>Trijaṭā</s> consoled her and led her away.
Then the monkeys with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> kept vigil;

children.text: ciceta rāgas tat kṛcchramoṣāṃcakre śucā 'tha saḥ,
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> regained consciousness from that affliction, and he grieved with sorrow;

children.text: manyuś cā 'sya samāpipye, virurāva ca lakṣmaṇam.
children.translated_text: His anger swelled, and he called out loudly to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
He resolved to die and honored the entire army with his words;

children.text: āpapṛcche ca sugrīvaṃ svaṃ deśaṃ visasarja ca.
children.translated_text: He bade farewell to <s>Sugrīva</s> and dismissed him to his own land.
He commanded <s>Aṅgada</s> to lead the two <s>Rāghava</s>s to <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>,

children.text: pratijajñe svayaṃ caiva sugrīvo rakṣasā vadham.
children.translated_text: And <s>Sugrīva</s> himself vowed to slay the <s>Rākṣasa</s>.
"This is the <s>Nāgāstra</s> (serpent-weapon) of that one; its antidote is the invocation of <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>)" —
Having heard this from <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, the best of the <s>Raghu</s>s meditated upon him.
Then the mountains shook, the ocean surged beyond its shores,

children.text: vṛkṣebhyaś cucyute puṣpair, virejur bhāsurā diśaḥ
children.translated_text: Flowers fell from the trees, and the directions shone brightly;
The <s>Nāgas</s> (serpents) plunged into the ocean, a delightful breeze blew,
The radiances subsided, and the serpent-bonds were loosened.

children.text: bhrejire 'kṣata-vad yodhā, lebhe saṃjñāṃ ca lakṣmaṇaḥ,
children.translated_text: The warriors shone as if unwounded, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> regained consciousness;
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> too shone brightly, and <s>Garutmān</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) arrived nearby.
He touched the two sons of <s>Kākutstha</s>; those two, freed from pain, recognized him;
He revealed himself to them, and then departed the way he had come.
They perspired, they shone, they rose, they split mountains and trees;
The monkeys then ran about and longed eagerly for battle.

children.text: ḍuḍhaukire punar laṅkāṃ, bubudhe tān daśānanaḥ
children.translated_text: They rushed again toward <s>Laṅkā</s>; the ten-faced one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) perceived them,

children.text: jīvataś ca vivedā 'rīn, babhraṃśe 'sau dhṛtes tataḥ.
children.translated_text: And learned that the enemies were alive; he then lost his composure.
He inferred that they had been freed from the divine serpent-bonds,

children.text: babhājā 'tha paraṃ mohamūhāṃcakre jayaṃ na ca.
children.translated_text: And thereupon experienced supreme delusion, and did not expect victory.
Then <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, approved by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, prepared to set forth;

children.text: siṃhā''syair yuyuje tasya vṛkā''syaiś ca rathaḥ khagaiḥ.
children.translated_text: His chariot was yoked with birds having lion-faces and wolf-faces.
They covered their bodies with leather armor, mounted their vehicles,
Strung weapons upon their human-like arms, and advanced toward the battlefield.

children.text: adhyuvāsa rathaṃ, teye purāc, cukṣāva cā 'śubham,
children.translated_text: He mounted his chariot, they issued forth from the city, and inauspicious signs arose;
<s>Dhūmrākṣa</s> proclaimed his fame and hastened likewise.

children.text: nililye mūrdhni gṛdhro'sya, krūrā dhvāṅkṣā vivāśire,
children.translated_text: A vulture settled on his head, fierce crows cawed,

children.text: śiśīke śoṇitaṃ vyoma, cacāla kṣmā-talaṃ tathā.
children.translated_text: Blood rained from the sky, and the surface of the earth trembled.
Then battle was joined; weapons were exchanged between the two sides;
They cut, they reeled, they clung together, and they roared.
Monkeys and <s>Rākṣasas</s> broke, shone, foamed in many ways;
Heroes showed no fear, but terrified their enemies.
The crushed ones shed blood; those wounded by arrows swelled;
Arms with thumbs and fists discharged arrows at the shooters.
<s>Dhūmrākṣa</s> sported in battle; the son of <s>Vāyu</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>) threatened him,

children.text: ādade ca śilāṃ, sā'śvaṃ pipeṣā 'sya rathaṃ tayā.
children.translated_text: And seized a rock, and with it crushed his chariot along with its horses.

children.text: papāta rākṣaso bhūmau, rarāṭa ca bhayaṃkaram,
children.translated_text: The <s>Rākṣasa</s> fell to the ground and roared terrifyingly,

children.text: tutoda gadayā cā'riṃ, taṃ dudhrāvā 'driṇā kapiḥ.
children.translated_text: And struck the enemy with his mace; the monkey rushed at him with a boulder.
<s>Akampana</s> then desired to fight by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s command;
He rushed forward in his chariot and roared most terrifyingly.

children.text: paspande tasya vāmā'kṣi, sasyamuś cā'śivāḥ khagāḥ,
children.translated_text: His left eye throbbed, and inauspicious birds cried out;

children.text: tān vavrājā 'vamatyā 'sau, babhāse ca raṇe śaraiḥ.
children.translated_text: He disregarded those with contempt, and blazed in battle with his arrows.
His arrows, stretched like ropes, flew skyward and earthward;
The armies were not ashamed by him; no one yielded to him.

children.text: sa bhasma-sāc cakārā'rīn, dudāva ca kṛtānta-vat,
children.translated_text: He reduced his enemies to ashes and burned like the god of Death;

children.text: cukrodha mārutis, tāla- muccakhne ca mahā-śikham.
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Māruta</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>) became enraged, and uprooted a great-crested palm tree.
With that, he offered <s>Akampana</s> as a great sacrificial victim to <s>Yama</s> (Death);
When he was slain, grief blazed in <s>Rāvaṇa</s> like fire.

children.text: sa bibhreṣa, pracukṣoda, dantairoṣṭhaṃ cakhāda ca,
children.translated_text: He was frightened, he gnashed his teeth, he bit his lip with his teeth;
He quickly arranged for the protection of the city all around with great effort.
He summoned <s>Prahasta</s>, of wondrous valor, to fight.
"What need is there for deliberation, O king of kings! We are here for battle!" — thus he
Spoke fearlessly, and the great chariot-warrior resolved to fight.
His warriors set forth, and his horses and elephants were readied.
They yoked the chariots with horses; the priests propitiated the gods;
They duly honored the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and recited blessings.

children.text: ūhire mūrdhni siddhārthā, gāvaś cā ''lebhire bhaṭaiḥ,
children.translated_text: They bore mustard seeds upon their heads, and the warriors received cows;
They consecrated their great weapons, and tested their horses.

children.text: laluḥ khaḍgān, mamārjuś ca, mamṛjuś ca paraśvadhān
children.translated_text: They licked their swords and polished them, and sharpened their battle-axes.
He adorned himself, anointed himself, dressed, ate, drank,

children.text: jahase ca kṣaṇaṃ, yānair nirjagme yoddhṛbhis tataḥ
children.translated_text: And laughed for a moment; then he sallied forth in vehicles with his warriors.

children.text: viprān prahasta ānarca, juhāva ca vibhāvasum.
children.translated_text: <s>Prahasta</s> honored the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and made an oblation to the fire.
He assembled his counselors and anointed himself with sandalwood paste;

children.text: cacāma madhu mārdvīkaṃ, tvak-traṃ cā''cakace varam.
children.translated_text: He tasted honey and grape-wine, and adorned himself with a fine leather garment.

children.text: uṣṇīṣaṃ mumuce cāru, rathaṃ, ca jujuṣe śubham,
children.translated_text: He fastened a beautiful turban, and took delight in his splendid chariot;
He grasped his great weapons, and then set out to march.
They struck all kinds of musical instruments, and his attendants sang his praises;

children.text: rajaḥ pravavṛdhe ghoraṃ, ghoṣaś ca vyānaśe diśaḥ.
children.translated_text: Terrible dust arose, and the din pervaded the directions.

children.text: taṃ yāntaṃ dudruvur gṛdhrāḥ, kravyādaś ca siṣevire
children.translated_text: As he marched, vultures followed him, and flesh-eating creatures attended him;

children.text: āvavur vāyavo ghorāḥ, khādulkāś ca pracakṣaruḥ.
children.translated_text: Terrible winds blew, and blazing meteors appeared in the sky.
Blood rained from the sky, the implements of war blazed;
Chariots with their horses stumbled, and the horses and elephants would not move.
The goads slipped, and sacrificial animals veered to the left;

children.text: dadāla bhūḥ, pupūre dyauḥ, kapīnāmapi niḥsvanaiḥ
children.translated_text: The earth split, the sky was filled also with the cries of the monkeys.

children.text: mimeha raktaṃ hastyaśvaṃ, rākṣasāś ca nitiṣṭhivuḥ,
children.translated_text: The horses and elephants urinated blood, and the <s>Rākṣasas</s> spat repeatedly.

children.text: tataḥ śuśubhatuḥ sene, nir-dayaṃ ca prajahratuḥ
children.translated_text: Then the two armies shone, and fought without mercy;

children.text: didviśur, dudyuvuś, cacchuś, caklamuḥ, suṣupur, hatāḥ
children.translated_text: They hated, they attacked, they cut, they grew weary, they fell asleep, slain.

children.text: cakhādire cakhāduś ca, vilepuś ca raṇe bhaṭāḥ
children.translated_text: Warriors in battle bit, chewed, and smeared [themselves with blood].
The monkeys slew and harassed <s>Prahasta</s>'s chief ministers;

children.text: vānarāḥ, karma senānī rakṣasāṃ cakṣame ne tat.
children.translated_text: The general of the <s>Rākṣasas</s> could not endure that deed.
He covered the monkey army with a flood of weapons,

children.text: śaśāsa ca bahūn, yodhān, jīvitena viveca ca,
children.translated_text: And commanded many warriors, and separated them from their lives;

children.text: āsasañja bhayaṃ teṣāṃ, didyute ca yathā raviḥ,
children.translated_text: He instilled fear in them, and shone like the sun;

children.text: nā''yayāsa, dviṣad-dehair jagāhe ca diśo daśa.
children.translated_text: He did not tire, and with the bodies of his foes he filled the ten directions.
Some cowered in fear, others collapsed in defeat;
Some fled from the battle, and others begged for mercy.

children.text: evaṃ vijigye tāṃ senāṃ prahasto, 'tidadarpa ca,
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Prahasta</s> conquered that army and was exceedingly proud;

children.text: śaśāma na ca saṃkruddho, nirjugopa niśācarān.
children.translated_text: His fury did not abate, and he protected the night-stalkers.

children.text: cukrudhe tatra nīlena, taruś coccikṣipe mahān,
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nīla</s> became enraged there, and hurled a great tree;
<s>Prahasta</s>, struck by it, released many arrows.

children.text: sehe kapī, rathā'śvāṃś ca ripos tatarha śākhinā,
children.translated_text: The monkey endured them, and smashed the enemy's chariot and horses with a branch;

children.text: dharitrīṃ musalī teye prahastaś, cikhide na ca,
children.translated_text: The mace-bearing <s>Prahasta</s> descended to the ground, but was not cut down.
The anger of those two flared up, and the lightness of their weapons was displayed;

children.text: nunoda śākhinaṃ nīla, āvavre musalī tarum,
children.translated_text: <s>Nīla</s> hurled a branch, and the mace-bearer warded off the tree;
They soared in the sky, and on the ground they traced circles;
The two heroes charged at each other, and did not grow weary.
Then the monkey hurled a rock at the <s>Rākṣasa</s>;
Wounded by it, he died and sank upon the surface of the earth.

children.text: tutuṣur vānarāḥ sarve, neśuś citrā niśā-carāḥ,
children.translated_text: All the monkeys rejoiced; the night-stalkers perished in various ways;

children.text: jerurāśā daśāsyasya, sainyaṃ nīlaṃ nunāva ca,
children.translated_text: The hopes of the ten-faced one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) decayed, and the army praised <s>Nīla</s>.

children.text: yadā na pheluḥ kṣaṇadā-carāṇāṃ manorathā rāma-balā'bhiyoge,
children.translated_text: When the desires of the night-stalkers did not bear fruit in the assault on <s>Rāma</s>'s forces,

children.text: laṅkāṃ tadā bhejurudīrṇa-dainyā, vyācakhyuruccaiś ca hataṃ prahastam,
children.translated_text: Then, with their spirits crushed, they retreated to <s>Laṅkā</s>, and loudly reported the death of <s>Prahasta</s>.
The lord of the <s>Rākṣasas</s> then feared, and surveyed the city all around;
He dispatched <s>Rākṣasas</s> to awaken <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.

children.text: te 'bhyagur bhavanaṃ tasya, suptaṃ caikṣiṣatā 'tha tam,
children.translated_text: They entered his palace and beheld him sleeping;

children.text: vyāhārṣus tumulān śabdān, daṇḍaiś cā 'vadhiṣur drutam
children.translated_text: They uttered tumultuous sounds and quickly struck him with staves.
They pulled his hair, and drove elephants over his limbs;
They sprinkled him with cold water and even burned him with firebrands.
They scratched him with sharp nails and bit him with teeth likewise;

children.text: śitairatautsuḥ śūlaiś ca, bherīś cā'vīvadan śubhāḥ.
children.translated_text: They prodded him with sharp tridents, and sounded auspicious drums.

children.text: sa tān nā 'jīgaṇat sarvā- nicchayā 'buddha ca svayam,
children.translated_text: He disregarded them all, and did not awaken of his own accord;

children.text: abūbudhata kasmān mā- maprākṣīc ca niśā-carān.
children.translated_text: He awoke and asked "Why are you waking me?" and questioned the night-stalkers.
They said: "The king wishes to see you, O night-stalker!"
He bathed, anointed himself, ate meat, and drank wine;

children.text: nyavasiṣṭa tato draṣṭuṃ rāvaṇaṃ, prāvṛtat gṛhāt.
children.translated_text: He then prepared to see <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and departed from his dwelling.
The king beheld him approaching and rose slightly from his seat;
He was pleased, and pointed out a golden seat nearby.
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> smiled slightly and sat down close by.

children.text: avādīn "māṃ kimityāhvo" rājñā ca pratyavādi saḥ
children.translated_text: He said: "Why have you summoned me?" And the king replied:

children.text: "mājñāsīs tvaṃ sukhī, rāmo yadakārṣīt sa rakṣasām.
children.translated_text: "May you not have known peace, for what <s>Rāma</s> has done to the <s>Rākṣasas</s>:
He crossed the ocean, besieged our city all around,
Blazed in battle with weapons, and brought the <s>Rākṣasas</s> to destruction.
I did not speak anything agreeable, as long as I lived;

children.text: bandhus tvamarcitaḥ snehān mādviṣo na vadhīr mama
children.translated_text: You are a kinsman, honored out of affection — do not slay my enemies,

children.text: vīryaṃ mā na dadarśas tvaṃ, mā na trāsthāḥ kṣatāṃ puram,
children.translated_text: May you not have overlooked my valor, may you not have feared the ruined city;

children.text: tavā 'drākṣma vayaṃ vīryaṃ, tvamajaiṣīḥ purā surān"
children.translated_text: We have seen your valor — you conquered the gods before."
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> said to him: "What we stated in the counsel —

children.text: na tvaṃ sarvaṃ tadaśrauṣīḥ, phalaṃ tasyedamāgamat.
children.translated_text: You did not hear all of that; this fruit of that has now arrived.
You despised the words of the wise, you relied on the words of fools,

children.text: adhyagīṣṭhāś ca śāstrāṇi, pratyapatthā hitaṃ na ca
children.translated_text: You studied the scriptures, yet you did not accept what was beneficial.
Fools deceived you — those who made war;

children.text: abhāṇīn mālyavān yuktamakṣaṃsthās tvaṃ na tan madāt
children.translated_text: <s>Mālyavān</s> spoke what was fitting — you did not heed that, out of pride.
You stole the wife of <s>Rāghava</s> — told by trusted ones, you did not return her;

children.text: mā nā'nubhūḥ svakān doṣān, mā muho mā ruṣo'dhunā.
children.translated_text: May you not have failed to experience your own faults — do not be deluded, do not be angry now.
The time for that too has passed — what I said then;
The <s>Rākṣasī</s> host was harmed by enemies, you spent the treasuries,

children.text: sandhāna-kāraṇaṃ tejo nyagabhūt te, kṛthās tathā,
children.translated_text: Your power, the ground for peace-making, has diminished; you have acted so

children.text: yat tvaṃ vairāṇi kośaṃ ca saha-daṇḍamajiglapaḥ."
children.translated_text: That you have exhausted enmities, treasury, and army together."
<s>Daśānana</s> (the ten-faced one) grew angry and spoke these words to <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>:
"Why do you reproach me? Display your own prowess!

children.text: mojjigrahaḥ su-nītāni, mā sma kraṃsthā na saṃyuge,
children.translated_text: Do not abandon good conduct — do not refuse to fight in battle;

children.text: mopālabdhāh kṛtair doṣair mā na vākṣīr hitaṃ param."
children.translated_text: Do not reproach me with faults already done — do not fail to speak what is supremely beneficial."
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> then roared and rallied the other warriors.

children.text: upāyaṃsta mahā'strāṇi, niragāc ca drutaṃ puraḥ.
children.translated_text: He took up great weapons and went forth swiftly from the city.
With his head he seemed to scratch the sky, he filled space with his vast body,
With his feet he seemed to crush the earth, with his gaze he seemed to burn his enemies.
He appeared like a scorched mountain, he strode like a cloud of dissolution,
The ocean trembled, and even the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s were terrified.
He was immovable like a winged mountain, he breathed like the wind at the end of an age,
He terrified the worlds with his roar, he blazed like the fire of destruction.
The earth sank under his weight, trees toppled by his momentum,
Lions fled in terror, the principal mountains were shaken.
Portents appeared around him — the sky rained blood,
Terrible winds blew, and cruel birds shrieked.

children.text: aspandiṣṭā 'kṣi vāmaṃ ca, ghorāś cā 'rāṭiṣuḥ śivāḥ,
children.translated_text: His left eye throbbed, and dreadful jackals howled,
Vultures descended upon his mace, and a blazing meteor fell.
With his stride, deeming the battlefield worthy of contempt, from pride,
Then he bellowed and rejoiced, and challenged his enemies to battle.

children.text: prāśīn, na cā 'tṛpat krūraḥ, kṣuc cā'syā'vṛdhadaśnataḥ,
children.translated_text: He ate but was not sated, the cruel one; and his hunger grew even as he ate;
He consumed the flesh and drank the blood of the forest-dwellers.
His belly was not satisfied by flesh, and his stomach did not swell;

children.text: bahūnāmaglucat prāṇā- naglocīc ca raṇe yaśaḥ.
children.translated_text: He swallowed the lives of many and also swallowed glory in battle.

children.text: sāmarthyaṃ cā 'pi so 'stambhīd vikramaṃ cā'sya nā 'stabhan,
children.translated_text: His might he indeed displayed, yet they could not restrain his valor;
Some monkeys climbed trees, others sought to dive into the ocean.
Others leapt onto mountains, others hid in caves,
Some sat motionless in stupor, some reeled with fear.
Other monkeys crossed the ocean by the bridge;
<s>Aṅgada</s> was ashamed there and resisted valiantly.
He milked courage from the monkeys and fought;
Then, wishing to hurl mountains, he uprooted trees.
The tiger-like monkeys roared and fought properly in battle;
He crushed them and devoured them, and struck them down with slaps of his palms,
And ground them to powder with his feet, and frightened them quickly,
And <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> pierced the monkeys with his trident.
He struck hard with his mace and crushed them in his embrace,
He trampled others with his knees and rolled them in his grasp.
Rocks shattered against his body, great trees were pulverized;

children.text: kṣiptās tasya na cā 'cetīt tānasau, nā 'pi cā 'kṣubhat.
children.translated_text: Those hurled at him — he did not feel them, nor was he disturbed.

children.text: adrāṣṭāṃ taṃ raghu-vyāghrau ākhyac cainaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The two tigers of the <s>Raghu</s> line saw him, and <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> described him:
"This one conquered the lord of the gods (<s>Indra</s>), he did not fear the sun-god (<s>Vivasvat</s>).
He shattered the power of the lord of <s>Yakṣa</s>s — no one could withstand him.

children.text: kumbhakarṇān na bhaiṣṭaṃ mā yuvāmasmān nṛpā''tmajau.
children.translated_text: Do not fear <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> — you two are sons of a king, [protect] us.

children.text: ghnantaṃ mopekṣiṣāthāṃ ca, mā na kārṣṭamihā''daram.,
children.translated_text: Do not overlook him while he slaughters; do not fail to exert effort here."

children.text: "amuṃ mā na vadhiṣṭe"ti rāmo'vādīt tataḥ kapīn.
children.translated_text: "Do not fail to slay this one" — <s>Rāma</s> then said to the monkeys.
They roared, challenged, and also leapt upon the <s>Rākṣasa</s>,
They displayed their own powers and hurled trees and boulders.

children.text: te taṃ vyāśiṣatā 'kṣautsuḥ pādair, dantais tathā 'cchidan.
children.translated_text: They surrounded him and struck him with feet, and likewise bit with teeth.

children.text: ārjijat śarabho vṛkṣaṃ, nīlas tvā ''dita parvatam.
children.translated_text: <s>Śarabha</s> hurled a tree; <s>Nīla</s> in turn brought a mountain.
<s>Ṛṣabha</s> wished to hurl rocks — they harassed him with those.
He roared, and <s>Gandhamādana</s> hurled a mountain peak,

children.text: akūrdiṣṭa, vyakārīc ca gavākṣo bhū-dharān bahūn.
children.translated_text: <s>Gavākṣa</s> leapt and scattered many mountain-holders.

children.text: sa tān nā'jīgaṇad vīraḥ kumbhakarṇo'vyathiṣṭa na.
children.translated_text: <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, the hero, disregarded them all and was not distressed.
He churned the enemy army and scorched without restraint,
He hastened to slay his foes and devoured those who came within reach.
The monkey army shrieked and fled as he approached;
He seized them with both hands by the throats and [thrust them] into his terrible mouth.
He made the earth slippery with blood, and with the scattered troops,

children.text: nā 'tārpsīd bhakṣayan krūro, nā 'śramad ghnan plavaṅgamān,
children.translated_text: The cruel one was not satisfied even while eating, nor did he tire of slaying the monkeys.
Some could not fight, some could not advance;

children.text: prāṇaśan nāsikābhyāṃ ca, vaktreṇa ca vanaukasaḥ.
children.translated_text: The forest-dwellers lost their life-breaths through their nostrils and mouths.
Others were digested in his belly, resembling the netherworld;
They screamed, called their companions, fled, and perspired.
The crushed monkeys dripped blood, and the wounded thirsted;
He was attended as a king by the broken ones — he challenged <s>Sugrīva</s>.
<s>Sugrīva</s> too grew angry at the enemy and uprooted a great tree to fight.
The enemy overpowered him as he arrived and took up a fearsome spear.
He brandished that terrible [weapon] and hurled it at the lord of monkeys.

children.text: prāpaptan mārutis tatra tāṃ cā 'lāsīd viyad-gatām.
children.translated_text: <s>Māruti</s> (Hanumān) arrived there and struck it aside while it was airborne.

children.text: aśobhiṣṭā'cakhaṇḍac ca śaktiṃ vīro, na cā 'yasat.
children.translated_text: The hero shone brilliantly and broke the spear without effort.
"The spear fashioned for me from a thousand loads of iron" —
The <s>Rākṣasa</s> was distressed; he then dug up a massive mountain
And hurled it at the lord of monkeys — by that he was wounded and fainted.
<s>Sugrīva</s> rolled on the ground, and blood also flowed;
He (<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>) seized him and ran off, and the <s>Rākṣasa</s> exulted.
The monkeys were terrified; the son of the Wind (<s>Hanumān</s>) obstructed <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>;
<s>Sugrīva</s> gradually regained consciousness and tore off the nose and ears
Of the <s>Rākṣasa</s>, and was not afraid, and succeeded in escaping.
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> became enraged and began to crush [monkeys] on the ground.
<s>Sugrīva</s> slipped from his hand and plunged into the sky;
He swiftly pursued <s>Rāma</s> and delighted the monkeys.

children.text: atatvarac ca tān yoddhumaciceṣṭac ca rāghavau.
children.translated_text: He hastened to fight them and challenged the two <s>Rāghava</s>s.
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> turned back, and the monkeys fought in battle.
At the king's command they surrounded and swiftly climbed upon the <s>Rākṣasa</s>;
He chased those who had climbed upon him, and they too, panicked, dropped off.
He seized, he ran, and he embraced mercilessly;

children.text: te cā 'pyaghoriṣur ghoraṃ, raktaṃ cā 'vamiṣur mukhaiḥ.
children.translated_text: And they too roared terribly and vomited blood from their mouths.

children.text: sa cā'pi rudhirair mattaḥ sveṣāmapyadayiṣṭa na,
children.translated_text: And he too, intoxicated by blood, showed no mercy even to his own;
He seized the lives of others and obstructed their valor.
The courage of the terrified forest-dwellers was stripped away;
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> cut off his crown and armor.

children.text: abhedi ca śarair dehaḥ prāśaṃsīt taṃ niśā-caraḥ.
children.translated_text: His body was pierced by arrows; the night-wanderer praised him [<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>].
He challenged <s>Rāma</s> to combat; <s>Rāma</s> then shot arrows at him —

children.text: yairaghāni kharo, vālī, mārīco, dūṣaṇas tathā.
children.translated_text: Those by which <s>Khara</s>, <s>Vālin</s>, <s>Mārīca</s>, and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> were slain.

children.text: avāmaṃsta sa tān darpāt, prodayaṃsīc ca mudgaram.
children.translated_text: He despised those from pride and raised his mace.
<s>Rāma</s> cut off that hand along with the weapon using the <s>Vāyavya</s> (wind) missile,
He, with a tree in hand, blazing, charged toward the enemy.
The king cut off his arm together with the tree by the missile of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra),
And shattered his legs with arrows, and struck his face with shafts.

children.text: aindreṇa hṛdaye 'vyātsīt, so 'dhyavātsīc ca gāṃ hataḥ.
children.translated_text: With the <s>Aindra</s> (Indra's) weapon he pierced his heart, and struck down, he fell to the earth.
Two thousand forest-dwellers were crushed by his falling body.

children.text: astāviṣuḥ surā rāmaṃ, diśaḥ prāpan niśā-carāḥ,
children.translated_text: The gods praised <s>Rāma</s>; the night-wanderers fled in all directions;
The earth with its great mountains trembled, the lord of waters shook.
The <s>Rākṣasa</s>s heard that their king <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> was slain;
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> wept and grieved, and fell into the deepest delusion.
He proclaimed the virtues of his brother and extolled his valor:
"Those enemies who were seen by <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> when enraged —

children.text: kathaṃ nvajīviṣus te ca, sa cā 'mṛta mahā-balaḥ."
children.translated_text: How did they survive, while he, of great strength, has died?"
Then, the princes, desiring to fight, consoled <s>Rāvaṇa</s> —
<s>Devāntaka</s>, <s>Atikāya</s>, <s>Triśiras</s>, and <s>Narāntaka</s>.
Those mighty sons of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> strode into battle.

children.text: yuddhonmattaṃ ca mattaṃ ca rājā rakṣārthamāñjihat
children.translated_text: The king dispatched <s>Yuddhonmatta</s> and <s>Matta</s> for the protection
Of his sons; those two <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, skilled in battle, went forth.
By them the armies were defeated, the enemies were thrown into confusion;
They felled the foremost monkeys to the ground like mountains.
<s>Narāntaka</s> engaged to fight with <s>Aṅgada</s>;
The <s>Rākṣasa</s> hurled a lance, and <s>Aṅgada</s> struck his chest.
The son of <s>Vālin</s> slew his horses and struck him with his fist.

children.text: rāvaṇiś cā 'vyatho yoddhumārabdha ca mahīṃ gataḥ.
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, unwounded, began to fight, having fallen to the ground.
His life was taken by the fist of <s>Vālin</s>'s son.
Then all the sons of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, enraged, rushed toward <s>Aṅgada</s>.
Then <s>Nīla</s> and <s>Hanumān</s> surrounded the sons of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>;
They hurled lofty mountains; <s>Triśiras</s> cut them with arrows.
Then <s>Devāntaka</s>, the mighty, struck with his iron bar in battle;
The son of <s>Māruta</s> (Hanumān) split his skull with his fist.

children.text: adīdipat tato vīryaṃ, nīlaṃ cā'pīpiḍac charaiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Yuddhonmatta</s> then blazed with valor and afflicted <s>Nīla</s> with arrows,
But <s>Nīla</s> brought him to destruction with a mountain.
Then <s>Triśiras</s> hurled a spear at the son of the Wind (<s>Hanumān</s>);
<s>Hanumān</s>, wounded, bore the pain of his horses in battle.

children.text: asrasac cā''hato mūrdhni, khaḍgaṃ cā 'jīharad dviṣā,
children.translated_text: Struck on the head, he (<s>Triśiras</s>) staggered, and his sword was seized by the enemy;

children.text: prāṇānaujjhīc ca khaḍgena chinnais tenaiva mūrdhabhiḥ.
children.translated_text: His life was taken by the sword, his heads severed by that very [blade].
<s>Matta</s>, having arrived, fought with <s>Śarabha</s> using a great mace;
<s>Atikāya</s> then sported in battle, slaying a thousand monkeys.
He tormented the enemies with his chariot and roamed without restraint;
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> identified that great chariot-warrior to <s>Rāghava</s>:
"This one withstood <s>Indra</s>'s thunderbolt and pleased <s>Svayambhū</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>),
He trained in great weapons, and he protected the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s in battle.
He mastered the <s>Arthaśāstra</s>s, he challenged the valor of <s>Yama</s> (Death),
He blazed in battles with gods — no fear was born in him.
This son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> has arrived, terrifying to the monkeys."

children.text: āhvatā 'tha sa kākutsthaṃ dhanuś cā 'pusphurad guru.
children.translated_text: Then he challenged <s>Kākutstha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) and twanged his heavy bow.
<s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>), like a serpent, crushed that one in the great battle.
The two spun to conquer, [releasing] volleys of arrows in abundance.

children.text: acchaittāṃ ca mahā''tmānau, ciramaśramatāṃ na ca,
children.translated_text: And the great-souled ones cut [each other's arrows]; for long neither grew weary,
And they stood shooting arrows, filling [the sky] with darkness as it were.
The <s>Rākṣasa</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> employed the <s>Saurya</s> (solar) and <s>Āgneya</s> (fire) missiles,
And those, meeting each other, came to destruction.
Then the <s>Rākṣasa</s> wielded the <s>Aiṣīka</s> (reed) weapon in battle;
That too was destroyed upon encountering the <s>Māhendra</s> (Indra's) missile launched by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Then <s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>) was angered and discharged [a weapon] at the unconquerable one.
The <s>Brahmāstra</s> (weapon of Brahmā) — with that he shattered the head of the enemy of men.
Then Ten-necked (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) cried out; <s>Indrajit</s> consoled him,

children.text: nirayāsīc ca saṃkruddhaḥ, prārcicac ca svayambhuvam.
children.translated_text: And went forth enraged, and worshipped <s>Svayambhū</s> (Brahmā).
He offered oblations into the fire, and consecrated his circle of weapons;

children.text: so 'labdha brahmaṇaḥ śastraṃ syandanaṃ ca jayā''vaham.
children.translated_text: He obtained from <s>Brahmā</s> a weapon and a victory-bearing chariot.
The son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> mounted that [chariot] with blazing tips and rejoiced;
Then, with concealed form, he cut the bodies of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s enemies.
He slew sixty-seven <s>koṭi</s>s (tens of millions) of monkeys with his arrows.

children.text: niśā'nte rāvaṇiḥ kruddho rāghavau ca vyamūmuhat.
children.translated_text: At nightfall, the enraged son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> bewildered the two <s>Rāghava</s>s.
He displayed his own power, covered the directions with arrows,

children.text: aghorīc ca mahā-ghoraṃ, gatvā, praiṣīc ca rāvaṇam.
children.translated_text: And roared a great and terrible roar, and having gone, sent word to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> then recognized the still-breathing <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>;
Taking a torch, he tended to the surviving monkeys.
"Do not grieve, O tigers of the <s>Raghu</s> line! Do not be angry," — saying thus,
He roused <s>Nīla</s> and the other fallen monkey-chiefs.
There <s>Jāmbavān</s> breathed, and opened his eyes,
And said to the descendant of <s>Pulastya</s> (<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>): "Has the son of <s>Māruta</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>) survived?"
"In his safety, O great king, we all shall not perish entirely."
The descendant of <s>Pulastya</s> then informed him that the son of the Wind (<s>Hanumān</s>) was alive.

children.text: āyiṣṭa mārutis tatra, tau cā 'pyahṛṣatāṃ tataḥ,
children.translated_text: <s>Māruti</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>) arrived there, and those two (<s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>) also rejoiced;
They then dispatched <s>Hanumān</s> to the ridge of the <s>Himālaya</s>,
To the mountain of all herbs, to bring the herb that revives the dead,
And another that heals wounds, and likewise one that extracts arrow-points.

children.text: prodapāti nabhas tena, sa ca prāpi mahā-giriḥ,
children.translated_text: He leapt into the sky with that [purpose], and that great mountain was reached;
On which, at night, thousands of great herbs blazed.
When <s>Hanumān</s> could not distinguish the individual herbs,

children.text: sarva eva samāhāri tadā śailaḥ mahauṣadhiḥ.
children.translated_text: He then carried the entire great mountain of herbs.

children.text: prāṇiṣur nihatāḥ kecit, kecit tu prodamīliṣuḥ
children.translated_text: Some of the slain revived, some opened their eyes;
Other warriors dispelled their darkness, and still others yawned.
Some smelled the herbs, others applied them likewise;
Thus all of them recovered, and gained even greater strength.

children.text: ajihladat sa kākutsthau, śeṣāṃś cā 'jījivat kapīn
children.translated_text: He (<s>Hanumān</s>) gladdened the two sons of <s>Kākutstha</s>, and revived the remaining monkeys;
Then <s>Hanumān</s> set <s>Laṅkā</s> ablaze with fire swiftly.
He then assembled the army and polished the <s>bhalla</s> and <s>tomara</s> weapons,
And sharpened the sword-leaves and the like, and made the battle-axes gleam.
The two mighty sons of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> there, fully armed —

children.text: nikumbhaś caiva kumbhaś ca, prāpatāṃ tau plavaṅgamān.
children.translated_text: <s>Nikumbha</s> and <s>Kumbha</s> — those two attacked the monkeys.
They guarded the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, protected the <s>Rākṣasa</s> army,
Maintained the weapon-force without abandoning it, and sought the destruction of the foes.
That army shrieked, and fled in confusion,

children.text: acyutac ca kṣataṃ raktaṃ, hataṃ cā 'dhyaśayiṣṭa gām.
children.translated_text: Blood flowed from the wounded, and the slain lay upon the ground.
Those two, who made [their foes] tremble in battle, were fought by <s>Aṅgada</s>;
<s>Prajaṅgha</s> too, jealously, assailed the son of <s>Vālin</s>.
<s>Aṅgada</s> split his head with his fist,

children.text: ahārṣīc ca śiraḥ kṣipraṃ yūpākṣasya nirākulaḥ.
children.translated_text: And swiftly, without agitation, severed the head of <s>Yūpākṣa</s>.
<s>Dvivida</s> then crushed the body of <s>Lohitākṣa</s>;

children.text: kruddhaḥ kumbhas tato 'bhaitsīn maindaṃ sa-dvividaṃ śaraiḥ
children.translated_text: The enraged <s>Kumbha</s> then pierced <s>Mainda</s> along with <s>Dvivida</s> with arrows.
Wounded, those two reeled, and both fell to the ground.

children.text: mātulau vihvalau dṛṣṭvā kumbhaṃ vāli-suto nagaiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing his maternal uncles overwhelmed, the son of <s>Vālin</s> [struck] <s>Kumbha</s> with mountains;
The night-wanderer repelled them with a shower of arrows.
<s>Rāma</s> desired <s>Aṅgada</s> to quickly protect the monkeys.
<s>Sugrīva</s> quickly rescued the nephew from the enemy's peril,
And, enraged, dispatched the son of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> from life with his fist.
<s>Nikumbha</s> then hurled a mace at the lord of the monkeys;
<s>Hanumān</s> broke that terrible serpent-shaped [weapon] as it fell.
He overwhelmed the enemy with his splendor and roared terrifyingly,

children.text: grīvāṃ cā 'sya tathākrākṣīdajijīvad yathā na tam.
children.translated_text: And so twisted his neck that he did not survive.
With the assembled monkey army in excessive joy, the lord of the forest-dwelling monkeys achieved lasting victory;

children.text: nṛ-pati-matiraraṃsta prāpta-kāmeva harṣāt, rajani-cara-patīnāṃ santato 'tāyi śokaḥ.
children.translated_text: The mind of the king delighted as if his desires were fulfilled, with joy; and unceasing grief befell the lords of the night-wanderers.
Then the king of the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, his kinsmen slain, lamented:
"What shall I do with the kingdom? What use is <s>Sītā</s>?

children.text: atikāye hate vīre protsahiṣye na jīvitum.
children.translated_text: With the heroic <s>Atikāya</s> slain, I shall not desire to live.

children.text: hrepayiṣyati kaḥ śatrūn, kena jāyiṣyate yamaḥ.
children.translated_text: Who will put the enemies to shame? By whom shall <s>Yama</s> (Death) be conquered?

children.text: atikāyād vinā pāśyaṃ ko vā chetsyati vāruṇam,
children.translated_text: Without <s>Atikāya</s>, who will sever the noose of <s>Varuṇa</s>?

children.text: rāvaṇaṃ maṃsyate ko vā, svayambhūḥ kasya tokṣyati.
children.translated_text: Who will respect <s>Rāvaṇa</s>? To whom will <s>Svayambhū</s> (Brahmā) be gracious?
In whom shall I take pride? Who, ever loftier, will lead the kinsmen to eminence?

children.text: kaḥ preṣyati pit n kāle, kṛtvā kitthaṣyate na kaḥ.
children.translated_text: Who will command the ancestors in due time? Who, having acted, will not boast?
<s>Hari</s> (<s>Indra</s>) will raise the thunderbolt, will roam without fear,

children.text: bhokṣyate yajña-bhāgāṃś ca śūra-mānaṃ ca vakṣyati.
children.translated_text: Will enjoy the shares of sacrifices, and will proclaim the honor of heroes.
The sun will burn without hesitation, the wind will blow unrestrained,
The cycle of seasons will proceed, and the moon will rise at its own will.
The clouds will pour fiercely, <s>Yama</s> will act sternly —
At the death of <s>Atikāya</s>, what will they not do? They will do nothing otherwise.

children.text: anmīliṣyati cakṣur me vṛthā, yad vinayā''gatam
children.translated_text: My eyes will close in vain, deprived of that which came through humility;
They will not see <s>Narāntaka</s>, bowing humbly, eager to receive commands.

children.text: dhiṅ māṃ, triśirasā nā 'haṃ sandarśiṣye 'dya yat punaḥ,
children.translated_text: Fie on me, that I shall no longer behold <s>Triśiras</s>!
By whom shall the enemies be slain, now that he has met with dissolution?

children.text: śatrubhir nihate matte drakṣye 'haṃ saṃyuge sukham,
children.translated_text: When <s>Matta</s>, slain by enemies, [is gone] — shall I see comfort in battle?

children.text: yuddhonmattād vinā śatrūn samāskantsyati ko raṇe.
children.translated_text: Without the battle-maddened one, who will assail the enemies in war?
Without fear, <s>Śatakratu</s> (<s>Indra</s>) will challenge me to fight,

children.text: prakalpsyati ca tasyā 'rtho nikumbe dur haṇe hate
children.translated_text: And his purpose will be accomplished, with <s>Nikumbha</s> the formidable slain.
Affection for <s>Hari</s> (<s>Indra</s>) will be established, and <s>Laṅkā</s> will be struck;

children.text: devāntaka ! tvayā tyakto ripor yāsyāmi vaśyatām.
children.translated_text: O <s>Devāntaka</s>! Abandoned by you, I shall come under the enemy's power.

children.text: mariṣyāmi, vijeṣye vā, hatāś cet tanayā mama,
children.translated_text: I shall die or I shall conquer — if my sons are slain,

children.text: haniṣyāmi ripūṃs tūrṇaṃ, na jīviṣyāmi duḥkhitaḥ
children.translated_text: I shall swiftly slay the enemies; I shall not live in sorrow.
The sages will smile, the gods will narrate unceasingly:
'The lineage of the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s has perished due to the ill-policy of Ten-necked (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>).'
By whom was it imagined, dear one, that <s>Rāghava</s> would rend the limbs of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>

children.text: raṇe kartsyati gātrāṇi marmāṇi ca vitartsyati.
children.translated_text: In battle, and pierce his vital parts?
The sun will fall to the earth, the earth will be weighed [in a balance],
The sky will be broken by the wind, and struck with fists.
Fire will flow from the moon, the ocean will be dried up,

children.text: jalaṃ dhakṣyati, tigmāṃśoḥ syantyanti tamasāṃ cayāḥ.
children.translated_text: Water will burn, and masses of darkness will flow from the scorching-rayed [sun] —
Before <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, enraged, is overcome by a man in battle;
These [impossibilities] are never to be expected from any person.
With <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> slain, the monkeys will climb <s>Laṅkā</s>,

children.text: daṅkṣyanti rākṣasān, dṛptā bhaṅkṣyanti ca mamā ''śramān.
children.translated_text: Will bite the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, and, insolent, will break my hermitages.

children.text: cartsyanti bāla-vṛddhāṃś ca, nartsyanti ca mudā yutāḥ
children.translated_text: They will harass the young and the old, and will dance with joy;

children.text: tena rākṣasa-mukhyena vinā tān ko nirotsyati.
children.translated_text: Without that foremost <s>Rākṣasa</s>, who will ward them off?

children.text: amarṣo me paraḥ, sītāṃ rāghavaḥ kāmayiṣyate,
children.translated_text: My indignation is supreme — <s>Rāghava</s> will desire <s>Sītā</s>;
What happiness will he obtain from one fallen from his kingdom?
I shall kill <s>Vaidehī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>), I shall have the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s devour her,
Or I shall bury her in the earth — the cause of this destruction.

children.text: nā 'nurotsye jagal-lakṣmīṃ, ghaṭiṣye jīvituṃ na vā
children.translated_text: I shall not enjoy the splendor of the world; I shall not strive to live;

children.text: na raṃsye viṣayaiḥ śūnye bhavane bāndhavairaham.
children.translated_text: I shall not delight in pleasures, in an empty house without kinsmen.

children.text: modiṣye kasya saukhye 'haṃ, ko me modiṣyate sukhe,
children.translated_text: In whose happiness shall I rejoice? Who will rejoice in my happiness?

children.text: ādeyāḥ kiṃkṛte bhogāḥ kumbhakaṛṇa ! tvayā vinā.
children.translated_text: For whose sake should pleasures be taken, O <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, without you?
Whatever fortunes come to me when my friends have perished,

children.text: tāḥ kiṃ manyu-kṣatā''bhogā na vipatsu vipattayaḥ.
children.translated_text: Are they not, marred by grief and devoid of enjoyment, misfortunes amid misfortunes?
'The city will perish quickly, the monkeys will come swiftly,
If you do not make peace' — this was the wise saying of <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>.
'Maintained by the king's wealth, we shall not speak [of peace];
We shall fight' — this was spoken by <s>Prahasta</s>.
A mere mortal, a flying creature, will fight in battle
The king of the man-eaters, who is invincible with divine weapons and chariots!
Or rather, I shall prepare myself to fight; I shall not cower like one devoid of courage.
Today the flesh-eaters will be satisfied; the earth will drink the blood of enemies.
I shall attract glory, and I shall remove the enemies by my deeds;
The daughter of <s>Mithilā</s> (<s>Sītā</s>) will today experience the grief of her husband's death.
The lord of the <s>Yakṣa</s>s will applaud, <s>Yama</s> will dance for us;
And the monkey women, bereft of husbands and sons, will languish in the forest.

children.text: sukhaṃ svapsyanti rakṣāṃsi, bhramiṣyanti ca nirbhayam,
children.translated_text: The <s>Rākṣasa</s>s will sleep in comfort and roam without fear;

children.text: na vikrokṣyanti rākṣasyo, narāṃś cā 'tsyanti harṣitāḥ.
children.translated_text: The <s>Rākṣasī</s> women will not cry out, and will eat men with delight.

children.text: prāṅ muhūrtāt prabhāte'haṃ bhaviṣyāmi dhruvaṃ sukhī
children.translated_text: Within a moment of tomorrow's dawn, I shall surely be happy;

children.text: āgāmini, tataḥ kāle yo dvitīyaḥ kṣaṇo'paraḥ
children.translated_text: And in the coming time, in the next moment thereafter,
I shall go to conquer the lord of the gods (<s>Indra</s>) together with the immortals;
And after that, again I shall return to <s>Laṅkā</s>, free of envy."
To him, deluded and speaking thus, <s>Indrajit</s> approached:
"I shall fight!" — thus speaking, terrifying to the enemy,
"You do not know, O great king! We two shall conquer the realm protected by <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>);
We two [shall conquer] the abode of the gods, filled with the virtues of proud deities, together.

children.text: nā 'bhijñā te, sa-yakṣendraṃ bhaṅkṣyāvo yad yamaṃ balāt,
children.translated_text: You do not know — we two shall break <s>Yama</s> by force, along with the lord of <s>Yakṣa</s>s,
And we shall carry off their jewels and gain this city.

children.text: eṣa pekṣyāmyarīn bhūyo, na śociṣyasi rāvaṇa !
children.translated_text: Behold — I shall see to the enemies once more; do not grieve, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>!
You shall see the world without <s>Rāma</s>; you shall pervade all directions.
With your servants, you shall spread fear once more in the abode of the gods;

children.text: praṇaṃsyatyadya devendras tvāṃ, vakṣyati sa sannatim.
children.translated_text: The lord of the gods (<s>Indra</s>) will praise you today, and will profess submission.
The sages will fear you; you will preside over your enemies.
I shall be known today in battle by all who consider themselves heroes.
And today, the hosts of enemies who think themselves brave shall be known by me;

children.text: gūhiṣyāmi kṣitiṃ kṛttai- radya gātrair vanākasām.
children.translated_text: I shall cover the earth with the severed limbs of the forest-dwelling [monkeys].

children.text: ārokṣyāmi yugānta-vārida-ghaṭā- saṃghaṭṭa-dhīra-dhvaniṃ niryāsyan rathamacchrita-dhvaja-dhanuḥ- khaḍga-prabhā-bhāsuram.
children.translated_text: I shall mount my chariot, blazing with the luster of raised banner, bow, and sword, with the steady thunder-sound of end-of-age cloud-masses, going forth to battle.

children.text: śroṣyasyadya vikīrṇa-vṛkṇa-vimukha- vyāpanna-śatrau raṇe tṛptāṃś choṇita-śoṇa-bhīṣaṇamukhān kravyā'śinaḥ krośataḥ."
children.translated_text: You shall hear today, on the battlefield strewn with scattered, severed, routed, and fallen enemies, the flesh-eating creatures crying out, satisfied, with terrifying faces red with blood."
Then the warriors invoked blessings and poured offerings into the fires;
They had the Brahmins recite [auspicious verses], and performed auspicious rites.
They worshipped the clan-elders and embraced the children.

children.text: strīḥ samāvardhayan sā'srāḥ, kāryāṇi prādiśaṃs tathā.
children.translated_text: They bade farewell to their tearful wives, and assigned duties likewise.
They put on garments, applied ointments, and then ate meat and liquor;
They drank honey-mead (<s>mādhvīka</s>) and ate delicacies as they wished.
They sharpened their chosen weapons, girded themselves with armor,
Mounted fine chariots, and cursed the enemies likewise.
They worshipped the Four-faced (<s>Brahmā</s>), honored the Brahmins and praised them;
The enemy of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) anointed himself and desired his excellent vehicle.
He put on jewel-studded armor, fastened his shining sword,

children.text: adhyāsta syandanaṃ ghoraṃ, prāvartata tataḥ puraḥ
children.translated_text: Mounted his terrible chariot, and then set forth at the head.

children.text: āghnan bherīr mahā-svānāḥ, kambūṃś cā 'pyadhaman śubhān,
children.translated_text: Great-sounding drums were struck, and auspicious conches were blown;

children.text: atāḍayan mṛdaṅgāṃś ca, perāś cā 'pūrayan kalāḥ.
children.translated_text: And <s>mṛdaṅga</s> drums were beaten, and <s>perā</s> drums filled with musical notes.
Bards sang praises, they inspired each other with cries;
They roared lion-roars, and the horses and elephants galloped.
Meanwhile, inauspicious omens appeared: the sun's orb split;
Clouds showered blood; winds blew unbearably.

children.text: ārcchan vāmaṃ mṛgāḥ kṛṣṇāḥ, śastrāṇāṃ vyasmaran bhaṭāḥ,
children.translated_text: Black deer crossed to the left; soldiers forgot their weapons;
Spitting blood, exhausted, he tormented horse and elephant.

children.text: na tānagaṇayan sarvānāskandaṃś ca ripūn, dviṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Not counting all those enemies who were assailing them, the foes
Were cutting with sharp swords and piercing with lances likewise,
Slicing with the edges of discuses and striking hard with spears,
Shooting with crescent-headed arrows of fierce tips, and crushing thoroughly with lances.
The monkeys hurled trees and struck violently with mountains,
Struck with fists in rage, and bit with teeth as well.
They swiftly struck with knees and hit with palms and elbows,
And they hurled back various weapons discharged by the enemy.
<s>Indrajit</s> (the conqueror of <s>Śakra</s>) tore through the enemies and whirled about on all sides,

children.text: adhvanac ca mahā-ghoraṃ, na ca kaṃcana nā'dunot.
children.translated_text: And roared most terribly, yet there was none whom he did not strike.

children.text: nā'jānan sandadhānaṃ taṃ, dhanur naikṣanta bibhratam
children.translated_text: They did not perceive him fitting his arrows, nor did they see him bearing his bow,
Nor were they aware of the arrows flying toward them — the enemies were slain by him without knowing.
They heard a sound from one direction and fled in another,
They cried out from one place and were slain from another.
They rolled about, were split open, blood flowed from all around,
They grew weary and were unsated, and the wounded died by his hand.
<s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>), distressed in that situation, wished to invoke the <s>Brahmāstra</s> (Brahmā's weapon) for the destruction of all <s>Rākṣasa</s>s;
<s>Raghunandana</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) restrained him from that.

children.text: tato māyā-mayīṃ sītāṃ ghnan khaḍgena viyad-gataḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Indrajit</s>, flying through the sky, was seen striking an illusory <s>Sītā</s> with a sword;
The son of <s>Māruta</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>) spoke these words to him:
"She has committed no offense; she has not strayed from her husband's side —

children.text: sītāṃ rākṣasa ! mā smaināṃ nigṛhṇāḥ pāpa ! duḥkhitām"
children.translated_text: O <s>Rākṣasa</s>, do not strike <s>Sītā</s>! Do not, O wicked one, torment the suffering woman!"
"It is to be done — the affliction of the enemies' friends," said <s>Indrajit</s>,
And having drawn his sword, he cut off her head.
"She for whose sake we seized the enemies, and crossed the ocean —
She is slain!" — speaking thus, the son of <s>Māruta</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>) approached <s>Rāma</s>.
Then the two heroes, the sons of <s>Raghu</s>, swooned and wept,

children.text: uṣṇaṃ ca prāṇatāṃ dīrghamuccair vyākrośatāṃ tathā.
children.translated_text: And breathed hotly and deeply and cried out aloud.
The grandson of <s>Pulastya</s> (<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>) addressed them: "Do not weep, you two!
Surely the wicked one, having deluded us, has gone to <s>Nikumbhilā</s>.
Do not remain here — stationed there, he is to be slain before the sacrificial fire is offered;
Before the terrible <s>Brahmaśiras</s> weapon and chariot are fully acquired.
<s>Brahmā</s> ordained his death when that rite is left uncompleted."
<s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) gave orders to <s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>) and the troop-leaders.

children.text: tāṃ pratyaicchan su-saṃpritās tatas te sa-vibhīṣaṇāḥ,
children.translated_text: They gladly accepted that command; then they, accompanied by <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
Marched upon <s>Nikumbhilā</s> and were obstructed by <s>Rākṣasa</s>s.

children.text: dik-pālaiḥ kadanaṃ tatra sene prākurutāṃ mahat,
children.translated_text: The guardians of the directions made great slaughter there among the two armies.
Having conquered the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s swiftly, the grandson of <s>Pulastya</s> (<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>) and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
Beheld <s>Indrajit</s> there, established in his sacrificial seat, concentrated in meditation.
He was offering oblations to the fire, murmuring the supreme <s>mantra</s>.

children.text: adhyāyac chakrajid brahma, samādheracalan na ca.
children.translated_text: <s>Indrajit</s> was reciting the <s>Brahma</s> (Vedic texts); he did not stir from his <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption).
<s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>) challenged him and roared terrifyingly.
<s>Indrajit</s> became enraged there and spoke these words to his uncle (<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>):
"You were born here, your body was nourished here with the food of the gods,
Here you lived — how is it that you have undertaken such cruelty here?
You did not see a hand still moist [with ritual water], nor did you regard the bond of kinship.

children.text: a-dharmān nā 'trasaḥ pāpa ! loka-vādān na cā 'bibheḥ,
children.translated_text: You did not tremble at unrighteousness, O wicked one, nor did you fear the censure of the world!
O defiler of <s>dharma</s>! Surely you know nothing and hear nothing of this.
By rejecting kinsmen thus, one undoubtedly goes to insignificance."
Then <s>Indrajit</s> was instructed by his uncle with these words:

children.text: "mithyā mā sma vyatikrāmo, macchīlaṃ mā na badhyathāh
children.translated_text: "Do not falsely transgress; do not fail to understand my nature.
Truly, I was born in the lineage of sinful <s>Rākṣasa</s>s.

children.text: na tvajāyata me śīlaṃ tādṛk, yādṛk pitus tava.
children.translated_text: But my character was not born such as that of your father.
When warned by me, he delighted in faults that bring destruction;
Therefore I abandoned <s>Daśagrīva</s> (the ten-necked one), but not out of hatred.
He seized others' property and violated other men's wives;

children.text: vyajighṛkṣat surān nityaṃ, prāmādyad guṇināṃ hite,
children.translated_text: He constantly sought to overpower the gods and was negligent in the welfare of the virtuous;
He suspected his well-wishing kinsmen and despised the elders greatly.
Your father delighted in those very faults for which I abandoned him.
Then he became angry and roared, and with twenty-two
