Arrows he struck his kinsman (<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>), and with twenty-five arrows the king (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>).
The son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> — <s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>) crushed his four horses.
He cut down the charioteer with arrows and shattered the chariot likewise.
Then the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> showered <s>Saumitri</s> with arrows from all sides.
The two brandished their strength and showered arrows upon each other repeatedly.
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> hurled the <s>Vāruṇa</s> (water-god's) weapon; <s>Indrajit</s> hurled the <s>Raudra</s> (<s>Rudra</s>'s) weapon.
Meeting each other, those weapons annihilated one another.

children.text: āsuraṃ rākṣasaḥ śastraṃ tato ghoraṃ vyasarjayat,
children.translated_text: The <s>Rākṣasa</s> then discharged the terrible <s>Āsura</s> (demonic) weapon;
From it poured forth abundant stones, tridents, clubs, and maces.
<s>Saumitri</s> arrested that invincible weapon with the <s>Māheśvara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>'s) weapon.
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> invoked the <s>Māhendra</s> (<s>Indra</s>'s) weapon, combined with the <s>Raudra</s>,
By that terrible weapon it was accomplished — and the head of the enemy was severed.
All the immortals rejoiced; the monkey troop-leaders were delighted;
<s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) embraced <s>Saumitri</s> and smelled his head.
The <s>Rākṣasa</s> army wept, the lord of night-wanderers (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) wept,
He cursed <s>Maithilī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>) and set out in distress to slay her.
"This is improper!" — his trusted ones restrained him,
And blocked his path, and kinship calmed his grief.
His heroism swelled and his fury also grew;
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s> readied his entire army for battle.
They tended the sacred fires and worshipped <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),
The <s>Rākṣasa</s>s propitiated <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s for peace, out of fear for their existence.
A pleasant wind blew from all sides, fragrant with the scent of ghee;
The auspicious sounds of "<s>Svasti</s>" (blessings) and "<s>Puṇyāha</s>" (auspicious day) were heard being uttered.
The warriors bore water with unbroken rice upon their heads for the rite of peace,
And they gave jewels and cows, and wished for blessings.
They anointed themselves with white sandalwood paste, dressed in splendid attire,

children.text: adhārayan srajaḥ kāntā, varma cā 'nye 'dadhur drutam.
children.translated_text: They wore beautiful garlands, and others quickly donned their armor.
They sharpened weapons and polished their collections of swords,
They mounted elephants and the rest, and then set forth swiftly.
The sound born of the army's mobilization filled the sky,
And the quarters were filled with tumultuous blasts of trumpets.
There was a crush at the gates of chariots, horses, elephants, and <s>Rākṣasa</s>s,
And it was accompanied by terrifying omens.
The monkeys were not afraid in that battle and broke great trees,
They swiftly dug up mountains and seized great boulders.
Then battle commenced — the monkeys and <s>Rākṣasa</s>s struck one another,
They overpowered one another and could not endure the crushing.

children.text: prāvardhata rajo bhaumaṃ, tad vyāśnuta diśo daśa,
children.translated_text: The dust of the earth grew, and it spread to the ten directions,
And it robbed the monkeys and <s>Rākṣasa</s>s of the ability to distinguish friend from foe.
Then in that darkness, the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s attacked their own as well as others;
And the monkeys too, merciless, attacked even their own monkeys.
They roared most terribly, and blood dripped;
On all sides a mire of blood formed.

children.text: gambhīrāḥ prāvahan nadyaḥ, samajāyanta ca hradāḥ,
children.translated_text: Deep rivers of blood flowed and pools were formed,

children.text: vṛddhaṃ ca tad rajo 'śāmyat, samavedyanta ca dviṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: And the swollen dust settled, and the enemies could be discerned again.
Then <s>Rāma</s> performed marvels with torrents of weapons, brandishing his great bow,

children.text: rāmaḥ, samīhitaṃ tasya nā'cetan sve na cā 'pare.
children.translated_text: And neither his own side nor the enemy could perceive his intention.
They saw the cut and the broken on all sides from <s>Rāma</s>'s arrows;

children.text: kruṣṭaṃ hāheti cā 'śṛṇvan na ca rāmaṃ nyarūpayan.
children.translated_text: They heard the cry "Alas! Alas!" — but they could not perceive <s>Rāma</s>.
He shattered masses of enemies, crushed horses and elephants,

children.text: apinaṭ ca rathā'nīkaṃ, na cā 'jñāyata saṃcaran.
children.translated_text: And destroyed the chariot-army, yet could not be discerned as he moved.
Ten thousand elephants, fourteen thousand
Great-souled charioteers with their horses and riders,

children.text: lakṣe ca dve padātīnāṃ rāghaveṇa dhanur-bhṛtā
children.translated_text: And two <s>lakṣa</s> (hundred-thousand) foot-soldiers — by <s>Rāghava</s>, the bow-bearer,
Were brought to destruction in the eighth part of the day.
He seemed to weave the realm of <s>Yama</s> (Death), to create a playground for <s>Rudra</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),
And to pave the earth with mountains of slain great <s>Rākṣasa</s>s.
The gods and <s>Gandharva</s>s praised him; the monkeys were astonished;
Affection swelled in the monkey-lord (<s>Sugrīva</s>); the grandson of <s>Pulastya</s> (<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>) deemed it wondrous.
The <s>Rākṣasa</s> women wailed aloud and reviled <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
The young and old were bewildered, and the people wept together.

children.text: sarvataś cā'bhayaṃ prāpnon naicchan nṛbhyas tu rāvaṇaḥ,
children.translated_text: Obtaining safety from all sides, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> still would not yield to the humans,
And they said: "This is the fruit of his ill speech that has come upon him."
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, mounting his great and terrible chariot, charged forth;
The earth shook, and terrifying vultures gathered.
Clouds with lightning rained down a drizzle of blood,
Terrible winds blew, and jackals howled inauspiciously.
He roamed about, disregarding the evil omens, and in the battle
He shook his bow with torrents of weapons and pressed upon the enemies.
Mountains hurled by <s>Sugrīva</s> destroyed the foes;
Then he grew weary, flagged, and fell to the ground.
Blood dripped, water flowed, and he was greatly agitated;
The army, afflicted by <s>Sugrīva</s>, was falling away, consumed by flesh-eating creatures.
Then <s>Virūpākṣa</s> sported in battle on a maddened elephant;
The monkey-lord (<s>Sugrīva</s>) shattered his head with a fist.
And immediately after, he pulverized <s>Yūpākṣa</s> with a boulder.
Enraged, <s>Aṅgada</s> thoroughly crushed <s>Mahodara</s> with his fist.
Then the ten-necked one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), enraged, wrung out the lives of the forest-dwellers (monkeys),
Protected the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, and caused the enemies to flee in all directions.
He looked upon <s>Kākutstha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), dared him, roared terribly,
Whirled his fearsome bow, and terrified the enemies.

children.text: āskandal lakṣmaṇaṃ bānairatyakrāmac ca taṃ drutam,
children.translated_text: He assailed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> with arrows and quickly overtook him,
The victorious one charged against <s>Rāma</s> and overwhelmed him with showers of arrows.

children.text: apauhad bāṇa-varṣaṃ tad bhallai rāmo nirākulaḥ,
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, unperturbed, repelled that rain of arrows with crescent-headed shafts,
And struck back at the ten-necked one with arrows like venomous serpents.
The two performed marvelous circling maneuvers and cut through each other's streams of weapons;

children.text: jagad vismāpayetāṃ tau, na ca vīrāvasīdatām.
children.translated_text: They amazed the world, yet neither hero faltered.
They filled the sky with arrows and made the earth invisible with fallen ones,
They struck each other swiftly and repeatedly displayed their martial skill.
The <s>Rākṣasa</s> of cruel valor fitted the <s>Āsura</s> (demonic) weapon;
From it issued forth great serpents and terrifying tigers and lions.

children.text: nyaṣedhat pāvakā'streṇa rāmas tad rākṣasas tataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> checked it with the <s>Pāvaka</s> (fire-god's) weapon; then the <s>Rākṣasa</s>
Employed the <s>Raudra</s> (<s>Rudra</s>'s) weapon, most fierce — from it poured forth pestles and the like.
The lord of the earth (<s>Rāma</s>) countered that with the <s>Gāndharva</s> weapon; then the man-eater (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>)
Struck <s>Kākutstha</s> in all his vital points with sharp arrows.

children.text: tatas triśirasaṃ tasya prāvṛścal lakṣmaṇo dhvajam,
children.translated_text: Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> cut off his three-headed banner,
And quickly crushed his charioteer and struck him with abundant arrows.
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> crushed his horses and swiftly destroyed his chariot;

children.text: nā'kṣubhnād rākṣaso, bhrātuḥ śaktiṃ codavṛhad gurum.
children.translated_text: The <s>Rākṣasa</s> was not shaken — he raised a heavy spear belonging to his brother.
<s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>) cut that descending spear into three with arrows;
The onlookers cheered; then the enraged night-wanderer (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>)
Raised a greater <s>Mahāśakti</s> (great spear) with eight bells,
And struck the brother of <s>Rāma</s> with it; he fell to the earth, lifeless.
The arrows of <s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) fell short; harassed by them,
The ten-necked one swiftly retreated from the battlefield.
The elder brother (<s>Rāma</s>) drew out with a trembling hand the spear from <s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>),
And sprinkled upon him those herbs which had been brought by <s>Hanumān</s>.
The son of <s>Sumitrā</s> revived; the brother embraced him long,
Gently kissed his head, and asked about his well-being.
Then all were ready to fight and rushed against the enemies;
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> too, having arrived with another chariot, fought fiercely.
"The battle is unequal between one standing on the ground and one in a chariot" — thus <s>Mātali</s>
Brought an exceedingly fierce chariot with weapons, by the command of <s>Maghavān</s> (<s>Indra</s>).
That was mounted by <s>Rāma</s>; then the ten-faced one
Discharged the <s>Pāśupata</s> weapon — the king conquered it with the <s>Śakra</s> (Indra's) missile.
Then <s>Rāma</s> overwhelmed the night-wanderer with a hundred thousand
Arrows, slew the lead horses, and swiftly struck down the charioteer.
Portents were seen, the disc of the earth trembled,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> hurled a trident, and the lord of the earth [hurled] the spear of <s>Indra</s>.
Those two, encountering each other, were mutually annihilated;

children.text: lakṣeṇa patriṇāṃ vakṣaḥ kruddho rāmasya rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: The enraged <s>Rākṣasa</s> covered the chest of <s>Rāma</s> with a hundred thousand feathered arrows.
<s>Rāma</s> then pierced him exceedingly with arrows; <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was not weakened;
His charioteer guided the chariot away.
The <s>Rākṣasa</s> berated the charioteer and again advanced the chariot;
Both discharged arrows, both pierced the yoke-horses,
Both cut each other's banners — neither of those two was distressed.
Both blazed boldly and employed skill,
Both exercised illusion — the two heroes did not tire.
Both swiftly executed various circular maneuvers,
And neither of the two could be perceived; both charioteers drove
The two chariots close together — the horses of both blazed.
Then the <s>Rākṣasa</s> displayed illusory heads in battle;
One hundred and one of those were severed by <s>Rāma</s>'s sharp arrows.
The oceans surged, the mountains trembled,
<s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) was seized by terror, the earth shook and quaked.
Then the weapon was recalled to the king's mind by <s>Mātali</s> —
The fierce one that <s>Svayambhū</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) had fashioned for the slaying of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
The wind was in its feathers, the fierce sun and fire at its tip,
Its weight was like <s>Meru</s>, its form subtle and made of sky.

children.text: rājitaṃ gāruḍaiḥ pakṣair viśveṣāṃ ghāma tejasām
children.translated_text: Adorned with <s>Garuḍa</s>'s wings, [bearing] the heat of all radiances —

children.text: smṛtaṃ tad rāvaṇaṃ bhittvā sughoraṃ bhuvyaśāyayat.
children.translated_text: That [weapon], remembered, having pierced <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, exceedingly terrible, laid him on the ground.

children.text: ābadhnan kapi-vadanāni saṃprasādaṃ, prāśaṃsat sura-samitir nṛpaṃ jitā 'rim,
children.translated_text: The monkey faces were bound with joy; the assembly of gods praised the king who had conquered the enemy;

children.text: anyeṣāṃ vigata-pariplavā digantāḥ, paulastyo'juṣata śucaṃ vipanna-bandhuḥ
children.translated_text: For others, the horizons were freed from disturbance; the descendant of <s>Pulastya</s> (<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>), his kinsmen destroyed, embraced grief.
Then grief born of kinship overtook him;
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> wept loudly for the ten-faced one.
"The ten-necked one lies on the ground, he who was accustomed to magnificent beds;

children.text: nekṣate vihvalaṃ māṃ ca, na me vācaṃ prayacchati.
children.translated_text: He does not look at me, distraught, nor does he give me his word.
This is the ripening [of fate], O ten-necked one! I foresaw it, [though] it had not yet come.

children.text: tvaṃ tenā'bhihitaḥ pathyaṃ kiṃ kopaṃ na niyacchasi.
children.translated_text: You were told by him what was wholesome — why did you not restrain your anger?
Misfortunes quickly seek out and prosperities swiftly pass by

children.text: tān, madān nā'vatiṣṭhante ye mate nyāyavādinām.
children.translated_text: Those who, intoxicated, do not abide by the counsel of those who speak rightly.
Those whose dependents bring what is unwholesome and harmful, extended by greed,

children.text: priyaṃ, śṛṇoti yas tebhyas, tamṛcchanti na sampadaḥ.
children.translated_text: Who hears pleasing [words] from them — prosperities do not reach him.

children.text: prājñās tejasvinaḥ samyak paśyanti ca, vadanti ca,
children.translated_text: The wise and the brilliant see clearly and speak clearly;
When they are disregarded, O great king, they languish and withdraw.

children.text: leḍhi bheṣaja-van nityaṃ yaḥ pathyāni kaṭūnyapi,
children.translated_text: He who, like medicine, always takes what is wholesome even if bitter,

children.text: tadarthaṃ sevate cā ''ptān, kadācin na sa sīdati.
children.translated_text: And for that purpose serves trusted [counselors] — he never falls.

children.text: sarvasya jāyate mānaḥ, sva-hitāc ca pramādyati,
children.translated_text: Everyone's pride arises, and one becomes negligent of one's own welfare,

children.text: vṛddhau bhajati cā 'pathyaṃ naro yena vinaśyati.
children.translated_text: And in prosperity one pursues what is unwholesome — by that a man perishes.

children.text: dveṣṭi prāyo guṇebhyo yan, na ca snihyati kasyacit,
children.translated_text: He who mostly hates the virtuous, who is affectionate to none,
And who makes enemies of the great — even one who is prosperous is destroyed.
By whom shall I be consoled? How shall I breathe, being wretched?

children.text: loka-traya-patir bhrātā yasya me svapiti kṣitau
children.translated_text: My brother, lord of the three worlds, sleeps upon the ground.

children.text: aho jāgarti kṛcchreṣu daivaṃ, yad bala-bhijjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, fate is awake in calamities — for those conquered by [superior] strength

children.text: luṭhyanti bhūmau klidyanti bāndhavā me svapanti ca.
children.translated_text: Roll upon the ground, are soaked [in blood], my kinsmen, and sleep [in death].

children.text: śivāḥ kuṣṇanti māṃsāni, bhūmiḥ pibati śoṇitam,
children.translated_text: Jackals tear the flesh, the earth drinks the blood;
Birds devour the meat of those born of the same navel as the ten-necked one.

children.text: yena pūta-krator mūrdhni sthīyate sma mahā''have,
children.translated_text: He upon whose head one used to stand in the great battle against the purifier of sacrifices (<s>Indra</s>) —
Even on the head of that <s>Indrajit</s>, by fate, crows now alight.
<s>Svarbhānu</s> (<s>Rāhu</s>) spits out the swallowed sun after performing his daily rite,

children.text: abhyupaiti punar bhūtiṃ rāma-grasto na kaścana.
children.translated_text: But one swallowed by <s>Rāma</s> never attains prosperity again.
You, not knowing this, O king, used to praise your own valor;

children.text: dātuṃ necchasi sītāṃ sma, viṣayāṇāṃ ca neśiṣe.
children.translated_text: You did not wish to give back <s>Sītā</s>, and you could not master your senses.
When fools speak in council, you too used to approve of them;

children.text: kathaṃ nāma bhavāṃs tatra nā 'vaiti hitamātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: How is it that you did not understand what was beneficial for yourself?

children.text: a-pṛṣṭo nu bravīti tvāṃ mantre mātāmaho hitam,
children.translated_text: Your grandfather, even unasked, used to tell you what was beneficial in counsel —
'I shall not do it,' O descendant of <s>Pulastya</s>! — thus you spoke from delusion.

children.text: tvaṃ sma vettha mahārāja ! yat smā''ha na vibhīṣanaḥ.
children.translated_text: You used to know, O great king, what <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> also used to say —

children.text: purā tyajati yat kruddo māṃ nirākṛtya saṃsadi.
children.translated_text: He whom, angry, you formerly rejected, dismissing him in the assembly.
<s>Madhavā</s> (<s>Indra</s>) fearlessly consumes the oblation at sacrifices;
The wind blows at its own will, the sun rises [freely].
The <s>Yakṣa</s> lord rules over wealth, <s>Yama</s> tames the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s,
<s>Varuṇa</s> extends his noose — the moon now rises [freely].
The cycle of seasons is calmed, the forest-dwellers perform austerities,

children.text: no namasyanti te bandhūn, varivasyanti nā 'marāḥ
children.translated_text: They no longer bow to your kinsmen, the gods no longer serve [them].
<s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) is expelled from <s>Laṅkā</s>, prosperities are disenchanted;

children.text: na veda tan, na yasyā'sti mṛte tvayi viparyayaḥ.
children.translated_text: One does not know that for which there is no reversal when you are dead.

children.text: śaktiṃ saṃsvajate śakro, gopāyati hariḥ śriyam,
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) embraces his thunderbolt, <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) guards his <s>Śrī</s> (glory),
Those worthy of divine worship rejoice, and rain-clouds become wonderful.
The gods angrily bear their weapons and desire battle;
It shines, and the flesh-eaters are also vigilant for openings.
They roam about surrounding <s>Laṅkā</s> and surpass even us;

children.text: bhūmayanti sva-sāmarthyaṃ, kīrtiṃ naḥ kanayanti ca.
children.translated_text: They magnify their own prowess and diminish our fame.

children.text: diśo vyaṣnuvate dṛptās tvat-kṛtāṃ jahati sthitim,
children.translated_text: The proud ones pervade the directions, they abandon the order established by you;

children.text: kṣodayanti ca naḥ kṣudrā, hasanti tvāṃ vipad-gatam.
children.translated_text: The base ones trample us and laugh at you, fallen into misfortune.

children.text: śamaṃ śamaṃ nabhasvantaḥ punanti parito jagat,
children.translated_text: The winds blow peacefully and purify the world on all sides;

children.text: ujjihīṣe mahārāja ! tvaṃ praśānto na kiṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Will you not rise, O great king? You lie still — what more [can I say]?

children.text: prorṇoti śokas cittaṃ me, satvaṃ saṃśāmyatīva me
children.translated_text: Grief overwhelms my mind, my fortitude is fading;
Sorrow obscures my vision — without you I release my strength.
With whom shall I converse? No other is as affectionate to kinsmen as you;
I cry out in emptiness — how shall I cover that which arises from grief?
I weep for myself, without protector, deprived of a kinsman in you,
I cannot fathom the measure of your kindnesses.
Now neither <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) nor the lord of <s>Yakṣa</s>s fears you, nor is he impoverished;

children.text: na garvaṃ jahito dṛptau, na kliśnīto daśā''nana !
children.translated_text: The proud ones have not abandoned their arrogance, they do not torment you, O ten-faced one!

children.text: tvayā 'pi nāma rahitāḥ kāryāṇi tanumo vayam,
children.translated_text: Deprived of you, we carry on our duties,

children.text: kurmaś ca jīvite buddhiṃ, dhik tṛṣṇāṃ kṛta-nāśinīm.
children.translated_text: And we form the intention to live — shame on desire that destroys what is gained!

children.text: tṛṇehmi dehamātmīyaṃ. tvaṃ vācaṃ na dadāsi cet,
children.translated_text: I care nothing for my own body; if you do not give me your word,

children.text: drāghayanti hi me śokaṃ smaryamāṇā guṇās tava.
children.translated_text: Your virtues, being remembered, only lengthen my grief.

children.text: unmucya srajamātmīyāṃ māṃ srajayati ko hasan,
children.translated_text: Who, smiling, having removed his own garland, will garland me?

children.text: nedayatyāsanaṃ ko me, ko hi me vadati priyam.
children.translated_text: Who will offer me a seat? Who indeed will speak kind words to me?

children.text: na gacchāmi purā laṅkā- māyur yāvad dadhāmyaham,
children.translated_text: I shall not go to <s>Laṅkā</s> before — as long as I hold my life —

children.text: kadā bhavati me prītis, tvāṃ paśyāmi na cedaham.
children.translated_text: When shall I have joy, if I do not see you?
I shall die within a moment, distraught, my kinsmen destroyed.

children.text: mantre sma hitamākhyāmi, na karomi tavā 'priyam.
children.translated_text: In counsel I used to tell what was beneficial — I did not act against your interest.
The women of the inner chambers and the citizens, deeply grieved,
Having heard that the descendant of <s>Pulastya</s> was slain by <s>Rāma</s> in battle, came running.
They tore their hair, they wailed with extreme anguish,
Repeatedly recalling the kindnesses of their lord, and also with great anger.

children.text: rāvaṇasya namanti sma paurāḥ sāsrā rudanti ca."
children.translated_text: The citizens bowed before <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, tearful, and wept."

children.text: bhāṣate sma tato rāmo vacaḥ paulastyamākulam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> spoke words to the distressed descendant of <s>Pulastya</s> (<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>):

children.text: "dātuḥ sthātur dviṣāṃ mūrdhni yaṣṭus tarpayituḥ pit n
children.translated_text: "Of one who was generous, steadfast, standing on the heads of enemies, who sacrificed and satisfied the ancestors —
Why do you grieve for the ten-faced one, who was unbroken in battle and unvanquished?

children.text: bobhavīti na sammoho vyasane sma bhavādṛśām,
children.translated_text: Delusion surely does not arise in persons like you in times of calamity;

children.text: kiṃ na paśyasi, sarvo 'yaṃ janas tvāmavalambate.
children.translated_text: Do you not see — all these people depend upon you?

children.text: tvamarhasi bhrāturanantarāṇi kartuṃ, janasyā 'sya ca śoka-bhaṅgam,
children.translated_text: You ought to perform the final rites for your brother, and [bring about] the breaking of grief for these people;

children.text: dhurye vipanne tvayi rājya-bhāro majjatyanūḍhaḥ kṣaṇadā-carendra !"
children.translated_text: When the chief is destroyed and you falter, the burden of the kingdom sinks, unborne, O lord of the night-wanderers!"
Then the descendant of <s>Pulastya</s> (<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>), with grief abated, spoke these words to <s>Rāma</s>:
"Even one who is not to be mourned — would not a kinsman grieve when he goes to destruction?

children.text: taṃ no devā vidheyāsur yena rāvaṇa-vad vayam
children.translated_text: May the gods grant us that by which, like <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, we
May also conquer our enemies and endure in battle.

children.text: kriyeraṃś ca daśā''syena yathā 'nyenā 'pi naḥ kule
children.translated_text: May the rites be performed for the ten-faced one as for any other in our family —
A lord, one whose offerings reach the gods, a devourer of humans, and a humbler of enemy hosts.
He alone would sustain his life-breaths in such a destruction of kinsmen
Who has a friend as able as you to give consolation.

children.text: mriyeyordhvaṃ muhūrtāddhi, na syās tvaṃ yadi me gatiḥ,
children.translated_text: I would die within a moment, if you were not my refuge;

children.text: āśaṃsā ca hi naḥ, prete jīvema-daśamūrdhani.
children.translated_text: And indeed our hope is that, with the ten-headed one dead, we may live.

children.text: prakuryāma vayaṃ deśe garhyāṃ tatra kathaṃ ratim,
children.translated_text: How could we make blameworthy pleasure in that place
Where there is no possibility of [seeing] our brother of twenty arms?"
Then <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> addressed the ministers who bowed respectfully:
"Go quickly to <s>Laṅkā</s> and enter the royal palace.
Take the most precious garments there with haste,
Raise the excellent banners and bring out the finest sandal-paste.
Release the sky-incense, and weave auspicious garlands;
Bring unlimited firewood, camphor, aloe-wood, and saffron.

children.text: uhyeran yajña pātrāṇi, hriyeta ca vibhāvasuḥ,
children.translated_text: Let the sacrificial vessels be carried, and let the sacred fire be brought;
Let the ghee be carried by the priests, and let the sacrificial fuel-sticks and <s>kuśa</s> grass be arranged.
Bathe [him] quickly with bathing materials, anoint with lovely unguents,
And adorn the ten-faced one with jewels worthy of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Clothe the lord of <s>Rākṣasa</s>s in two fine, pure garments;
Let the priest place him, garlanded, head facing east, upon a deer-skin.
Let the sacrificial vessels be arranged by lineage according to proper rite,

children.text: juhuyāc ca havir vahnau, gāyeyuḥ sāma sāmagāḥ."
children.translated_text: Let oblations be offered to the fire, and let the <s>Sāmaveda</s> chanters sing the <s>Sāman</s>."

children.text: gatvā 'tha te purīṃ laṅkāṃ kṛtvā sarvaṃ yathoditam
children.translated_text: Having gone to the city of <s>Laṅkā</s> and having done everything as instructed,
They, tearful, near the time of the final oblation, reported to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>:
"Everything has been done as directed; to perform the fire and water rites,
Endeavor, O great king, together with all your kinsmen.
Be not faint-hearted like one without command; adopt unwavering steadfastness;

children.text: stheyāḥ kāryeṣu bandhūnāṃ, heyāḥ śokodbhavaṃ tamaḥ.
children.translated_text: Stand firm in the duties toward kinsmen; abandon the darkness born of grief.
This is not to be imagined — that you too should languish in calamities;

children.text: na pṛthag-jana-vaj jātu pramuhyet paṇḍito janaḥ.
children.translated_text: A wise person should never be bewildered like a common man.

children.text: yacca yatra bhavāṃs tiṣṭhet, tatrā 'nyo rāvaṇasya na,
children.translated_text: And whatever place you should occupy — there is no other for <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s [succession];

children.text: yacca yatra bhavān sīden mahadbhis tad vigarhitam.
children.translated_text: And whatever place you should falter — that is condemned by the great.

children.text: āścaryaṃ, yacca yatra tvāṃ prabrūyāma vayaṃ hitam,
children.translated_text: It would be a wonder if we should tell you what is beneficial;
You could teach even <s>Indra</s>'s own priest in times of difficulty.
The people's desire [is:] 'May you abandon negligence, O lord of the <s>Nairṛta</s>s!'
Even enemies would grieve at the calamity — how much more kinsmen?

children.text: sa bhavān bhrātṛ-vad rakṣed yathāvadakhilaṃ janam,
children.translated_text: May you protect all the people, as a brother would, in the proper manner;

children.text: na bhavān saṃpramuhyec cedāśvasyuś ca niśācarāḥ,
children.translated_text: If you should not be bewildered, the night-wanderers would be consoled."
Then he went to perform the fire and water rites for his brother.
<s>Rāma</s> then spoke to the <s>Rākṣasa</s> who had accomplished his duties.
Sprinkling water with a golden pitcher upon his head, the concentrated one [said]:
"You are the king of the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s — may you watch over <s>Laṅkā</s>, O <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>!
You should properly conciliate the angry, you should win over the greedy with wealth,

children.text: mānino mānayeḥ kāle, trastān paulastya ! sāntvayeḥ.
children.translated_text: You should honor the proud in due time, O descendant of <s>Pulastya</s>, you should soothe the frightened.

children.text: icchā me paramā, nandeḥ kathaṃ tvaṃ vṛtra-śatru-vat,
children.translated_text: My supreme wish is: how may you rejoice like the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s> (<s>Indra</s>)?

children.text: iccheddhi suhṛdaṃ sarvo vṛddhi-saṃsthaṃ yataḥ suhṛt.
children.translated_text: For every friend wishes a friend established in prosperity, since he is a friend.
May you prosper among your own people; may you destroy the enemy hosts;

children.text: bhūyās tvaṃ guṇināṃ mānyas, teṣāṃ stheyā vyavasthitau.
children.translated_text: May you be honored by the virtuous; may you stand firm in their establishment.

children.text: dheyās tvaṃ suhṛdāṃ prītiṃ, vandiṣīṣṭhā divaukasaḥ,
children.translated_text: May you give delight to your friends; may you worship the celestials;

children.text: somaṃ peyāś ca, heyāś ca hiṃsrā hāni-karīḥ kriyāḥ
children.translated_text: May you drink <s>Soma</s>; and may you abandon violent deeds that cause harm.
And may you settle the affairs of the city-dwellers according to <s>dharma</s> (righteousness);

children.text: anurāgaṃ kriyā rājan ! sadā sarva-gataṃ jane.
children.translated_text: O king, may your actions always produce universal affection among the people.
May anger be destroyed by you; may eminence be grasped;

children.text: rakṣobhir darśiṣīṣṭhās tvaṃ, drakṣīran bhavatā ca te.
children.translated_text: May you be seen by the <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, and may they be seen by you.

children.text: manyuṃ vadhyā bhaṭa-vadha-kṛtaṃ bāla-vṛddhasya rājan !, śāstrā'bhijñāḥ sadasi su-dhiyaḥ sannidhiṃ te kriyāsuḥ,
children.translated_text: O king, you should suppress anger born of warrior-slaying toward the young and old; let the wise, versed in the <s>śāstra</s>s (scriptures), attend your presence in assembly;

children.text: saṃraṃsīṣṭhāḥ sura-muni-gate vartmani prājya-dharme, saṃbhutsīṣṭhāḥ su-naya-nayanair vidviṣāmīhitāni."
children.translated_text: May you delight in the path of abundant <s>dharma</s> traversed by gods and sages; may you discover the designs of enemies through the eyes of good counsel."
Then, having approached <s>Sītā</s>, the son of the Wind (<s>Hanumān</s>) spoke:
"By good fortune, prosper, O <s>Vaidehī</s>! The thorn of the three worlds has been slain.
Give permission — let these be slain by me, these of petty minds,
Your <s>Rākṣasī</s> guards — harbor resentment toward them.
Consider them as grass — of evil conduct, terrible form, vile purpose and deed,

children.text: hiṃsrā bhavatu te buddhiretās, kuru niṣṭhuram.
children.translated_text: Cruel — let your mind be [set against] them; be merciless.

children.text: paścimaṃ karavāmaitat priyaṃ devi ! vayaṃ tava,"
children.translated_text: Let us do this last favor for you, O queen!"
Then <s>Sītā</s>, compassionate in heart, spoke to the monkey:
"Let your mind be calmed toward those who carried out [another's] orders for their sustenance,
Being of lowly nature — the fault lies with him who committed it; he has been slain, the unworthy one.

children.text: na hi preṣya-vadhaṃ ghoraṃ karavānyastu te matiḥ,
children.translated_text: I shall certainly not commit the terrible slaying of servants — let that be your resolve.

children.text: edhi kārya-karas tvaṃ me gatvā pravada rāghavam.
children.translated_text: Be a doer of my task — go and tell <s>Rāghava</s>:
'<s>Maithilī</s>, desiring to see [you], O <s>Rāma</s>, wishes to see you without delay.'"
Having promised 'So be it,' he went and said to <s>Rāghava</s>:
"Let the eager queen be brought, O joy of the <s>Kākutstha</s> line!"
Having scratched the earth, having sighed, having looked at <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
<s>Rāghava</s> said: "Bring <s>Sītā</s>, adorned."

children.text: gatvā praṇamya tenoktā maithilī madhuraṃ vacaḥ.
children.translated_text: Having gone and bowed, he (<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>) spoke to <s>Maithilī</s> with sweet words:
"Abandon your grief, O <s>Vaidehī</s>! Set your mind to joy.
Abandon your hatred toward <s>Rāvaṇa</s>; leave the pleasure-garden.
Bathe, anoint yourself, fumigate with incense, dress, and put on a garland;
Put on jewels; pour oblations into the kindled fire;

children.text: addhi tvaṃ pañca-gavyaṃ ca, chindhi saṃrodha-jaṃ tamaḥ,
children.translated_text: Eat the five products of the cow (<s>pañcagavya</s>); cut through the darkness born of confinement.

children.text: āroha śibikāṃ haimīṃ, dviṣāṃ jahi mano-rathān.
children.translated_text: Mount a golden palanquin; destroy the hopes of your enemies.
May the lord of kings wipe away the grief arising from separation from you;
May you henceforth be engaged in your own home.
Be consecrated with <s>Rāma</s> swiftly in the horse-sacrifice (<s>aśvamedha</s>);

children.text: dṛśyasva patyā prītena prītyā prekṣasva rāghavam.
children.translated_text: Be seen by your pleased husband; gaze upon <s>Rāghava</s> with love.

children.text: ayaṃ niyogaḥ patyus te, kāryā nā'tra vicāraṇā,
children.translated_text: This is the command of your husband — no deliberation is needed here.

children.text: bhūṣayā 'ṅgaṃ, pramāṇaṃ ced, rāmaṃ gantuṃ yatasva ca
children.translated_text: Adorn your body, if this is authoritative; and strive to go to <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: mudā saṃyuhi kākutsthaṃ, svayaṃ cā ''pnūhi sampadam,
children.translated_text: Meet <s>Kākutstha</s> with joy, and attain prosperity yourself;
Approach the presence of <s>Rāghava</s> within a moment, O queen!

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ muhūrtādahno 'ṅga ! svāminī sma bhava kṣiteḥ
children.translated_text: Within a moment of the day, O dear one, become the sovereign of the earth,
Standing in the role of chief queen — govern the people of the city.
Rise by your husband's will; strive likewise for adornment;

children.text: pratiṣṭhasva ca taṃ draṣṭuṃ draṣṭavyaṃ tvaṃ mahī-patim."
children.translated_text: And set forth to see that king who must be seen by you."
Having carried out the appointed command as instructed, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>
Mounted the vehicle, her face veiled with a silken cloth.
Bowed with modesty, agitated by the memory of the grief of separation,
Tearful, having come to her husband's presence, she, miserable, wept.
Then the king, having conceived doubt about her conduct, spoke to her,
As he wished: "I do not accept you, O <s>Sītā</s>! Go hence."
You, who were clasped upon <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s lap, are a cause of heart-anguish to me.

children.text: matiṃ badhāna sugrīve , rākṣasendraṃ gṛhāṇa vā.
children.translated_text: Fix your mind on <s>Sugrīva</s>, or take the lord of <s>Rākṣasa</s>s.

children.text: aśāna bharatād bhogān, lakṣmaṇaṃ pravṛṇīṣva vā,
children.translated_text: Enjoy pleasures from <s>Bharata</s>, or choose <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
Or go where you desire — let hopes bound to <s>Rāma</s> be released.

children.text: kva ca khyāto raghor vaṃśaḥ, kva taṃ para-gṛhoṣitā,
children.translated_text: Where is the renowned lineage of <s>Raghu</s>, and where is she who dwelt in another's house?
Give your heart to another — let us not unite in what is undesired.

children.text: yatheṣṭaṃ cara vaidehi !, panthānaḥ santu te śivāḥ,
children.translated_text: Do as you wish, O <s>Vaidehī</s>! May your paths be auspicious.

children.text: kāmās te'nyatra tāyantāṃ viśaṅkāṃ tyaja mad-gatām.
children.translated_text: Let your desires be fulfilled elsewhere — abandon suspicion directed at me."
Then <s>Maithilī</s>, of noble birth, addressed the king with these words:
"Let the suspicion born of the common [nature of] women be abandoned toward me.

children.text: daivād bibhīhi kākutstha ! jihrīhi tvaṃ tathā janāt,
children.translated_text: Fear fate, O <s>Kākutstha</s>! And be ashamed before the people likewise,
[You who are] falsely enraged at me — I who was helpless, carried off by the enemy.

children.text: cetasas tvayi vṛttir me, śarīraṃ rakṣasā hṛtam,
children.translated_text: My heart's inclination is toward you; [only] my body was carried off by the <s>Rākṣasa</s>.
May the righteous gods make known that this statement is true.

children.text: tvaṃ punīhi punīhīti punan vāyo ! jagattrayam
children.translated_text: You, O <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind)! who purify again and again, purifying the three worlds,

children.text: caran deheṣu bhūtānāṃ viddhi me buddhi-viplavam.
children.translated_text: Moving through the bodies of beings — know my purity of mind.
Traversing the sky, traversing heaven, traversing the earth — O supremely purifying
Waters! Know my auspicious mental disposition.

children.text: jaganti dhatsva dhatsveti dadhatī tvaṃ vasundhare !
children.translated_text: O <s>Vasundharā</s> (Earth)! You who bear and uphold the worlds —
Know my conduct, undeviated by day and night.

children.text: rasān saṃhara, dīpyasva, dhvāntaṃ jahi, nabho bhrama,
children.translated_text: Gather flavors, blaze forth, destroy darkness, revolve through the sky —

children.text: itīhamānas tigmāṃ'śo ! vṛttaṃ jñātuṃ ghaṭasva me.
children.translated_text: O fierce-rayed one (<s>Sūrya</s>, the Sun)! Thus engaged, strive to know my conduct.
Existing in heaven, dwelling on earth, abiding in the serpent-realm —
O <s>Ākāśa</s> (Space)! Dwelling thus in me, perceive what has been done and not done.

children.text: citāṃ kuru ca saumitre ! vyasanasyā 'sya bheṣajam,
children.translated_text: And prepare a pyre, O <s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>)! — the remedy for this calamity.

children.text: rāmas tuṣyatu me vā 'dya, pāpāṃ pluṣṇātu vā 'nalaḥ
children.translated_text: May <s>Rāma</s> be satisfied with me today, or may fire burn the sinful one.
Then, seeing the pyre built by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> with <s>Rāghava</s>'s consent,
Having circumambulated it, she addressed <s>Rāma</s> with these words:

children.text: pravapāṇi vapur vahnau rāsā 'haṃ śāṅkitā tvayā,
children.translated_text: "I cast my body into the fire, being suspected by you.

children.text: sarve vidantu śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ sa plavaṅgamāḥ.
children.translated_text: Let all of you, with the monkeys, know and hear!

children.text: māṃ duṣṭāṃ jvalita-vapuḥ pluṣāṇa vahne ! saṃrakṣa kṣata-malināṃ suhṛd yathā vā,
children.translated_text: O Fire! If I am wicked, burn my blazing body; but if I am stained by injury, protect me as a friend.

children.text: eṣā 'haṃ kratuṣu vasor yathā ''jya-dhārā tvāṃ prāptā vidhi-vadudīrṇa-dīpti-mālam.
children.translated_text: Here I am — like a stream of clarified butter in the sacrificial rites — I have reached you, blazing with your kindled garland of flames, as ordained."
Then Fire, lifting up <s>Maithilī</s>, said to <s>Rāma</s>:
"O <s>Kākutstha</s>! How could you have suspected your beloved, virtuous wife?
If she were not going to be pure, then I would have abandoned her.

children.text: na caināṃ, pakṣapāto me dharmādanyatra rāghava !
children.translated_text: And my partiality for her is for no reason other than <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), O <s>Rāghava</s>!
Even there, the evil-minded enemy would not have solicited <s>Sītā</s>;
At times he would have spoken cruelly, and at times he would have praised his own glory.
And he would not have formed a resolve there — she being of pure mind.
You, <s>Rāma</s>, would have obtained true indignation on account of <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: tvayā 'drakṣyata kiṃ nā 'syāḥ śīlaṃ saṃvasatā ciram,
children.translated_text: Would you not have perceived her character, having dwelt with her for so long?

children.text: adarśiṣyanta vā ceṣṭāḥ kālena badhunā na kim.
children.translated_text: Or would her conduct not have been seen over such a long time?
You would have grieved for life, and if this darkness had not been dispelled,
Even the sun would have fallen to the earth, and this [earth] would have been shaken.
If feminine fickleness had occurred here, O great king,
These world-protectors would have come here, but they are hostile to strife.

children.text: āścaryaṃ yacca yatra strī kṛcchre 'vartsyan mate tava,
children.translated_text: And it is wonderful that a woman would have persevered in hardship, in your esteem;
If she had perished from fear, what fruit would you have obtained?
And wherever a woman, free from fault, would have died from virtuous fear,
In a world given to fault-finding, the ground for a false accusation against her [would have remained].

children.text: amaṃtsya bhavān yadvad tathaiva ca pitā tava
children.translated_text: Had you thought [wrongly], even your father,
King <s>Daśaratha</s> himself, standing in his celestial car, would not have come.
<s>Sthāṇu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), the trident-bearer, the bull-rider, would not have made his presence,
If <s>Maithilī</s>, the devoted wife, had been touched by another.
How would the lotus-seated (<s>Brahmā</s>), the creator of the universe, have come to gladden you,

children.text: rājendra ! viśva-sūr dhātā cāritrye sītayā kṣate.
children.translated_text: O great king, if <s>Sītā</s>'s character had been tainted?"
Bowing, addressed by <s>Brahmā</s>, the lord of kings then [said]:
"<s>Maithilī</s> would not have grieved in the world, if she had not performed this [ordeal].

children.text: nā'mokṣyāma vayaṃ śaṅkā- mihādhāsyan na ced bhavān,
children.translated_text: We would not have been freed from doubt, if you had not established [this test] here.

children.text: kiṃ vā citramidaṃ yuktaṃ, bhavān yadakariṣyata.
children.translated_text: What wonder is it that this was fitting — that which you would have accomplished?
If your actions had proceeded in accordance with truth,
In the world governed by you, <s>Rāma</s>, I would have declined greatly thereafter."
Then <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) spoke to the bowing <s>Rāma</s>:
"Would you not have known yourself to be <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the unborn?

children.text: ko nyo 'kartsyadiha prāṇān dṛptānāṃ ca sura-dviṣām,
children.translated_text: Who else would have taken the lives of the proud enemies of the gods?
Or who would have succeeded in deeds affecting all the worlds,
In the destruction of the <s>Daitya</s>s, O great king? — that which you would have accomplished there.

children.text: samāptiṃ jātu tatrāpi kiṃ nā 'neṣyas tvamīhitam.
children.translated_text: Would you not eventually have brought that enterprise to completion there too?
Having propitiated [your] father, <s>Kaiyyeyā</s> (<s>Kaikeyī</s>), and the tormented <s>Bharata</s>,
<s>Rāma</s>, desiring to bow, beheld the thousand-eyed one (<s>Indra</s>).

children.text: pretā vareṇa śakrasya prāṇantaḥ kapayas tataḥ
children.translated_text: By the boon of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), the monkeys who had died
Were reborn, with fruit-laden, bowing, luminous trees streaming [around them].
With trees of exceedingly fragrant flowers swarming with families upon families of bees, with lofty peaks made tawny by young <s>madhūka</s> blossoms,
With water-resting-places set in the intervals of peak-rocks, Mount <s>Suvela</s> displayed the glory of abundant fruits.

children.text: saṃvādbhiḥ sa-kusuma-reṇubhiḥ samīrai- rānamrair bahu-phala-dhāribhir vanā 'ntaiḥ
children.translated_text: By fragrant breezes laden with flower-pollen, by forest-ends bowing with abundant fruit-bearing,

children.text: ścyotadbhir madhu-paṭalaiś ca vānarāṇām āpyāno ripu-vadha-sambhavaḥ pramodaḥ
children.translated_text: By dripping masses of honey — the joy of the monkeys born of the enemy's slaying was nourished.

children.text: āyāntyaḥ sva-phala-bhareṇa bhaṅguratvaṃ bhṛṅgā''lī-nicaya-citā latās tarūṇām
children.translated_text: Creepers of trees, bending with the weight of their own fruits, covered with swarms of bees,

children.text: sā ''modāḥ kṣiti-tala-saṃsthitā'valopyā bhokt ṇāṃ ṣramamadayaṃ na nītavatyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Standing on the surface of the earth, their fragrance not to be carried away, did not bring weariness to those who enjoyed them.
Then <s>Rāma</s> said to the joyful <s>Hanumān</s>:
"Tomorrow you shall go to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, protected by <s>Bharata</s>, O monkey!
You shall traverse the sky again, with rows of bursting clouds,
You shall behold the cool spray of the waters of the lord of waters (the ocean).
You shall frequent the plateaus of Mount <s>Mahendra</s>, O monkey,
With moonlit lotus-ponds, beyond the path of the sun.
Covered with sandalwood trees, free from the dissolution of snow —

children.text: darśitāras tvayā tāś ca malayopatyakāḥ śubhāḥ.
children.translated_text: Those auspicious plateaus of <s>Malaya</s> have been seen by you.

children.text: pratanvyaḥ komalā vindhye sahitāraḥ syadaṃ na te
children.translated_text: The delicate creepers on the <s>Vindhya</s>, adorned with clusters [of flowers], swarming with bee-families —
They shall not be companions to you in your speed.
You shall see with delight, from nearby, <s>Kiṣkindhā</s> frequented by friends,
With partiality, remembering past play again and again.
Those two [mountains] in the <s>Mālyavad</s>-<s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest were shown by you,
Where, troubled long by duels, I suffered.
The two pleasant hermitages, swarming with deer, reached by you,
Filled with holy waters and twice-born [birds] — of <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s> and <s>Śarabhaṅga</s>.
Having passed by the lovely, painful <s>tapo-vana</s> (ascetic forest) of <s>Atri</s>,
You shall stop at the sacred <s>Citrakūṭa</s> mountain out of curiosity.

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ bharadvājo bhavatā darśitā muniḥ,
children.translated_text: Then beyond that, the sage <s>Bharadvāja</s> shall be seen by you,
And the holy people shall be seen — those whose sins are washed by the waters of the <s>Yamunā</s>.

children.text: syantvā syantvā divaḥ śambhor- mūrdhni skantvā bhuvaṃ gatām
children.translated_text: Having flowed and flowed from heaven, having leaped upon <s>Śambhu</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) head, having descended to earth —
You shall then plunge into the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, like the swift embodiment of merit.
Of the <s>Tamasā</s> [river], resembling a great dark rock in its hue —
From the edge of the forests, you shall see many trees of the city's pleasure-gardens.
Beholding the lovely <s>Sarayū</s>, tawny with fresh saffron

children.text: vilokya sarayūṃ ramyāṃ gantā 'yodhyā tvayā purī.
children.translated_text: Applied to the breasts of the city's women and washed off, you shall enter the city of <s>Ayodhyā</s>.

children.text: ānanditāras tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā praṣṭāraś cāvayoḥ śivam
children.translated_text: Overjoyed at seeing you, and inquiring about our welfare,

children.text: mātaraḥ saha maithilyā, toṣṭā ca bharataḥ param.
children.translated_text: The mothers shall be with <s>Maithilī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>), and <s>Bharata</s> shall be supremely pleased.
You shall relate how the enemy was slain, how <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> was consecrated,

children.text: sugrīvaṃ cā 'rjitaṃ mitraṃ, sarvāṃś cā''gāmukān drutam
children.translated_text: How <s>Sugrīva</s> was won as a friend, and all those who are coming swiftly.

children.text: gantāraḥ paramāṃ prītiṃ paurāḥ ṣrutvā vacas tava,
children.translated_text: The citizens, hearing your words, shall go to the highest joy;

children.text: jñātvaitat sammukhīnaś ca sametā bharato dhruvam.
children.translated_text: And having learned all this, <s>Bharata</s> shall surely come forward to meet [you].
When you have gone by this path, we too shall have been carried along;

children.text: labdhāhe 'haṃ dhṛtiṃ prāpte bhūyo bhavati sammukhe.
children.translated_text: I shall have obtained firmness, once you arrive again before me.
When he had departed, having grasped the meaning, <s>Rāma</s> said to <s>Sugrīva</s> and the <s>Rākṣasa</s> (<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>):

children.text: uktavān śvo 'bhigantāstho yuvāṃ saha mayā puram.
children.translated_text: "Tomorrow you two shall go together with me to the city.

children.text: draṣṭāsthas tatra tisro me māt s tuṣṭa'ntarā''tmanaḥ
children.translated_text: There you shall see my three mothers, their inner souls content;
You shall have attained the friendship of the highest women, and the refuge of <s>Bharata</s>.
We shall not have been so afflicted by the sorrow of separation;

children.text: śramo nubhavitā naivaṃ bhavadbhyāṃ ca viyoga-jaḥ,
children.translated_text: Nor shall you two have experienced such fatigue born of separation from us.

children.text: evaṃ yuvāṃ mama prītyai kalptāsthaḥ kapi-rākṣasau !
children.translated_text: Thus you two, O monkey and <s>Rākṣasa</s>, have been appointed for my pleasure!

children.text: gantuṃ prayatitāsāthe prātaḥ saha mayā yadi.
children.translated_text: You shall endeavor to depart in the morning together with me."
Then, eager, the descendant of <s>Paulastya</s> (<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>) and the monkey spoke to <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: anugraho 'yaṃ kākutstha ! gantāsvo yat tvayā saha.
children.translated_text: "This is a favor, O <s>Kākutstha</s>! That we shall go together with you.
We two shall not consent to separation from you,

children.text: api prāpya surendra-tvaṃ, kiṃ nu prattaṃ, tvayā ''spadam.
children.translated_text: Even upon obtaining the lordship of <s>Surendra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) — what, then, of what has been given by you as a realm?"

children.text: tataḥ kathābhiḥ samatītya doṣā- māruhya sainyaiḥ saha puṣpakaṃ te
children.translated_text: Then, having passed the night with stories, mounting the <s>Puṣpaka</s> (aerial chariot) together with the armies,
They set forth, agitating the fathomless waters of the ocean by their speed.

children.text: setuṃ, mahendraṃ, malayaṃ sa-vindhyaṃ, sa-mālyavantaṃ girimṛṣyamūkam,
children.translated_text: The bridge, <s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Malaya</s>, with the <s>Vindhya</s>, the mountain <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s> with <s>Mālyavān</s>,

children.text: sa-daṇḍakā'raṇya-vātīṃ ca pampāṃ rāmaḥ priyāyāḥ kathayan jagāma.
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, describing these to his beloved along with the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest region and <s>Pampā</s>, traveled on.

children.text: ete te muni-jana-maṇḍitā digantāḥ, śailo'yaṃ lulita-vanaḥ sa citrakūṭaḥ,
children.translated_text: "These are the horizons adorned by communities of sages; this is the mountain <s>Citrakūṭa</s> with its swaying forests;

children.text: gaṅgeyaṃ su-tanu-! viśāla-tīra-ramyā, maithilyā raghu-tanayo diśan nananda.
children.translated_text: This is the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, O slender one, lovely with wide banks" — the son of <s>Raghu</s>, pointing these out to <s>Maithilī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>), rejoiced.
With clusters of flowers at their tips swarming with buzzing bees, submerged in the flooding of cool waters,

children.text: ete te su-tanu ! purī-janopabhogyā dṛśyante nayana-manoramā vanā 'ntāḥ.
children.translated_text: "These, O slender one, are the pleasure-gardens to be enjoyed by the city's people, delightful to the eyes" — thus they are seen.

children.text: sthānaṃ naḥ pūrva-jānāmiyamadhikamasau preyasī pūrayodhyā, dūrādālokyate yā huta-vividha-haviḥ- prīṇitā 'śeṣa-devā,
children.translated_text: "This is the abode of our ancestors, and that, dearer still, is the great city <s>Ayodhyā</s>, seen from afar, where all the gods have been propitiated with various oblations offered into the fire;

children.text: so 'yaṃ deśo, rudantaṃ pura-janamakhilaṃ yatra hitvā prayātau āvāṃ sīte ! vanā 'ntaṃ saha dhṛta-dhṛtinā lakṣmaṇena kṣapā'nte.
children.translated_text: This is the region, O <s>Sītā</s>, where, leaving behind the entire weeping populace, we two departed to the forest at the end of the night, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> who bore his composure with resolve."

children.text: tūryāṇāmatha niḥsvanena sakalaṃ lokaṃ samāpūrayan vikrāntaiḥ kariṇāṃ girīndra-sadṛśāṃ kṣmāṃ kampayan sarvataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, filling the entire world with the sound of musical instruments, shaking the earth on all sides with the strides of elephants resembling the kings of mountains,

children.text: sā ''nandā 'śru-vilocanaḥ prakṛtibhiḥ sārdhaṃ sahā 'ntaḥ puraḥ samprāpto bharataḥ sa-mārutiralaṃ namraḥ samaṃ mātṛbhiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s>, with eyes full of tears of joy, together with the ministers and the inner court, arrived — along with the son of <s>Māruta</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>), bowing humbly with the mothers.
Then, surrounded by the excited citizens, with a brilliant <s>cāmara</s> (fly-whisk) held in <s>Bharata</s>'s hand,
Celebrated by the elders, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and kinsmen, the scion of <s>Raghu</s> entered the city.

children.text: pravidhāya dhṛtiṃ parāṃ janānāṃ yuva-rājaṃ bharataṃ tato'bhiṣicya
children.translated_text: Having bestowed supreme joy upon the people, and then consecrating <s>Bharata</s> as crown prince,

children.text: jaghaṭe turagā'dhvareṇa yaṣṭuṃ kṛta-sambhāra-vidhiḥ patiḥ prajānām.
children.translated_text: The lord of the people, having completed the preparations, undertook the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice) for worship.
This [poem], wondrous in revealing the path to liberation, born from the resolve of those who debate and speak,

children.text: janayati vijayaṃ sadā janānāṃ yudhi susamāhitamaiśvaraṃ yathā 'stram.
children.translated_text: Always generates victory for people, like the divine weapon well-concentrated in battle.
This composition is like a lamp for those whose eyes are the characteristics of words;
Without grammar, it would be like a hand-mirror for the blind.
This poem, accessible through commentary, is a pure festival for the wise;
And the wicked <s>Durmeghas</s> have been slain herein by me through delight in the learned.
This poem was composed by me at <s>Valabhī</s>, governed by the king <s>Śrīdharasena</s>;

children.text: kīrtirato bhavatān nṛpasya, tasya prema-karaḥ kṣiti-po yataḥ prajānām.
children.translated_text: He whose delight is fame — that king is the joy-maker of his subjects.
